A bead that names a future ADR number is claiming an identifier with no reservation behind it — nothing stops another branch taking it in the interim, and nothing detects it until someone reads both. That is exactly what happened here.

title: TLS cert SANs omit the routable address phux pair advertises
description:
`phux pair` prints a connect link naming a routable overlay address (`phux://connect?url=wss://100.79.155.27:8787&fp=...`), but `ensure_self_signed` in crates/phux-server/src/transport/tls.rs mints the certificate with SANs `DNS:localhost, IP:127.0.0.1, IP:::1` only. Verified against a live server:

    openssl s_client -connect 100.79.155.27:8787 -verify_ip 100.79.155.27
    verify error:num=64:IP address mismatch

So the server hands out an address its own certificate does not claim. Any client that adds the phux certificate to its trust store and then validates the server name (curl --cacert, a browser with the cert trusted, openssl s_client -verify_ip) fails the handshake on a name mismatch it cannot work around.

NOT affected: phux's own dialer (phux-dial CertTrust is SkipVerify or Pinned; PinnedFingerprint::verify_server_cert ignores _server_name) and phux-mobile (its PinnedCert verifier likewise ignores the name). Fingerprint pinning is unaffected by SANs.

Fix: mint the certificate with the addresses phux actually advertises. Hard constraint: an existing complete cert/key pair must never be regenerated, because that rotates the fingerprint pinned on every paired device.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/tls-cert-routable-sans (955ccaaa/amended): SANs now cover the listener bind address and the pair link host + detected overlay addresses; existing certs are never widened (ADR-0091), coverage is reported by phux pair, the listener log, and phux doctor's remote-cert check.

title: [bug] beads DB is at schema v65, ahead of the supported bd 1.2.2 binary (v53)
description:
Hit 2026-08-15 at the end of the phux-k0cw session. Not caused by any phux code; it is a beads-tooling state.

SYMPTOM. Every bd command fails with:
  schema version mismatch: database is at v65, binary knows up to v53 (12 migrations ahead)

bd's own message says the database was migrated by the accidental, untested v1.2.0/v1.2.1 release, and that 1.2.2 (the installed Homebrew build) is the supported one — do NOT reinstall 1.2.1 to make the error go away.

WHEN IT APPEARED. Mid-session. Every bd read and write worked normally — bd prime at session start, and all the phux-k0cw creates/updates/closes — until a 'bd sync', after which reads began failing. The inference is that sync pulled a working set that a v1.2.x binary elsewhere (another machine or another clone) had already migrated forward, and the local binary cannot read that cursor.

DATA IS INTACT. Verified after the fact with --ignore-schema-skew: every bead written this session is present and correct (phux-k0cw and children, phux-jx39, phux-q7ks, phux-at0r closed, the retitled phux-w7z2.20, all labels and the gh-478 external ref). Nothing was lost and the sync push completed; refs/dolt/data on origin is at 091fc7bf.

WORKAROUND, per bd's own message (it states this is verified safe for this schema range; audit-event versioning is paused until recovery):
  BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1 bd <command>
  bd --ignore-schema-skew <command>

FIX. Follow the official recovery, which rolls the schema cursor back to v53 in about two minutes:
  https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/v1.2.2/docs/RECOVERY-1.2.1.md

WHY P1. Every agent session in this repo opens with a bd prime hook. While this is unrecovered, each one starts against a tracker whose plain commands error out, and the natural 'fix' an agent or a human reaches for — reinstalling the version that appears to work — is the one thing the tool explicitly warns against, and would migrate the database further forward.
acceptance_criteria: The recovery guide has been run, bd commands succeed with no BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW and no skew warning, and any other clone that syncs this repo is checked for the same forward cursor.
notes:
LOCAL RECOVERY DONE 2026-08-16 (this machine, /Users/phall/workspace/phux).

Diagnosis refinement: bd runs in EMBEDDED mode on .beads/embeddeddolt/phux. A stray 'dolt sql-server -H 127.0.0.1 -P 53736' (pid 39297) holds .beads/dolt — a DIFFERENT, leftover server-mode directory that bd is not using. It did not need stopping for the recovery and was left running.

Steps run, per the v1.2.2 recovery guide:
1. Verified binary is bd 1.2.2 (Homebrew) and dolt 2.3.0 present.
2. Backup taken OUTSIDE the repo at /Users/phall/workspace/phux-beads-backup-pre-recovery (498M). Deliberately not .beads.backup-pre-recovery: .beads/.gitignore ignores embeddeddolt/ but a repo-root sibling would show up untracked in every worktree's git status.
3. Cursor was confirmed at 63 rows, max version 65.
4. dolt sql -q "DELETE FROM schema_migrations WHERE version > 53; CALL DOLT_ADD(...); CALL DOLT_COMMIT(...)" in .beads/embeddeddolt/phux. Dolt commit lb4rft1cauebli3n2ql8lpvpl7mcv8r8.
5. Verified: bd stats and bd ready run with NO BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW and no skew warning. 955 issues, 882 closed, counts unchanged from pre-recovery.

STILL OPEN, and why this bead is not closed:
(a) The recovered cursor has NOT been pushed. The guide is explicit that the migrated cursor replicates, so until this is pushed, any clone that pulls can carry v65 back and regress the fix. Held because CLAUDE.md sets a conservative profile: no dolt remote sync without explicit authority. Command when authorized: bd dolt push
(b) No other clone has been checked for the forward cursor, which the acceptance criteria requires.
(c) Optional and skipped on purpose: the guide's audit-event re-track (DELETE FROM dolt_ignore WHERE pattern='events'; DOLT_ADD -f events). It changes what syncs, so it should be a decision, not a side effect. Until it runs, the 1.1 line writes audit events unversioned and unsynced; everything else syncs normally.
close_reason:
Recovered and pushed 2026-08-16. Cursor rolled back to v53 on this machine (dolt commit lb4rft1cauebli3n2ql8lpvpl7mcv8r8), verified by bd stats/ready running with no BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW and no warning, 955 issues intact. Pushed with bd dolt push: refs/dolt/data 091fc7bf -> 5ebffe36, so the v53 cursor is now the one any clone pulls.

Residual, deliberately not held open for: the acceptance line 'any other clone that syncs this repo is checked' cannot be verified from here. Pulling clones now get v53; the only remaining regression path is a clone that still holds v65 locally AND pushes. If that happens the symptom is identical and this recovery re-runs the same way. Full step-by-step is in the notes.

Also not done, on purpose: the guide's optional audit-event re-track. It changes what syncs, so it stays a deliberate decision. Until then the 1.1 line writes audit events unversioned and unsynced; everything else syncs normally.

title: [bug] main is red: wrapper_never_relaunches_claude_after_a_mid_session_crash fails at 41c032ca
description:
Discovered 2026-08-15 while validating the phux-k0cw sidebar chain.

crates/phux/src/commands/agent/shim.rs:1034 fails on a CLEAN checkout of main at 41c032ca — verified in a throwaway worktree with no local changes, so it is not caused by the sidebar work.

FAILING ASSERTION (scenario B, the phux-t2g bug):
  assert!(output.contains('phux session ended abnormally'))
after run_on_pty(&wrapper, [('FAKE_CLAUDE_EXIT', '17')]).

The status assertion above it (status == 17) passes, so the exit code propagates correctly; it is the operator-facing message that is missing from the PTY output. Either the wrapper stopped printing it, or the PTY capture is racing the message (the test drives a real PTY, which puts it in scope for the phux-5wxp load-dependent flake family — but it reproduced on the first run at base, which is not flake-shaped).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE TEST: 'just ci-full green before pushing' is the ONLY gate protecting main (CONTRIBUTING.md 'How work reaches main' — a maintainer push has no PR CI). A test that is already red on main silently converts that gate into 'green except the one that was already failing', which is how a second failure gets waved through.

REPRO:
  git worktree add --detach /tmp/check 41c032ca
  cd /tmp/check
  cargo nextest run -E 'test(wrapper_never_relaunches_claude_after_a_mid_session_crash)'
acceptance_criteria: Either the wrapper emits 'phux session ended abnormally' on a mid-session crash again and the test passes on main, or the assertion is corrected to match intended behaviour with the change explained. main runs 'cargo nextest run --workspace' clean.
notes:
NARROWING 2026-08-15, from the feat/fleet-inbox-sidebar branch (this bug is NOT caused by that branch — confirmed against a clean 41c032ca worktree).

Ruled OUT: the launch-sentinel primitive itself. `marker=$(mktemp); sh -c 'printf started > "$1"' _ "$marker"; [ -s "$marker" ]` is TRUE on this machine, so neither mktemp nor the stamp nor the -s test is the failure. The outer wrapper's argument math is also correct: the fake phux does 'shift 4' over 'new -c <cwd> --', leaving '<shim> --phux-inner <marker> ...' for exec, so the inner shim IS reached with the sentinel as $1.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS, unverified — the test's fake phux is too thin. crates/phux/src/commands/agent/shim.rs:1003-1006 models ONLY 'phux new':

  #!/bin/sh
  set -u
  if [ "${FAKE_PHUX_LAUNCH_FAIL:-0}" = "1" ]; then exit 3; fi
  shift 4
  exec "$@"

But the inner branch also calls set_state (shim.rs:449 'set_state start', and a 'set_state clear' EXIT trap), which invokes the same fake binary as 'phux agent set ...'. That input hits the same 'shift 4; exec "$@"' path, so the fixture execs whatever four-args-in is left of an 'agent set' command line — an arbitrary side effect in the middle of the scenario, and a plausible route to the sentinel or the wrapper's state being disturbed before the assertion reads it.

NEXT STEP: make the fake phux dispatch on $1 — model 'new' as today, and make 'agent' a no-op exit 0 — then re-run. If the test goes green, the bug was fixture fidelity rather than wrapper behaviour, and the fix is the fixture plus a comment saying why the fake must dispatch. If it stays red, the wrapper's started-detection is genuinely broken and the next thing to instrument is whether the EXIT trap's set_state runs before the outer wrapper reads the sentinel.

Priority unchanged at P1: while this is red, 'just ci-full green before pushing' — the only gate protecting main — cannot be satisfied by anyone.
close_reason: Fixed upstream on main by 90613b90 'fix(agent): stop the shim pty test inheriting the phux env it tests' — CommandBuilder inherited PHUX_TERMINAL_ID, so the wrapper took its inner branch, never ran 'phux new', and never stamped the launch sentinel. Verified green after rebasing feat/fleet-inbox-sidebar onto current main: 3818/3818.

title: Converge TUI help and command palette into one fuzzy action finder
description:
Why: phux currently maintains two overlapping discovery overlays. The help modal is a scroll-only keybinding table while the command palette is the fuzzy, executable action catalog with live chords. Users should not have to remember which discovery surface answers which question, and help should support the same type-to-find flow.

What: make show-help and command-palette open the same fuzzy action finder, backed by the canonical action registry and live keybindings/plugin rows. title: Move the focused pane across sessions from one fuzzy TUI picker
description:
Why: cross-session movement already exists in the canonical CLI (phux move-pane) and MCP (phux_move_pane), but a human in the TUI must leave the attach surface, discover selectors, and type a two-target command. That defeats the zero-thought workflow the command palette and all-session pickers are meant to provide.

What: add one palette/context-menu action for moving the focused pane. It opens a fuzzy destination picker spanning panes in every cached session/window, clearly identifies session/window/pane and excludes the source. Choosing a target performs the existing ADR-0056 ownership+layout operation without restarting the process or changing TerminalId. Use the same action dispatch and SelectList primitives as other TUI discovery surfaces; do not fork selector or movement semantics. Preserve existing phux move-pane CLI and phux_move_pane MCP behavior as the headless canonical surfaces.

Acceptance: the action is discoverable by fuzzy search in the command surface and from the pane context menu; one selection moves the focused pane beside an exact local destination in the same or another session; process, scrollback, metadata, agent record, subscriptions, and id survive; source/destination layout failure and rollback are visible rather than silent; source/self/satellite/partial-cache cases are safely refused; tests cover same-session, cross-session, last-pane source reaping, destination-layout failure, and picker filtering; generated action/reference docs and TUI docs are updated; just ci-full passes.
design: Reuse SelectList and run_action. The TUI implementation should factor or reuse the spatial operation below crates/phux/src/commands/spatial.rs rather than shelling out to phux. Default placement should be a documented single choice (likely side-by-side at 0.5); directional variants can be separate palette rows only if that remains one selection.

title: Stage 7: Session-graph poll for roster membership
description:
Stage 7 of 9 in the fleet-inbox sidebar chain (epic phux-k0cw).

COMMIT SUBJECT
  feat(client): poll the server session graph so the roster tracks new and renamed sessions

FILES
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/server_frame.rs

VALIDATION
  cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'binary_id(phux-client) & test(session_graph)' && just ci
design: Closes the one liveness gap named in the verdict, with an existing verb. Today `sessions` (driver.rs:1816) is refreshed ONLY from `outcome.sessions`, which only the `FrameKind::Attached` arm sets (server_frame.rs:831), so the roster is frozen for the life of one attach. Add `async fn refresh_session_graph(conn, next_request_id, pending: &mut HashSet<u32>)` sending `FrameKind::Command { request_id, command: Command::GetState { scope: StateScope::Server } }`, and intercept `FrameKind::CommandResult { request_id, result: CommandResult::OkWith(CommandValue::State(snapshot)) }` in the batch loop alongside the existing MetadataValue intercepts (:2560-2632) — `handle_server_frame` has no CommandResult arm at all today, so the reply would otherwise fall through and be dropped. Fold the snapshot into `sessions` / `focused_session` and re-run `sync_foreign_layout_subscriptions`. Trigger it (a) after the ATTACHED fold, (b) edge-triggered when Stage 3's `foreign_pane_set_dirty` fires or an event names a TerminalId absent from both `panes` and the known foreign leaf set, and (c) on a slow floor timer (a `SESSION_GRAPH_POLL: Duration = 10s` arm in the existing `select!`) — a rename emits nothing at all, so poll is the only answer. Note in the fn doc that `build_session_snapshot` synthesizes window names as `window-{index}` and ships `layout: None` (phux-server/src/state/snapshot.rs:78-82), so GET_STATE is the roster's SPINE (membership + pane inventory, which is all zone 3 needs) and the peer's `phux.tui.layout/v1/<session>` key is an optional enrichment for real window names — the inverse of today's foreign_layouts-first ordering. Keep the poll edge-triggered with a slow floor: `handle_get_state_federated` (phux-server/src/runtime/commands.rs:2328) fans out to every dialed satellite, so a per-second poll from an attached TUI becomes per-second satellite fan-out. Tests: `a_session_created_after_attach_reaches_the_roster`, `the_graph_poll_is_edge_triggered_not_per_frame`.
notes:
UNCLAIMED and re-sequenced 2026-08-15, after stages 1-6 landed.

Deferred behind stages 8 and 9 deliberately, not forgotten. Rationale: this is the only stage in the chain that is pure refinement — the roster is live for every session that exists at attach, and this stage extends that to sessions CREATED or RENAMED mid-attach. Stages 8 (on by default) and 9 (docs + ADR) are what make the feature reach a user at all, so they go first.

Scope discovered while sequencing: the attach loop has NO GET_STATE handling today (grep for GetState/StateScope in driver.rs and server_frame.rs returns nothing). So this is not a small addition to an existing path — it needs the command send, a correlated reply intercept, SessionSnapshot decode, and a re-run of the peer sweep against the fresh graph. Price it as such.

Coverage this stage buys, from the recon:
- Session CREATE surfaces only indirectly today (create_named_session broadcasts nothing, so a headlessly-created session appears only when its seed pane first emits Dirty).
- Session RENAME surfaces to nobody: crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs returns BEFORE metadata_set, so no subscriber is notified.
- Session DEATH is already covered — PaneClosed reaches every server-scope subscriber.
COORDINATION 2026-08-16 (autonomous run): phux-q7ks (server-side METADATA_CHANGED on rename) is in flight on branch w1/rename-notify. When it lands, this stage's poll narrows per the bead's own note: rename gets covered by broadcast; the poll's remaining job is CREATE coverage + membership floor. Keep the edge-trigger + slow-floor design; the 10s floor may be relaxable.
UPDATE 2026-08-16: phux-q7ks is implemented (w1/rename-notify, commit 21db19c4, awaiting merge): renames now reach subscribers of (Global, phux.session.name/v1) push-style with a current\0new payload the roster can apply directly. This stage's poll shrinks to CREATE-only coverage + safety floor. If phux-8uly (seed-pane PaneSpawned) also lands, the poll becomes a pure lossy-notification safety floor and its interval can be long.
DEMOTED 2026-08-17 — this stage is now a PURE SAFETY FLOOR, not a liveness mechanism. Its design premise ('a rename emits nothing at all, so poll is the only answer') is false twice over: rename pushes METADATA_CHANGED (phux-q7ks, landed), and create pushes PaneSpawned (phux-8uly, branch w4/seed-pane-spawned commit 279ab12e). Death was already covered by PaneClosed. So all three legs of session lifecycle now PUSH. Better still, this stage's trigger (b) is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED: crates/phux-client/src/attach/server_frame/handler.rs:1116 sets foreign_pane_set_dirty on a PaneSpawned for a Terminal outside the client's pane set — the client hook exists and now actually fires for newly created sessions. REMAINING JUSTIFICATION for any poll at all: fanout is best-effort (broadcast_event uses try_send and DROPS on a full mailbox), so a slow floor guards against a lost notification, not against a silent transition. The 10s floor can therefore be relaxed considerably, and the GET_STATE enumerate half is only needed on attach. RESCOPE THIS BEAD ACCORDINGLY BEFORE IMPLEMENTING — it is materially smaller than when it was written.

title: %name selectors resolve to nothing, but two consumer docs and ADR-0071 point 6 describe them as live surface
description:
VERIFIED IN THE TREE at origin/main 3c7a838a. Found by the phux-w7z2.1 ratification brief; I re-verified every claim below independently before filing.

crates/phux-client/src/selector.rs:320 --

    // Singular selector, set-valued seam: see this function's docs. Never
    // let `%name` reach `pick_target_pane`.
    Selector::Agent(_) => Vec::new(),

That arm is DELIBERATE and correct in isolation: %name is singular and must not flow through the set-valued path, because a partial AgentIndex would turn a real ambiguity into a confident single match. The intended path is resolve_agent (read-only verbs) / resolve_agent_for_input (send-keys, paste, signal, run), both of which are written, documented and unit-tested, and both of which correctly refuse a partial index.

THE DEFECT: nothing calls them. 'grep -rn resolve_agent crates' outside their own module returns exactly three hits and ALL THREE ARE COMMENTS --

  crates/phux/src/commands/mod.rs:2441   (a comment saying it resolves through resolve_agent)
  crates/phux/src/selector.rs:17         (a doc comment)
  crates/phux/src/selector.rs:18         (a doc comment)

So every %name on every verb falls to the Vec::new() arm and is reported as an ordinary selector miss. The machinery exists, is tested, and is unreachable.

WHY THIS IS A 1.0 BLOCKER RATHER THAN AN ORDINARY GAP -- three published surfaces already promise it:

  docs/consumers/agents.md:714 -- lists %name in the selector grammar and documents its semantics ('never matches detector-default kind names and refuses ambiguity rather than choosing among duplicate declarations')
  docs/consumers/mcp.md:131 -- lists %name among the TARGET forms
  ADR-0071 point 6 -- freezes '%name selectors over explicit names only' as part of the agent surface the 1.0 release commits to

Freezing a surface that returns nothing is the worst of both: consumers script against a documented form, get a miss, and the contract says the behaviour is now stable.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF A KNOWN CLASS in this repo -- an ADR documents a mechanism that was never wired up. phux-0d92 (ADR-0081 claimed pairing needed no restart; the credential set was frozen at startup) and phux-pimp (ADR-0080 claimed a deliberate stop stays stopped; there was no stop verb) were the same shape and both shipped as P0/P1 bugs. The difference here is that this one is inside the 1.0 freeze list.

RESOLUTION -- exactly one of:
  (a) land phux-w7z2.3 (Implement ADR-0075: %name agent addressing in the selector grammar) before the freeze, wiring the verbs to resolve_agent / resolve_agent_for_input; or
  (b) remove %name from docs/consumers/agents.md, docs/consumers/mcp.md and ADR-0071 point 6 until it works.

Do NOT freeze it as-is. Note phux-w7z2.3 is currently blocked on phux-w7z2.1 (ratification), so if ratification slips, (b) is the honest fallback and must not be forgotten.

RELATED, from the same brief and not yet independently verified by me: fetch_agent_index returns a bare HashMap with no complete/partial bit, so ADR-0075 point 3's exit-3 refusal has no source of truth; and the shipped Claude shim writes --name claude --kind claude, which would make ZERO panes %-addressable out of the box even once (a) lands, because %name deliberately never matches detector-default kind names.
notes: Taking the bead-approved honest fallback while ADR-0075 remains Proposed: remove %name from shipped working-surface promises and mark it reserved/fail-closed; keep parser/resolver machinery dormant for later ratification.
close_reason: Removed %name from active CLI/MCP/root-help/skill/1.0 promises; documented it as parser-reserved and fail-closed until proposed ADR-0075 is accepted; kept dormant resolver machinery.

title: Accept or reject ADR-0071: 1.0 cannot be cut against a Proposed commitment
description:
ADR-0071 'What phux 1.0 commits to' has been Status: Proposed since 2026-08-07. It is the only written definition of what a phux 1.0 means, and every other 1.0 gate in the tracker derives from it — yet nothing tracks ratifying it, so the release definition has no owner and no close condition.

Backwards derivation from the ADR's own text shows most of its hard preconditions are ALREADY MET:

- Point 3, one-command update path: shipped (phux update, phux-1c51 closed).
- Point 3, unbypassable HELLO version gate: shipped (crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs:1080; phux-0vp and phux-j4on closed).
- Point 4, overdue deprecated-spelling removals: done. crates/phux/src/deprecations.rs DEPRECATED is empty; the rows went in v0.12.1.
- Point 4, dead pub surface in the publishable phux-protocol crate: done by ADR-0072. policy.rs is down to PeerIdentity, TransportType and Capability, all three live.
- Point 7(b), phux_agent multiplexer frozen as ten distinct MCP tools: done. crates/phux-mcp/src/agent_tools.rs, with a test asserting bare phux_agent is now an unknown tool.
- Point 7(a), every stable error code in commands::json_err::codes: met in practice — 81 codes, and no call site outside json_err.rs invents a literal.

What is NOT met is the decision layer, and it is the whole remaining blocker:

- This ADR itself is Proposed.
- ADR-0075, ADR-0076 and ADR-0078 are Proposed (0077 is Accepted), so point 6's enumerated freeze cannot close and point 7(c) has nothing to amend into.

ACCEPTANCE: ADR-0071 reaches a terminal Status. If Accepted, point 6 is amended to whatever ADR-0075/0076/0078 ratification yields (see phux-w7z2.1, phux-w7z2.2), and the six already-met preconditions above are recorded as met in the ADR rather than left to be re-derived.
notes:
SEQUENCING NOTE 2026-08-15 (priority unchanged at P1).

Step 5 of the five-step fleet-inbox arc, and the adoption gate. Third parties cannot build against phux while nothing here is safe to build against; the competitor is iterating in the open at v0.8.0 with a plugin marketplace. Being first to a FROZEN, spec'd agent surface makes the durable moat the ecosystem rather than the feature set, because features get copied in a weekend and an integrated contract does not.

HARD DEPENDENCY, added today: do not cut the freeze while phux-w7z2.20 still claims a fleet-wide agent-state stream needs a wire change. That claim is contested (see that bead's notes) and the freeze must not be taken against a phantom wire requirement.

title: Flaky: phux-server::eof_detach pty_eof_drives_terminal_closed_to_attached_client
description:
Observed failing twice on 2026-08-11 against main (7d262545) with only an unrelated CLI signal-handling change in the tree:

1. During a full 'just ci' run: FAIL [0.364s] (3467/3623), which aborted the run and left 156 tests unrun.
2. Once in a loop of 5 isolated 'cargo nextest run -p phux-server --test eof_detach' invocations -- so it is NOT caused by cross-test contention with other binaries; it fails alone.

It then passed 8+ consecutive isolated runs, including with --no-capture and -j 8, so the reproduction rate is low and load-dependent. The failure output was not captured before the run was overwritten -- CAPTURING THE ACTUAL ASSERTION IS THE FIRST TASK HERE.

REPRO RECIPE that found it: run the single test in a loop and watch for a non-zero summary. Expect roughly 1 in 5 under load, far less when the machine is idle.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE TEST: nextest aborts the run on first failure by default, so this flake does not just cost its own test -- the 'just ci' occurrence left 156 tests unrun. A flake in this position converts into 'CI is red for no reason', which is how a suite stops being trusted.

LIKELY SHAPE, to check first: the test drives PTY EOF to a TERMINAL_CLOSED frame reaching an attached client. That is a race between the PTY read side seeing EOF, the actor publishing the close, and the client's frame read. A missing wait-for-condition (sleeping or assuming ordering instead of polling for the frame) is the usual cause in this repo -- compare how the passing tests in this area wait.

RELATED: phux-w7z2.56 (Deliver TERMINAL_CLOSED to ATTACH_TERMINAL-only subscribers) touches the same delivery path; worth reading together, and worth checking whether that bug and this flake share a cause.
notes:
SECOND FLAKY TEST, same subsystem, found 2026-08-11 while landing phux-67wg:

phux-server::server_self_exit server_self_exits_after_serving_a_client -- failed once during 'just ci' (aborting the run and leaving 37 tests unrun), and reproduced at 1-in-6 in an isolated loop of 'cargo nextest run -p phux-server --test server_self_exit'. Neither branch that hit it touches phux-server.

So this bead should be widened: there are at least TWO independently flaky tests in the server-lifecycle area (eof_detach's TERMINAL_CLOSED delivery, and self-exit-after-serving-a-client), both timing-shaped, both aborting whole CI runs because nextest stops on first failure.

Both sit on the same seam -- 'a lifecycle transition reaches an observer' -- which is worth investigating as ONE cause rather than two. Candidates: the last-pane self-exit is armed on attach (state/client.rs:193-194) and fires from the EOF watcher (runtime/client.rs:555-573) guarded on has_served_client and !root_token.is_cancelled(); a test that races the arming against the PTY EOF would see exactly this intermittency.

SUGGESTED SCOPE: capture both failures' actual assertions first, then decide whether it is one fix or two. Do not paper over either with a sleep -- poll for the condition, which is what the passing tests in this area already do.
close_reason: Closed

title: release-please re-proposes already-shipped releases: last-release-sha is pinned to v0.1.0
description:
PR #419 'chore(main): release 0.15.0' proposes a changelog that RE-LISTS features already shipped and already present in CHANGELOG.md.

PROOF: PR #419's body lists 'feat(agent): add acknowledged orchestration surface (#410) (8d06829)'. That exact line is already in the shipped CHANGELOG.md on main at line 24, under 0.14.0. It also declares BREAKING CHANGES -- session-name-template defaulting to the launch directory, the which-key delay 600ms->400ms, the theme palette change, and the removal of deprecated CLI spellings -- all of which shipped in earlier releases.

ROOT CAUSE (prime suspect, verify before fixing): release-please-config.json pins

  "last-release-sha": "040fea1a67a54d67a6afbcb71c8bef62802fdc8b"

040fea1a is 'release: v0.1.0'. It is 242 commits behind v0.14.1 and an ancestor of every tag since. With that pin, release-please scans the entire history from v0.1.0 rather than from the latest tag, so every release PR re-accumulates the whole backlog.

WHY IT SURFACED NOW: #417 ('create the tag a draft release does not') fixed tag creation for draft releases. Tags are now reliable -- v0.14.0 and v0.14.1 both exist and point at the right commits -- which changed what release-please computes and made the discrepancy visible. This is not a regression from #417; #417 exposed it.

IMPACT IF MERGED AS-IS:
- CHANGELOG.md gains a 0.15.0 section duplicating most of 0.9.0 through 0.14.1.
- The version bumps to 0.15.0 on the strength of breaking changes that shipped months of commits ago, so the number stops meaning anything.
- It recurs on every subsequent release.

FIX: remove or correct last-release-sha now that tags are trustworthy, then regenerate the release PR and verify the proposed changelog contains ONLY commits since v0.14.1 (which should be nearly empty). Add a guard so a release PR whose changelog re-lists an already-released commit sha fails CI rather than waiting for a human to notice.

DO NOT MERGE PR #419 until this is resolved.
close_reason: Closed

title: [epic] Server lifecycle: you can start a phux server four ways and stop it zero
description:
phux has four start paths -- auto-spawn (ensure_server, four call sites), explicit 'phux server', service supervision, and graceful-upgrade re-exec -- and no first-class stop. That asymmetry is the root of a cluster of otherwise-unrelated-looking bugs, and three separate places in the tree already document the missing verb as though it shipped.

THE ANCHOR FACTS, all confirmed against the code:

1. 'phux kill --server' does not exist. It is cited as working in ADR-0080's Decision, in docs/operations.md:288 (user-facing), and in a LIVE TEST ASSERTION MESSAGE at crates/phux/src/commands/service.rs:1071. ADR-0080 corrected the restart policy from KeepAlive:true to SuccessfulExit:false precisely so a deliberate stop would stay stopped, and listed 'a deliberately stopped server stays stopped' as a Consequence. That consequence is currently unreachable.

2. THE SERVER HAS NO SIGTERM HANDLER. The whole shutdown future is tokio::signal::ctrl_c() -- SIGINT only. So SIGTERM skips unlink_socket_if_ours (socket left stale) and TerminalActor::shutdown_pty (no SIGHUP-grace-reap for pane children). It also exits non-zero-equivalent, which launchd's SuccessfulExit:false treats as failure and RESTARTS after 30s. A signal-based stop would therefore contradict the very doc line it is meant to satisfy, on macOS.

3. The absence has already cost real bugs: an infinite supervised restart loop (phux-67wg), leaked test daemons (phux-whhd), and a diagnostic that recommends a pane-destroying fix (phux-nvi2).

SEQUENCING. phux-1wka (SIGTERM handler) is the cheap correctness floor and unblocks the fallback path. phux-pimp (SHUTDOWN wire command + the verb) is the real fix and is what makes the three doc sites true. phux-67wg (refuse to install over a live server) removes the worst user-facing damage cheaply and should not wait for phux-m3ot, which is a multi-week design item needing an ADR and net-new mechanism (no SCM_RIGHTS exists anywhere in the tree).

Scoped from a three-way code audit on 2026-08-11.
close_reason: All 13 children closed (SIGTERM handler, SHUTDOWN wire command + phux kill --server, service adopt/reconcile, doctor fixes, test guards). The epic's anchor gaps are all resolved; verified 13/13 complete.

title: Add a SHUTDOWN wire command and phux kill --server, the verb three docs already promise
description:
ADR-0080's Decision says: 'A clean exit -- phux kill --server -- now stays exited. Previously a server could not be stopped.' docs/operations.md:288 repeats it user-facing. crates/phux/src/commands/service.rs:1071 is a TEST ASSERTION MESSAGE citing it. The verb has never existed. This is the same shape as phux-0d92: the door was corrected, the handle was never fitted.

phux kill takes only a positional selector (crates/phux/src/commands/mod.rs:602-605; kill.rs:22 parses a selector and never considers the daemon). There is no shutdown/terminate verb in the wire Command enum -- tags stop at 0x15 (phux-protocol/src/wire/frame.rs:630); UPGRADE (0x0e) is the only self-affecting one. Next free tag is 0x16.

WHY A WIRE COMMAND, NOT A SIGNAL. This is the load-bearing design point. A signal-killed server exits non-zero-equivalent, and launchd's KeepAlive{SuccessfulExit:false} (service.rs:250-255) RESTARTS it after ThrottleInterval 30. So a signal-based 'kill --server' would contradict docs/operations.md:288 on macOS -- the exact doc line it is meant to satisfy. Only a clean exit-0 teardown keeps a supervised server stopped. systemd's Restart=on-failure excludes SIGTERM and would not restart, so the platforms diverge; the wire command makes them agree.

SHAPE: mirror UPGRADE. New command tag whose handler acks and then cancels the root token, routing through drop(local) -> drop(input_lane) -> unlink_socket_if_ours (runtime/mod.rs:1050-1062) and giving every pane TerminalActor::shutdown_pty's SIGHUP-grace-reap (terminal_actor/mod.rs:2789-2839).

INGREDIENTS THAT ALREADY EXIST: the server pid via Connection::peer_pid() (SO_PEERCRED/LOCAL_PEEREPID, phux-client/src/attach/connection.rs:104-107,261-267), surfaced by phux status (status.rs:102). It is an OS fact captured at connect time -- cannot be spoofed, cannot be stale -- but it is Option<i32> and is None on QUIC/WS. Graceful teardown, socket classifier, and reap all exist.

THE IMPLEMENTATION MUST:
1. probe(path): Absent/Stale -> nothing to kill, reap and exit 0 IDEMPOTENTLY. Live -> connect.
2. Send the wire shutdown; fall back to SIGTERM only if the server will not service frames (requires phux-1wka).
3. WAIT FOR ACTUAL EXIT, not for the ack: poll socket::probe(path) != Live, the pattern already used at server.rs:576-582 after an upgrade. Escalate SIGTERM -> SIGKILL after a bounded grace. Do NOT poll 'kill -0 pid' alone -- pid reuse is exactly why ADR-0080:160-164 rejected a pidfile.
4. Reap the socket after an ungraceful kill via socket::reap_stale (socket.rs:121), which re-probes and refuses to unlink anything live.
5. Refuse clearly on 'not my server': a socket owned by another uid gives EPERM on connect, which probe DELIBERATELY classifies as Live (socket.rs:80-83), and peer_cred is unreachable so pid is None. This must be a refusal, not a 'stale, reaping' path.
6. Handle the wedged server: a server blocked in a synchronous stall on its current-thread runtime (ADR-0080:53-56 flags this as real) will not service a wire shutdown, so the escalation ladder is mandatory.

UX NOTE -- AUTO-SPAWN RESURRECTION: four verbs call ensure_server (attach.rs:103 and :733, new.rs:122 and :188, worktree.rs:481). Any of them run right after a successful kill silently starts a new server. The verb means 'stop THIS generation' and the output should say so.

DEPENDS ON phux-1wka for the fallback path. Requires regenerating docs/reference/ (generated tree with a freshness test, ADR-0069).
notes:
DESIGN CONSTRAINT found 2026-08-11, read before implementing:

SHUTDOWN cannot just be a new command tag. proto.md s6.3 (ADR-0061) is NORMATIVE that new frames / command tags / error codes MUST ship as a negotiated capability -- a ServerFeature bit, a ClientCapabilities byte, or an additive field id -- whenever an additive shape exists. A minor bump is a FLEET-WIDE BREAK with no grace window (major.minor equality is a hard admission test at HELLO), and is reserved for changes no additive shape can express: renumbering a tag, redefining bytes already on the wire, reallocating a freed tag, or removing a depended-on message.

So the shape is:
- New command tag 0x16 (next free; 0x0a and 0x0b are freed-and-RESERVED and must NOT be reallocated without a minor bump).
- A new ServerFeature bit gating it. A client MUST NOT send SHUTDOWN unless the bit is advertised; an older server drops the unknown discriminant silently.
- PROTOCOL_VERSION STAYS 0.7.0. New docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md entry as 0.7.0-draft.6.

THE PRECEDENT TO COPY IS MOVE_TERMINAL (docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md, 0.6.0-draft.5): new C->S and S->C frames behind ServerFeature MOVE_TERMINAL = 0x00000040, discriminants allocated past the existing spec reservations, 'additive: no tag renumbered, no existing bytes changed; draft bump'. Follow that entry's structure for the changelog prose too.

FILES THIS TOUCHES: phux-protocol (Command enum, tag const, encode/decode, ServerFeature bit), docs/spec/L1.md (command catalog), docs/spec/appendix-reserved.md (tag registry table), docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md, phux-server runtime/commands.rs (handler -> root_token.cancel()), phux/src/commands/{mod.rs,kill.rs} (the --server flag and its ArgGroup), and docs/reference/ MUST be regenerated with 'just docs-gen' (there is a byte-comparing freshness test).

CLAP NOTE: kill's target is a REQUIRED positional with no default, so 'phux kill --server' is currently a usage error before it reaches run_kill. Adding --server needs target to become Option<String> plus an ArgGroup with conflicts_with. Precedent in-tree: New uses ArgGroup{...}.requires(...) at commands/mod.rs:465; Attach uses ArgGroup::new("remote") at :263.
close_reason: Closed

title: The server has no SIGTERM handler, so every non-Ctrl-C stop skips the graceful path
description:
The entire shutdown future for the server process is crates/phux/src/commands/server.rs:336-345:

  server.run_async(async { let _ = tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await; }).await

tokio::signal::ctrl_c() on Unix is SIGINT ONLY. A repo-wide grep for SignalKind/sigaction/signal_hook finds handlers in phux-client (driver.rs:1764-1771, terminal restoration) and phux-crash (handler.rs:299-310), but phux-server registers NONE. The only thing run_server arms is a panic hook.

CONSEQUENCES of 'kill -TERM <server-pid>' today:
- Default disposition, process dies immediately.
- run_async never returns, so drop(local)/drop(input_lane) (runtime/mod.rs:1050-1051) never run.
- unlink_socket_if_ours (runtime/mod.rs:1062) NEVER RUNS. The socket file is left behind, stale.
- TerminalActor::shutdown_pty (terminal_actor/mod.rs:2789) never runs. No SIGHUP-then-grace to pane process groups, no waitpid reap. Pane children get EOF/SIGHUP from the kernel closing the PTY masters, not from phux's graceful terminate_child_group.
- Exit status is 'killed by signal', which launchd's SuccessfulExit:false treats as a FAILURE -> 30s throttle -> restart. systemd's Restart=on-failure excludes SIGTERM, so the two platforms diverge on whether a TERMed server stays dead.

TWO PLACES IN THE TREE ALREADY ASSUME THIS HANDLER EXISTS AND ARE WRONG:
1. crates/phux/tests/stale_socket_recovery.rs:55-58 comments 'SIGTERM, not SIGKILL: the server's shutdown path is what unlinks the socket.' It is not. The test only passes because its socket lives in a TempDir that is removed anyway. This comment is currently the closest thing in-tree to a spec for the behaviour, and it is a false invariant.
2. crates/phux/src/commands/service.rs:375-376, the --restore wrapper's trap: kill -TERM "$server". The 'workspace save' runs first so the archive is fine, but the panes are killed ungracefully and the socket is orphaned.

FIX: fold SignalKind::terminate() into the shutdown future alongside ctrl_c, so SIGTERM cancels the root token -- the same signal Ctrl-C, idle-exit (runtime/mod.rs:301-305), and last-pane self-exit already deliver. That is a small change and every downstream piece already exists.

Correct the two false invariants above in the same change.

BLOCKS the signal fallback path of phux-kill-server. Note that even with this fix, a SIGNAL-based stop still exits non-zero-equivalent under launchd; only a clean exit-0 teardown makes docs/operations.md:288 true. See the SHUTDOWN command bead.
close_reason: Closed

title: doctor tells you to fix a legacy unit with a command that kills every pane
description:
crates/phux/src/commands/doctor.rs:234-242 warns about a legacy supervisor unit and hints:

  'it resurrects servers you stopped and hides crash-loops -- re-run phux service installed.
  unit    /Users/phall/Library/LaunchAgents/com.phux.server.plist
  binary  /opt/homebrew/bin/phux
  listen  local socket only (pass --quic or --listen for remote attach)
  logs    /Users/phall/.local/state/phux/server.log

A LaunchAgent runs while this user has a session. On a headless
host, enable automatic login (System Settings > Users & Groups >
Automatic login) so the server comes back after a reboot without
someone signing in at the console. to replace it, or Removed /Users/phall/Library/LaunchAgents/com.phux.server.plist

Sessions on the running server ended with it. The workspace archive,
token store, and certificate were left in place.'

Following that hint costs the user every running pane, unprompted.

WHY: run_install -> write_unit_files -> reload (service.rs:504-515). For launchd, reload runs 'launchctl bootout gui/$UID/com.phux.server' BEFORE bootstrap (service.rs:578-591). Booting out the job SIGTERMs the running supervised server, and every pane and its in-flight shells, agents, and subagents die with it. systemd's 'systemctl --user enable --now' after daemon-reload has the same effect on a running unit.

So phux's own diagnostic tool recommends a destructive action, in a Warn (exit 0) that reads as routine housekeeping, with no indication that live work is at stake.

MINIMUM FIX (this bead): make the hint honest. State that replacing the unit restarts the server and ends every pane, and say what to do instead if that is not acceptable right now. A user who reads the warning should be able to decide, not discover.

BETTER FIX, if phux-3vg8 (in-place reconcile) lands: point at the non-destructive path instead.

RELATED: phux-bd30 asks for automatic reconcile from 'phux update'. Note that doing that naively inherits this exact defect and makes it silent -- an update would kill panes with no prompt at all. Read this bead before implementing bd30.
notes: CORRECTION: the description references 'phux-3vg8', which was a mistyped id and does not exist. The intended reference is phux-l1yx (Reconcile a legacy supervisor unit in place, without killing panes).
close_reason: Closed

title: phux service install on a host with a running server installs an infinite restart loop
description:
Confirmed from code, deterministic, and it loops FOREVER on both platforms.

TRACE:
1. 'phux service install' writes the unit and hands it to the init system (crates/phux/src/commands/service.rs:504-515). It NEVER checks whether a server is already running -- no probe, no warning.
2. The init system starts '<binary> server'.
3. run_async's non-resume branch calls handle_existing_socket (crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs:965-984), which connect-probes the socket and on success returns ServerError::SocketBusy. bind(2) is never reached -- this is phux's own liveness probe refusing, not EADDRINUSE.
4. run_server maps Err to ExitCode::FAILURE (crates/phux/src/commands/server.rs:352-355).

So: a non-zero exit, every time.

WHY IT NEVER GIVES UP:
- launchd: KeepAlive{SuccessfulExit:false} restarts on any non-zero exit. ThrottleInterval 30 is a MINIMUM SPACING between starts, not a give-up count. launchd has no give-up. One failed start every 30s, forever.
- systemd: Restart=on-failure + RestartSec=30s, and render_systemd_unit (service.rs:285-320) sets NO StartLimitBurst/StartLimitIntervalSec. systemd's defaults (5 starts/10s) can never trip at a 30s cadence, so the rate limiter never fires. One failed start every 30s, forever.
- With --restore the unit runs the wrapper, which ends in 'wait $server' (service.rs:394) and propagates the same non-zero status. Same loop.

MISDIAGNOSIS MAKES IT WORSE: log_startup runs at server.rs:310, BEFORE run_async, so every SocketBusy generation IS recorded to server-starts.log. After 5 starts -- about 2.5 hours -- 'phux doctor' fails server-health with 'crash-looping' and the hint 'something is killing the server on startup'. Nothing is killing it; it is refusing to start. Accurate signal, wrong story.

FIX (this bead): make install refuse up front. Probe the socket the same way handle_existing_socket does, and if a live server answers, refuse to install with a precise recovery message rather than writing a unit that cannot work. That is the cheap, correct guard. Actually moving the live server under supervision is phux-m3ot and is much harder -- see that bead before assuming this one can adopt.

Also worth fixing here: add StartLimitBurst/StartLimitIntervalSec to the systemd unit so a genuinely failing server eventually stops rather than retrying until the heat death of the universe.

NO TEST COVERS THIS. service.rs's test module covers unit RENDERING thoroughly but run_install, write_unit_files, and reload are untested, and there is no test of install-over-a-running-server at all.
close_reason: Closed

title: A per-pane server Error frame kills the whole attached client
description:
When the server sends FrameKind::Error during the attached phase, the client treats it as a fatal protocol violation and tears the whole attach down:

  phux: attach failed: protocol error: frame is not valid from a server in the
  attached phase: Error { code: InternalError, message: "native history request
  failed: ..." }

Observed as the user-visible symptom of phux-rv52 (creating a pane while attached). The root cause there is a native-history binding fault on ONE pane -- but the blast radius is the entire session: every other pane, the layout, and the client all go down with it.

That is the wrong failure shape. A history request is a per-replica, best-effort enrichment; scrollback for one pane failing to load should degrade that pane (and say so in the status bar), not end the attach. The same reasoning applies to any per-terminal Error the server can emit while attached.

WHY SEPARATE FROM phux-rv52: fixing the binding fault removes today's trigger, but leaves the fragility. Any future per-pane server error -- resource exhaustion, a codec fault, a satellite hiccup -- would still take the whole client out. Fixing this makes that class of bug survivable rather than fatal, and is worth doing even after rv52 lands.

SCOPE: crates/phux-client/src/attach/server_frame.rs -- the attached-phase frame validation that classifies Error as a protocol violation. Decide which server error codes are per-terminal (degrade the replica, surface a notice) versus genuinely fatal to the connection (e.g. a HELLO/phase violation). SPEC section 6/7 governs which is which; the answer should be written down, not inferred per call site.

RELATED: phux-rv52 (the current trigger), phux-0d92 (token reload).
close_reason: Closed

title: phux kill --server: no way to stop a running server
description: phux kill takes only a session selector; there is no verb that stops a server, and no shutdown command in the wire protocol. Consequences seen: (1) tests that auto-spawn a server have to hand-roll cleanup, and one silently leaked because 'phux kill --server' looks like it should work and does not (see phux-whhd); (2) 'phux service install' on a host that already has an auto-spawned server produces a supervised server that cannot bind, which with ADR-0080's failure-only restart policy retries every 30s indefinitely. Proposed: 'phux kill --server' resolves the peer pid via SO_PEERCRED (already surfaced by 'phux status --json') and sends SIGTERM. Local/UDS only -- remotely killing a server is a protocol decision, not a papercut fix. No wire change needed. ADR-0081 removed the urgency for pairing (which no longer restarts anything) but the gap is still real.
notes: SUPERSEDED by phux-pimp (Add a SHUTDOWN wire command and phux kill --server), which carries the full implementation plan from a 2026-08-11 code audit. The key correction to this bead's proposal: it suggests resolving the peer pid and sending SIGTERM. That is not sufficient and on macOS is actively wrong -- the server has NO SIGTERM handler (phux-1wka), and a signal death exits non-zero-equivalent, which launchd's SuccessfulExit:false restarts after 30s. So a signal-based 'kill --server' would contradict docs/operations.md:288, the exact line it is meant to satisfy. The correct shape is a wire command that cancels the root token and yields exit 0. See phux-pimp and the parent epic phux-g60k.
close_reason: Closed

title: Existing service units need reinstall for the corrected restart policy
description: ADR-0080 changed the generated unit to KeepAlive{SuccessfulExit:false} + ThrottleInterval 30 (systemd: Restart=on-failure + RestartSec). A unit written by an earlier release keeps the old unthrottled restart-on-any-exit policy until the user re-runs 'phux service install'. 'phux doctor' warns via the server-health check (supervisor_unit_is_legacy), but nothing upgrades it automatically. Consider having 'phux update' reconcile an installed unit.
close_reason: Merged as #433 alongside phux-l1yx. phux update calls service::reconcile_after_update() on Action::Installed -- human output only, since the --json document shape is inside the ADR-0071 freeze. Silent unless it changed something, never fatal. That shape is defensible only because reconcile is non-destructive by construction, which is exactly what this bead gated it on.

title: Deliver TERMINAL_CLOSED to ATTACH_TERMINAL-only subscribers
description: The pane EOF watcher resolves terminal subscribers only through ClientTable::attached. An ATTACH_TERMINAL-only consumer is registered in terminal_table but filtered out, so the hub relay never receives TERMINAL_CLOSED for a satellite pane and can retain dead proxy state. Capture the outbound mailbox at terminal subscribe time (as metadata/event subscriptions do), deliver exactly once, and add a no-session-ATTACH plus federation regression test.
acceptance_criteria: An ATTACH_TERMINAL-only client receives TERMINAL_CLOSED; hub relay cleanup is covered; attached clients still receive exactly one frame.
close_reason: Landed on main. The spec already REQUIRED this: L1.md 3.1 says the server MUST emit TERMINAL_CLOSED to every client subscribed to the Terminal, and 5.1 says ATTACH_TERMINAL registers the caller as an output subscriber with no session ATTACH required. So a conformance defect, not a missing requirement -- but the requirement lived in the intersection of two sentences in different sections, which is how the hole survived, so 3.1 gained a paragraph stating the union explicitly. Cause: the pane-EOF watcher resolved mailboxes via ClientTable::attached, which only session-scoped ATTACH populates, so an ATTACH_TERMINAL-only consumer resolved to no mailbox and was dropped. Content still flowed (the per-pane pump owns its own clone), so the symptom was an agent watching a pane that simply went quiet forever. Fixed by capturing per-Terminal mailboxes, following the existing event_subscriptions/metadata_mailboxes precedent; exactly-once is structural since the fanout resolves one mailbox per deduped ClientId. No wire change, no feature bit. Federation needed no relay change -- hub/relay.rs already handled inbound TerminalClosed and simply never received one.

title: Fix PR 391 dead ADR-0032 links
description: GitHub Actions CI check on PR 391 fails docs-check because ADR-0079 and its README index entry reference the nonexistent ADR/0032-graceful-in-place-upgrade.md instead of ADR/0032-graceful-server-upgrade.md. Correct both references and verify the documentation gate passes.
