title: ADR for phux agent start: what an available shell is, who owns the launch argv, who writes the name
description:
phux-w7z2.6 shipped the verb; the ADR gap it flagged is still open. ADR-0076 covers agent prompt and agent wait only and has no decision point about launching into an existing pane.

The implementation (crates/phux/src/commands/agent/start.rs) embodies these choices and they need ADR text before 1.0 freezes the CLI surface under ADR-0071:

1. agent start is a new verb under the agent noun, NOT a placement flag on launch. It shares resolve_launch + prepare_for_launch and diverges only at delivery: launch hands argv to SPAWN_TERMINAL (no shell, ADR-0042), agent start types a quoted line into a live shell. That inverts ADR-0042's no-shell-evaluation property for half the invocations and is the single biggest semantic break.
2. Ready is the FIRST detector publication after submit, observed as a transition off the unknown the verb binds. Not state == idle: no shipped manifest asserts idle positively.
3. A --kind with no loaded detection manifest is refused (exit 2) before anything is written, because an unmanifested kind is never identified, so readiness is unreachable and the verb could only time out AFTER typing into the pane and binding a name.
4. The bind writes name only, never kind, because compose fills kind only when the stored record has none: a pre-declared wrong kind would survive forever, blessed by the detector.
5. Rollback is asymmetric. Pre-handoff APPLY_INPUT refusals (INPUT_LEASE_HELD, CANONICAL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) unwind the bind by read-compare-delete; INPUT_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN, timeout, and kind mismatch do not, because deleting a name after bytes are on the PTY leaves a running agent with no handle.
6. The integration id and the detection kind are different namespaces. A template's own kind is a category (terminal-agent) and its [agent_identity] kind is not surfaced by the config loader, so there is no client-side map. The verb defaults --integration to the kind slug and takes an override. That default is a convention the ADR should either bless or replace.
7. Normative meaning of an available shell — see the sibling bead for the server surface that would make it answerable.
notes: Writing an ADR against current shipped agent-start behavior. Updating the stale no-positive-idle premise after OSC 9;4: readiness remains the first post-submit detector publication, not a pre-existing state level.
close_reason: Accepted ADR-0084 defining the in-place agent-start contract: verb boundary, shell availability, argv ownership, kind/integration namespaces, name-only bind, transition readiness, and proof-based rollback. Corrected the stale ready-state comment for Claude OSC 9;4. just ci-full passed on origin/main base; integrated and pushed as b6de1741.

title: Three id spaces, two overflow semantics: IdBridge panics where IdSpace saturates
description:
`IdSpace` (crates/phux-server/src/state/id_space.rs) holds three core-to-wire id mappings — sessions, terminals, windows — and two of them behave differently from the third on the same failure.

- Sessions go through the reusable `IdBridge` (crates/phux-server/src/id_bridge.rs). `IdBridge::intern` **panics** on u32 exhaustion — id_bridge.rs:97 is a literal `.expect("IdBridge exhausted u32 wire-id space")`.
- Terminals and windows are the same data structure open-coded directly on `IdSpace`. `intern_terminal` / `intern_window` **saturate** instead.

The module doc (id_space.rs:11-27) already names this: "That asymmetry is deliberate and predates this module... Collapsing them into one generic bridge would change one of those behaviours; it stays out of scope here."

So it is a known deferral, not an oversight. What makes it worth closing now rather than later:

- The divergence is in failure semantics, not policy. Exhausting the session wire-id space aborts the server; exhausting the terminal space silently reuses the ceiling id. One of those is wrong, and nothing in the codebase argues which.
- ADR-0071 freezes the 1.0 surface. A panic-versus-saturate split on identity allocation is the kind of thing that gets much more expensive to change once it is load-bearing behaviour someone depends on.

The second stated reason for the asymmetry — that `phux_protocol::ids::TerminalId` is an enum rather than a newtype, so only `Local` is ever minted and `terminal_from_wire` returns `None` for a `Satellite` by design — is real and should survive any unification. It argues for a generic bridge parameterized on the mint/lookup shape, not for three hand-rolled copies.
acceptance_criteria: One decision recorded and applied uniformly across sessions, terminals, and windows: either all three saturate or all three fail loudly, with a test pinning the chosen behaviour at the u32 boundary for each space. The Satellite-never-interned property of TerminalId is preserved explicitly, not by accident of open-coding.
close_reason: Integrated on untangle/architecture-knots; full just ci passes.

title: Split tree is encoded three ways with no cross-representation conformance test
description:
The binary split tree (ADR-0012) exists in three independent encodings that must agree, plus a fourth client-local state model:

1. `phux_core::window::{LayoutNode, SplitDir}` — crates/phux-core/src/window.rs:57,75
2. `phux_protocol::wire::info::{LayoutNode, SplitDir}` — crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/info.rs:65,48
3. `phux_server::upgrade::blob::{LayoutBlob, SplitDirBlob}` — crates/phux-server/src/upgrade/blob.rs:213,233
4. `phux_client_core::layout::{LayoutState, WindowState, Workspace}` plus its own CBOR codec

(1) versus (2) is justified by ADR-0011 (protocol/core independence) and documented at info.rs:5-8. (3) exists because the upgrade blob needs serde and wire ids (ADR-0032). (4) is justified by ADR-0017/0019 as TUI-private. Each rationale is individually sound.

The knot is the missing guard. Contrast with the cell projection, which is ALSO knowingly triplicated (phux-client/src/attach/render.rs, phux-server/src/grid/synthesizer.rs, phux-record/src/replay.rs) and is explicitly reasoned about at replay.rs:20-44 AND pinned by crates/phux/tests/cell_projection_conformance.rs, which feeds one corpus through all three and compares cell-for-cell.

The layout tree has no equivalent. Each encoding has its own round-trip test; nothing asserts that core, wire, and blob describe the same tree. A split-ratio or axis-convention drift in one encoding is caught only if a human notices.
acceptance_criteria: A layout conformance test in crates/phux (the only member depending on all three) builds a corpus of split trees: nested splits on both axes, boundary ratios, single leaf, deep asymmetric nesting. It asserts core, wire, and blob encodings round-trip identically, mirroring cell_projection_conformance.rs in shape and intent.
close_reason: Integrated on untangle/architecture-knots; full just ci passes.

title: [epic] Untangle the architecture: unguarded duplication, id-space drift, and god modules
description:
Graph-derived architectural knot inventory from a full graphify pass over the repo (17,039 nodes / 45,659 edges, AST over 676 code files + semantic over 226 docs).

Scope: the duplications and tangles that are NOT already reasoned about and guarded. This repo documents most of its deliberate duplication well (see phux-record/src/replay.rs and the cell_projection_conformance.rs guard) - those are explicitly out of scope. What follows are the ones with no guard, divergent semantics, or no stated rationale.

Ground truth notes for anyone picking this up:
- The Cargo crate DAG is clean and acyclic. phux-protocol and phux-core have zero internal deps. Any 'crate cycle' reported by graph tooling is an artifact of same-name symbol resolution across crates, not a real dependency.
- Workspace is 151,249 production lines + 70,985 inline-test lines (32% test).
close_reason: All five architecture-knot children completed and published as PR #408

title: Port identity-only lifecycle to the pi and opencode integrations
description:
Deferred from the phux-w7z2.26 fix by explicit ruling. Both shipped npm
integrations declare a real `state` on their lifecycle hooks and therefore
disarm their own manifests exactly as the Claude shim did:

- integrations/pi/src/lifecycle.ts:169
- integrations/opencode/src/lifecycle.ts:165-170

CONSEQUENCE: pi.toml and opencode.toml (two working rules and two blocked
rules each) never reach the record on any pane running these integrations.
phux ships the manifest and the integration disarms it.

WHY IT WAS DEFERRED, not dismissed: these are separately-versioned npm
packages with their own test suites. Dragging them into a Rust bugfix branch
couples two release cadences for no urgency gain, and after phux-w7z2.13
landed they are no longer WEDGED — a killed pi now heals to `unknown` within
about 10 s instead of pinning the pane forever. What remains is display
correctness, which is honestly P1-at-most, not P0.

UNBLOCKED BY: phux-w7z2.13 and phux-w7z2.26 (both landed on this branch).

DO THIS ONE AFTER phux-w7z2.37. That bead found that identity-only writes on
EVERY hook clobber the record's state to `unknown` and break `phux agent wait`
with exit 1 mid-turn. Porting the same shape to pi and opencode before .37 is
resolved would reproduce the regression in two more integrations. Take .37's
final shape — identity written once at session start — and port THAT.

ACCEPTANCE: neither integration writes a `state` on a lifecycle hook; each
one's own suite covers it; the `phux ask` / attention path is preserved with
its hook-exact timing, as it was for Claude.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/integration-identity-only. Both integrations declare identity only, and only once. pi: state removed from the Binding (not merely the record), so a lifecycle transition produces no write; the agent_start/agent_settled subscriptions are removed. opencode: publish() returns early when the session already holds the record on that exact target. Also relaxed AgentRecord.state/attention to optional per L3.md 3.7 (only name is required), tolerated their absence in parseAgentRecord, and made agentSet omit the flags. Proven by: pi 'the record is identity only, and only owner or target changes write it' and 'registration subscribes to no per-turn lifecycle event'; opencode 'documented session status events declare owner-labelled identity, and never a state', which asserts the write count is unchanged across a turn boundary. Three tests that encoded the old behavior were corrected, not deleted. Also fixed the opencode test helper reading an absent flag as argv[0] (indexOf -1, +1 = 0). Both npm suites green (pi 83/83 incl. pack+load smoke, opencode 10/10 incl. pack); just ci rc=0; docs-check 142 files 0 violations. docs/consumers/pi.md and opencode.md updated -- both described the removed state-reporting behavior.

title: Split the phux_agent MCP action multiplexer into distinct tools before ADR-0071 freezes its argument shape
description:
Completeness-critique risk R3. A one-way door with a deadline attached, and the plan did not mention 1.0 at all.

ADR-0071 decision 1 freezes THE MCP TOOL NAMES AND ARGUMENTS at 1.0. phux_agent is today a single action multiplexer covering list, show, explain, set and clear - see docs/consumers/mcp.md sections 3.13 through 3.22. If prompt, wait, read and send-keys get folded in as new action values, the argument UNION is frozen with them, and every future agent verb must fit a shape designed for five READ verbs. A prompt argument set carries text, an operation id, a wait sub-object and a timeout. A wait argument set carries a repeatable until list. A read argument set carries tail, unwrap and eventually transcript. None of those belong in the same union as list and clear, and once frozen none can leave.

SPLIT THEM BEFORE 1.0, NOT AFTER. That is the whole decision. The cost of getting it wrong is not a bad API, it is a bad API that cannot be changed.

Small, but deadline-bound, which is why it is P1 rather than P2. It should be settled in the same pass as the ADR-0071 carve-out phux-w7z2.2 and it constrains phux-w7z2.11.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-0071 either enumerates the agent MCP tools as distinct named tools, or explicitly accepts the multiplexer with the argument union it will be frozen with, stated in the ADR.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: VERIFY whether the acknowledged-input lane is per-Terminal or per-server before agent prompt lands
description:
Completeness-critique risk R2. XS to verify, and it is the difference between a scaling bug and a non-issue. It must be answered BEFORE phux-w7z2.5 implements agent prompt, because the answer changes whether fan-out works at all.

ADR-0076 own Tradeoffs say agent prompt occupies the SINGLE acknowledged-operation lane, so two orchestrators prompting different panes can collide into RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. The CLI answer is bounded backoff then exit 1. Under a twelve-pane worktree-per-agent fan-out - which IS the use case this whole epic exists for - that is a thundering herd against one lane, and six months out it reads as phux cannot drive more than a couple of agents.

The wave-2 ADR-0076 revision made this WORSE by naming a second consequence in Tradeoffs: the single server-wide acknowledged lane completion wait blocks the thread every attached keystroke flows through, and agent prompt is the verb that exposes it. A human typing into an attached pane stalls behind another orchestrator prompt.

THE ACTUAL TASK IS TO READ crates/phux-server/src/runtime/input_lane.rs CLOSELY AND ANSWER ONE QUESTION: is the lane per-Terminal or per-server. The reviewer explicitly did not read it closely enough to know, and said so rather than guessing. Do not carry the assumption either way into the implementation.

IF PER-SERVER, this is a design change with an ADR consequence, not a tuning knob, and it should be decided before agent prompt ships rather than after a fan-out user files it. IF PER-TERMINAL, correct ADR-0076 Tradeoffs, which currently overstates the collision, and close this.
acceptance_criteria: A written answer citing the code, and either a correction to ADR-0076 Tradeoffs or a filed design bead for making the lane per-Terminal.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: The detector never retracts or corrects on an occupant KIND CHANGE, leaving a stale kind with a live state
description:
BUG in shipped behaviour, surfaced by the ADR-0075 revision, which names it as an ADR-0046 dependency percent-name cannot ship safely without. Filed P1 for that reason.

VERIFIED IN THE TREE:
- crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/mod.rs:512-523 - when the newly identified kind differs from self.identified, the detector resets its own memory - self.published to None, pending_idle to None, current to None, cadence to Identified - and returns None. It emits NO Retract. Retract is emitted only on the path above, where identification fails entirely.
- crates/phux-server/src/agent_state.rs:159-161 - compose then does if prior.kind.is_none, set kind. A kind that is already present is PRESERVED, so the next State write from the new occupant overwrites state while leaving the OLD kind in place.

FAILURE: a pane hosting claude is killed and codex is started in the same pane. The published record keeps kind claude and gains a live state derived from codex screen rules. A consumer reading that record is told, with full confidence, that a claude agent is working. Nothing in the record is stale-looking - state is fresh, name is present, kind is a lie.

SECOND HALF, worse because it is undetectable by construction: a SAME-kind restart is invisible. crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/identify.rs:52-56 - foreground_agent resolves the foreground pgid, reads its argv, and returns only kind_from_argv. The pgid is DISCARDED. So a new claude process in the same pane is indistinguishable from the old one and no code path anywhere can notice the swap.

WHY IT IS P1 RATHER THAN A CURIOSITY: ADR-0075 point 6 states this exactly - the percent-name write gate refuses only the WITHDRAWN shape, a record carrying a kind with state unknown, which is what withdraw_state leaves behind. It does NOT refuse a record whose occupant changed inside a surviving pane, because that record looks perfectly healthy. So percent-build resolves and delivers input to whatever is in the pane now. ADR-0075 point 7b names the fix as an ADR-0046 change ADR-0075 does not own, which is this bead.

THE FIX ADR-0075 point 7b SPECIFIES, and it has three parts, all of them in ADR-0046 territory:
1. Emit Retract on an identity change when the record is detector-owned.
2. When the record is not detector-owned, a withdraw_state that ALSO overwrites kind, rather than only clearing state.
3. A compose amendment, because today compose refuses to overwrite a present kind and part 2 requires it to.
Retaining the pgid in identify would additionally make a same-kind restart detectable, and that is a separate decision with its own cost - it means the detector holds process identity, which it deliberately does not today.

RELATED: completeness-critique risk R5 - state unknown now carries three distinct meanings and a consumer cannot tell them apart. That argument for a distinguishing marker was declined when point 7 was its only consumer and now has several. Re-run it here rather than in the ADR.
acceptance_criteria: A test that a claude-to-codex swap inside one surviving pane leaves no record claiming kind claude. ADR-0046 amended for whichever of the three parts is adopted. The same-kind-restart hole either closed or written down as accepted with its reason.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-09 on branch fix/agent-detection-p1-bugs. Both halves. Closing
on MUTATION-VERIFIED tests.

WHAT SHIPPED, and it differs from the fix ADR-0075 point 7b specified:

1. compose STOPS PRESERVING a detector-authored kind and name, and reasserts
   both on every write. This is the load-bearing part and it is mandatory, not
   merely tidier: emit_agent_state is try_send (terminal_actor/mod.rs:1908) and
   silently drops on a full sink, so an edge-triggered correction can be LOST.
   Level-triggered reassertion on every write is the only thing that
   self-heals. An explicit writer's name and kind are still preserved — a new
   `explicit_kind` arbiter bucket tracks the latter, which note_explicit_set
   deliberately did not before ("kind is not identity"), leaving an explicit
   kind-only record unprotected against exactly the overwrite L3.md 3.7's
   MUST-preserve list forbids.
2. The foreground pgid is RETAINED (identify.rs already computed and discarded
   it — zero extra syscalls). A same-kind restart is now an identity change
   rather than being undetectable by construction, which was the bead's
   "second half, worse because it is undetectable".
3. An occupant change is a CORRECTION, ONE SET write landing on state
   "unknown" — NOT a Retract. This OVERRULES ADR-0075 point 7b, which asked for
   a Retract, and the reasons are recorded in ADR-0046's new point 11: a
   Retract broadcasts a tombstone, leaves a multi-second hole, kills an
   in-flight `phux agent wait` with exit 1 mid-turn, and cannot fix a
   human-named record's kind at all because withdraw_state never touches kind.

THE INVARIANT this establishes: state "unknown" is the only value that may pair
with a possibly-stale kind, because "unknown" describes no process and
therefore cannot describe a DIFFERENT one. Every correction and withdrawal
routes through it.

TESTS THAT JUSTIFY THIS CLOSURE — all confirmed RED by reintroducing the
defect, then reverted:

  Kind half (mutation: restore `if prior.kind.is_none()` in compose):
    agent_state::tests::compose_reasserts_a_kind_the_detector_authored   FAIL
    runtime::client::agent_drain_tests::
      a_kind_change_corrects_the_record_in_one_write_landing_on_unknown  FAIL
      a_dropped_correction_is_healed_by_the_next_state_write             FAIL
    phux-server::agent_detect::
      a_kind_change_never_leaves_a_stale_kind_beside_a_live_state        FAIL
      (real PTY, real claude -> codex handover in one surviving pane —
       this is the bead's stated acceptance criterion, executed)

  pgid half (mutation: same_occupant = same_kind, discarding the pgid):
    agent_detect::tests::a_same_kind_restart_is_a_new_occupant           FAIL

`a_dropped_correction_is_healed_by_the_next_state_write` is the one to protect:
it fails if anyone reimplements Reidentified as the SOLE path that corrects
kind. Reidentified is a latency optimization, not a correctness mechanism.

WHY THERE IS NO END-TO-END SAME-KIND-RESTART TEST: one was built and deleted.
`exec` preserves the pgid (an occupant swap, not a restart), and emulating a
real shell's tcsetpgrp with `bash -m -c` does not work — verified directly that
`bash -m -c 'sleep 4; sleep 4'` in a pty leaves tcgetpgrp at bash's own pid, so
the first agent is never identified at all. Coverage is the seam unit test plus
a real-PTY test proving the pgid comes back from the kernel.

TWO LIMITS CARRIED FORWARD, both filed rather than hidden:
- phux-w7z2.45 (P2): the correction does NOT reach panes running the Claude
  shim, because the shim writes --kind and the spec requires preserving an
  explicit writer's kind. Spec-faithful, and it is the largest pane
  population. Three options laid out there.
- phux-w7z2.43 (P3): pid-reuse. A pgid alone is recyclable; pairing it with
  the process start time closes that, fielded behind Option<u64> so no
  signature change is needed. Deferred for want of a demonstrated
  misidentification.

R5 (state "unknown" now carrying several distinct meanings) was re-run as the
bead asked, and the answer was NO distinguishing marker: the record carries no
provenance field, and adding one is a record-shape change. ADR-0075's %name
write gate instead uses a shape test, documented there.
close_reason: Both halves fixed: compose reasserts a detector-authored kind/name on every write, and the foreground pgid is retained so a same-kind restart is an identity change. Corrections are one SET landing on unknown, not a Retract (ADR-0046 point 11, overruling ADR-0075 7b). Mutation-verified by compose_reasserts_a_kind_the_detector_authored, a_kind_change_corrects_the_record_in_one_write_landing_on_unknown, a_dropped_correction_is_healed_by_the_next_state_write, the real-PTY a_kind_change_never_leaves_a_stale_kind_beside_a_live_state, and a_same_kind_restart_is_a_new_occupant. Limits filed as phux-w7z2.45 and .43.

title: The shipped Claude shim declares state on every hook, standing the ADR-0046 detector down on the flagship integration
description:
BUG in shipped behaviour. Filed P1: it disables phux's own detection layer on the one agent phux ships the deepest manifest for, and it is the exact precondition for the wedged-forever failure already filed as phux-w7z2.13.

VERIFIED IN THE TREE. crates/phux/src/commands/agent/shim.rs:282-287, the set_state function the hook wrapper installs, emits for every lifecycle hook:
  agent set TARGET --name claude --kind claude --state blocked --attention high
  agent set TARGET --name claude --kind claude --state done --attention normal
  agent set TARGET --name claude --kind claude --state idle --attention none
  agent set TARGET --name claude --kind claude --state working --attention none

Every one supplies a real, non-unknown state. crates/phux-server/src/agent_state.rs note_explicit_set therefore marks the terminal DECLARED, and crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs:175 drops every subsequent detector State write unconditionally, per ADR-0046 point 8. The detector is also removed from detector_owned, so its Retract is dropped too at client.rs:131.

TWO SEPARATE PROBLEMS, both real:
1. The three shipped claude.toml screen and title rules never reach the record on any pane running the shim. phux ships its best manifest and its own integration disarms it. The detection-parity audit ranked claude depth as a gap while the flagship install path makes depth irrelevant.
2. It arms phux-w7z2.13. The audit stated fairly that the DEFAULT phux-agent-wrap.sh leaves state unset and so does not trip the wedge. That mitigation does NOT apply here - agent install-claude installs a wrapper that declares state on every hook, so a SIGKILLed Claude leaves a declared record with no EXIT trap, no agent clear, and a dropped Retract. The pane reads its last hook state forever.

NOTE the shim is not wrong to write state. A lifecycle hook is better evidence than a screen rule and ADR-0046 point 8 says so deliberately. What is wrong is that declared is a permanent latch with no liveness or freshness gate, so hook-quality evidence and a corpse are indistinguishable. Fix directions, and they compose rather than compete:
- Let Retract clear declared. That is the narrow fix already filed as phux-w7z2.13 and it is the one that makes the shim safe to keep as-is.
- Or have the shim declare identity only and let the detector fill state in, which loses the Stop-hook done that is the ONLY done writer phux ships.
Decide which before treating either as done. Also note the third-party consequence: the shim writes --name claude, which is the same kind-constant collision filed as phux-w7z2.25, and ADR-0075 point 7a requires the shim write an addressable per-pane name before percent-name can ship.
acceptance_criteria: TWO THINGS, both still missing. (1) A test that executes the GENERATED shim's hook command against a live server on a pane with a claude-shaped screen and asserts the record carries a claude.toml-DERIVED state. The current proof asserts on the rendered wrapper string only; the detector-stays-armed half is tested separately with a hand-written SET and the two are never joined. (2) phux-w7z2.37 resolved: the identity-only writes clobber state to unknown on every hook and break phux agent wait with exit 1 mid-turn on every shim pane. Do not close this bead while the flagship orchestration loop is broken by its own fix.
notes:
STATUS 2026-08-09, branch fix/agent-detection-p1-bugs: FIX IMPLEMENTED,
DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN. Two reasons, both concrete. Do not close this on the
green CI run — this bug shipped under green CI.

WHAT LANDED. crates/phux/src/commands/agent/shim.rs set_state now writes
identity only:

    blocked)             run_phux agent set "$target" --name claude --kind claude
                         run_phux ask "$target" "Claude needs attention"
    done|idle|working)   run_phux agent set "$target" --name claude --kind claude
    clear)               run_phux agent clear "$target"

No --state, no --attention. The `ask` ladder (ADR-0035/0036) is untouched and
keeps its hook-exact timing — it is the only thing the blocked hook still
contributes that the screen cannot see for itself. The wrapper is now
version-stamped (`# phux-shim-schema: 2`) and install-claude reports
installed / reinstalled / upgraded (schema 1 -> 2).

The bead asked which of the two fix directions to take, and BOTH were taken:
phux-w7z2.13 made `declared` survivable (now closed), AND the shim stopped
declaring state. The `done` loss is written down — L3.md 3.7, the `agent wait`
entry in docs/consumers/agents.md, and phux-w7z2.42 for the CLI honesty.

REASON 1 IT IS OPEN — the causal claim is not test-joined. The proving test,
shim::tests::wrapper_routes_outer_interactive_claude_and_declares_inner_identity_only,
was mutation-verified (restoring `--state "$state" --attention none` makes it
FAIL), so the MECHANISM is pinned. But it asserts on the RENDERED WRAPPER
STRING. The other half of the claim — that the detector consequently stays
armed on a shim pane — is covered only separately, by
phux-server/tests/agent_detect.rs:918
an_identity_only_set_gets_its_state_filled_in_by_the_detector, which uses a
HAND-WRITTEN identity-only SET. Nothing anywhere executes the GENERATED shim
against a live server and observes claude.toml's rules reaching the record.
The two halves are joined by reasoning, not by a test. Given this bead is
about a shipped integration silently disarming a shipped manifest, "the string
looks right" is the same class of evidence that let the original defect ship.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one test that runs the generated wrapper's actual hook
command against a live server on a pane with a claude-shaped screen, and
asserts the record ends up carrying a claude.toml-derived state.

REASON 2 IT IS OPEN — the fix ships a P0 regression, phux-w7z2.37. Identity
writes with no --state serialize `state:"unknown"` (AgentRecord.state has
serde(default) and NO skip_serializing_if), SET_METADATA replaces the record
wholesale, and EdgeTracker treats any edge into Unknown as a departure. So on
a shim pane the Stop hook fires an identity write at the end of EVERY turn and
an in-flight `phux agent wait` exits 1 (agent_departed) mid-turn. That breaks
`agent send-keys` then `agent wait` — the flagship orchestration loop — on
exactly the panes this bead was fixing. Entirely uncovered by tests.
phux-w7z2.37 carries the ~6-line repair (write identity once at SessionStart
rather than on every hook), which keeps this bead's substance intact.

Documented meanwhile as a known divergence in docs/consumers/agents.md section
5.1; remove that callout when .37 closes.

The name half of the original note (the shim writes --name claude, the same
kind-constant collision as phux-w7z2.25) was RULED not-a-bug: a per-pane name
from the shim would break every shipped `agent send-keys --expect-agent
claude` script, since send_keys.rs:420-424 is an exact whole-string match on
record.name. See phux-w7z2.25 for the full reasoning; ADR-0075 point 7a was
reworded to drop its `claude-${PHUX_TERMINAL_ID}` requirement.
close_reason:
Headline was STALE; acceptance criterion was not, and is now met. The shim defect itself was fixed by eb93020b (PR #382), which took SHIM_SCHEMA to 3 and named this bead in its body: set_state now has three arms (clear, start=identity-only, blocked=ask-only), the done/idle/working arms are gone, and the four hooks the installer registers in claude-hooks.json carry no state payload by any route. Verified beyond the wrapper text.

What was genuinely missing was acceptance criterion (1): no test ran the GENERATED wrapper's own hook command against a live server on a claude-shaped pane and asserted the record ends up with a claude.toml-derived state. The mechanism was pinned by a rendered-string assertion and the consequence by a hand-written SET_METADATA, joined by reasoning only. Branch army/w7z2-26-claude-shim adds the_generated_claude_shim_leaves_the_detector_armed_on_a_live_pane to agent_record_e2e.rs (already in the just e2e filterset): it installs the shim for real, runs the installed wrapper's --phux-hook entry point against a live server, and checks three phases -- detector converges on blocked with the shim's identity intact, the per-hook blocked write does not clobber it, and the counterfactual that a schema-1 style state declaration DOES stand the detector down on the same pane.

Mutation-verified both ways: restoring --state working reproduces the original bug verbatim (record pinned to working while the detector's explanation reads blocked); restoring schema 2's identity write fails phase 2. Notably the guard is the schema stamp rather than the absence of --state, because the first draft asserted the string and failed the mutation before reaching the server -- the exact substitution of evidence for behaviour the test exists to end.

No ADR-0046 amendment (point 8's withdrawal rule and point 10's explicit rejection of a TTL already cover staleness), no SHIM_SCHEMA bump (no schema change, so doctor's staleness check still keys correctly). shim.rs:405's --name claude --kind claude was deliberately NOT changed: see phux-8xrw, where I retracted my own instruction to change it.

title: No fleet-wide agent-state stream for the headless watch API (phux agent wait --any)
description:
There is no way to stream agent state for the whole fleet, and closing it is a wire
change, so it was stopped at rather than worked around.

SUBSCRIBE_METADATA (0x54) names ONE (scope, key) pair, and L3's `Scope` has no
wildcard-Terminal variant. So a server-wide subscription to `phux.agent/v1` across
every Terminal is not expressible.

Two no-wire-change workarounds were considered and both are wrong:
- Enumerate Terminals via GET_STATE and subscribe per-Terminal: silently misses
  every pane spawned afterwards, and races spawn.
- Subscribe Scope::Global: wrong scope. Agent records are Terminal-scoped.

COSTS NOTHING TODAY: the CLI's `run_watch` always resolves a target before opening
the stream (`parse_selector(None)` yields `Selector::Current`), so `phux watch` with
no TARGET still watches the focused pane and does get agent_state lines. The gap is
only reachable through the phux-client API.

IT WILL BITE `phux agent wait` if that verb ever wants "wait for ANY agent in the
fleet to go blocked", which is the natural fleet-supervisor query and the thing an
orchestrator actually wants.

The limitation is pinned by a test rather than left to be rediscovered downstream:
crates/phux-client/src/watch.rs `a_server_wide_watch_subscribes_to_events_only`.

FIXING IT means either a `Scope::AnyTerminal` variant or a wildcard key
subscription — a wire change, so: docs/spec/L3.md update, docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md
entry, version bump, and probably a ServerFeature bit. Do not start without that
spec work scoped first; docs/spec/ is normative and code conforms to it.
notes:
REPRICED 2026-08-15 (P3 -> P1) AND THE CONCLUSION IS CONTESTED.

This bead concluded 'closing it is a wire change' and dismissed enumerate-then-subscribe because it 'silently misses every pane spawned afterwards, and races spawn'. That dismissal looks wrong. Evidence read 2026-08-15:

- crates/phux-server/src/state/events.rs:19-21 documents EventScope::Server as 'every event the server emits for ANY Terminal the client may observe'.
- crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs:1968 already sends SubscribeEvents { terminal: None }, i.e. the client is ALREADY a server-wide event subscriber.
- crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/frame.rs:1942-1953 defines AgentEvent::PaneSpawned and PaneClosed with the terminal id carried on the FrameKind::Event envelope.
- crates/phux-server/src/runtime/attach.rs:1799 and :1898 broadcast PaneSpawned server-wide on spawn.

So the pattern is enumerate-at-attach THEN FOLLOW PaneSpawned/PaneClosed to keep the per-Terminal phux.agent/v1 subscription set current. That is not a race; it is the standard enumerate-and-follow shape, and it needs no wildcard-Terminal Scope and no wire change.

Repriced to P1 because two things now depend on the answer: the cross-session attention sidebar (step 1) and the supervisor-agent stream (step 3), and because the wire freeze (ADR-0071, phux-nudq) must not be cut while a phantom wire requirement is on the books.

ACTION: re-verify the four citations above, then either rewrite this bead as a client-side enumerate-and-follow task or document precisely which case PaneSpawned does not cover.
REFINEMENT 2026-08-15, after five-agent recon. My earlier note overreached; the precise finding:

The disqualifier ('enumerate-then-subscribe silently misses every pane spawned afterwards') is FALSE FOR THE TUI, which already holds SubscribeEvents { terminal: None }. EventScope::Server matches every terminal (crates/phux-server/src/state/client_table.rs:350-354), so new panes announce themselves via PaneSpawned and the subscription sweep re-converges. The cross-session sidebar therefore needs NO wire change (epic phux-k0cw).

But the gap this bead names IS REAL somewhere else: the headless watch API, crates/phux-client/src/watch.rs:144-159, where 'phux agent wait --any' has no fleet-wide stream to key on.

ACTION: RE-SCOPE this bead to the watch.rs/'wait --any' gap rather than closing it, and drop the claim that the TUI needs it. It must not block phux-k0cw.

Also recorded, deferred and NOT required by anything: one additive AgentEvent::SessionChanged { session, kind } on the existing server-scoped EVENT stream would retire the k0cw Stage-7 poll. AgentEvent is #[non_exhaustive] with a TLV decoder that yields Unknown for unrecognised tags (phux-protocol/src/wire/frame.rs:1900-1915), so it is strictly additive with no capability bit — but it still costs docs/spec/L1.md, docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md and a PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. Ship the poll first; revisit only if the poll proves too coarse.
RESOLVED FOR THE TUI 2026-08-15 by ADR-0089 (PR #478). The cross-session sidebar shipped with NO wire change, using enumerate-at-attach plus follow-AgentEvent::PaneSpawned/PaneClosed over the server-wide event subscription the client already holds. ADR-0089's 'Alternatives considered' records the rejection and the reasoning.

This bead is therefore now ONLY about the headless surface: crates/phux-client/src/watch.rs, where 'phux agent wait --any' has no equivalent follow and the gap is real. Re-title/re-scope to that when picked up; do not treat it as blocking any TUI work.
RETITLED 2026-08-15. The old title ('L3 has no wildcard-Terminal scope (wire change)') asserted a conclusion that ADR-0089 overturned for the TUI, and it would mislead anyone skimming bd ready. The remaining scope is crates/phux-client/src/watch.rs only.
VERDICT 2026-08-16 (autonomous run, adversarial code-read): NO wire change needed. The stated blocker (Scope has no wildcard-Terminal) is true as fact, false as blocker. Design that works today, one connection, mirroring agent_wait's push+floor: (1) SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS{terminal:None} FIRST (follow channel); (2) GET_STATE{Server} to enumerate panes; (3) per local pane SUBSCRIBE_METADATA(Terminal(id), phux.agent/v1) THEN GET_METADATA on the SAME connection (subscribe-before-get closes the race by frame ordering — the pattern already shipped 3x in attach/driver/subscriptions.rs); (4) on Event PaneSpawned do (3) for the new pane, on PaneClosed prune; (5) GET_STATE poll floor for the residue. EdgeTracker becomes HashMap<TerminalId,EdgeTracker>. Files: phux-client watch.rs (subscribe_fleet), agent_wait.rs (wait_for_any_agent_state), phux commands/agent/wait.rs (--any). CAVEATS that stay: satellite panes normatively refused (L3 does not federate); 512-sub cap silent (poll floor covers); broadcast_event try_send lossiness (poll floor covers). ONE REAL GAP FOUND: session-SEED panes never broadcast PaneSpawned — both emission sites are inside handle_spawn_terminal; seed_session_with_pty on the CreateIfMissing path (runtime/attach.rs ~680) and the headless CREATE_SESSION path (runtime/commands.rs ~2236-2246, used by phux new/worktree) broadcast nothing. Filed separately. ADR-0089's hedge about 'no equivalent follow' for headless does not survive watch.rs:144-160. If a wire change is ever wanted anyway: additive Scope::AnyTerminal tag 0x03, but ADR-0071 wire freeze argues against buying what a HashMap already provides.

title: Review the metadata fanout relaxation: an L3 subscriber no longer has to be attached
description:
A server invariant was relaxed this run to make `phux watch` carry agent state, and
the verify pass flagged it for a reviewer's eye rather than silent acceptance. It
is tested and load-bearing, but nobody has reviewed the invariant change itself.

WHAT CHANGED (no wire change; same frames, same bytes, only fanout target
resolution):
- crates/phux-server/src/state/client_table.rs — new `metadata_mailboxes` map,
  `remember_metadata_mailbox`; `broadcast_metadata_changed` resolves `attached`
  first and falls back to the captured mailbox.
- crates/phux-server/src/state/metadata.rs — `ServerState::metadata_subscribe`
  gained a `tx: mpsc::Sender<Outbound>` parameter (mirrors `subscribe_events`).
- crates/phux-server/src/state/client.rs — `detach` clears `metadata_mailboxes`.
- crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs — `handle_subscribe_metadata` takes
  `&out_tx` and passes it through.

WHY IT WAS NEEDED: `broadcast_metadata_changed` resolved each subscriber's mailbox
through `self.attached` only. `phux watch` never attaches, by design, so it had no
`attached` entry, so its SUBSCRIBE_METADATA registered a subscription that could
never be delivered to. Every agent-detect integration test attaches first, which is
why nothing caught it. The fix mirrors the precedent three files away —
`ClientTable::event_subscriptions` captures the mailbox for exactly this reason,
with a comment saying so.

THE INVARIANT NOW: an L3 metadata subscriber no longer has to be attached. That is
a real semantic change to the client table's lifecycle model and deserves a
reviewer, not a diff skim. Specifically check: mailbox lifetime vs. client
disconnect (detach clears it, but does a dropped connection without detach leak an
entry?), and whether any other broadcast path still assumes attachment.

Load-bearing test: crates/phux-server/tests/agent_detect.rs
`an_unattached_subscriber_receives_the_detectors_record` — verified to fail
(deadline elapses) with the `.or_else(|| self.metadata_mailboxes.get(client_id))`
fallback removed.

ALSO IN SCOPE: this belongs in docs/architecture/ if anywhere. It was deliberately
left out of docs/consumers/agents.md because it has no consumer-visible surface
beyond "`phux watch` now works", which the agent_state paragraph already implies.

`phux agent wait` builds directly on this path, so review it before that lands.
notes:
RAISED TO P1 IN WAVE 2. The reason this bead said review it BEFORE agent wait lands no longer applies, because agent wait LANDED FIRST - phux-w7z2.4 is closed and crates/phux-client/src/agent_wait.rs is now a production consumer of the relaxed fanout path. The invariant change is therefore load-bearing in shipped code and still unreviewed by anyone. That is the whole reason for the bump.

WHAT THE NEW CONSUMER DOES ON THAT PATH, so the reviewer knows what it is protecting: agent wait opens ONE connection, issues SUBSCRIBE_METADATA and then the baseline GET_METADATA on it, and relies on the server registering the subscription strictly before answering the read so nothing published in between is lost. It never attaches. It also runs a CONTINUOUS 150 ms GET_METADATA poll floor alongside the subscription, deliberately, because METADATA_CHANGED is try_send and droppable - so a leaked or misrouted mailbox degrades to a slower correct answer rather than a hang, which is a mitigation but not a reason to skip the review.

THE TWO SPECIFIC QUESTIONS FROM THE ORIGINAL BEAD ARE UNCHANGED AND STILL UNANSWERED: mailbox lifetime versus client disconnect - detach clears metadata_mailboxes, but does a dropped connection WITHOUT a detach leak an entry - and whether any other broadcast path still assumes attachment. A long-lived agent wait that times out and exits without a clean detach is exactly the shape that would expose the first one, and it now happens every time a wait hits 124.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: OSC 9;4 progress as a detection region: the missing working backstop for Claude
description:
Audit rank 1 — the highest accuracy gained per unit of work in the whole
detection-parity report.

crates/phux-server/rules/claude.toml documents its own hole in a trailing comment:
there is no screen-side `working` backstop for installs that set
CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1. phux's ENTIRE `working` derivation for Claude
rests on one rule matching a braille spinner glyph in the OSC title
(`title-busy-spinner`). Disable the title and phux reports `idle` for a working
agent, permanently.

OSC 9;4 (ConEmu-style progress) is an independent, non-string, non-styling-dependent
second source for exactly that state — the agent explicitly telling the terminal "I
started / finished a task". Structural evidence, so it does not decay when an agent
restyles. herdr feeds it alongside the title as
`DetectionInput { screen, osc_title, osc_progress }` (src/detect/manifest.rs:18),
storing the payload with the leading `9;` stripped; manifests match `^4;0` (idle),
`^4;0;0`, `^4;1;-1` (indeterminate/working). 3 rules across claude and grok.

THE CODE SAYS PHUX CANNOT SEE THIS, TWICE, AND IT IS WRONG.
crates/phux-server/src/terminal_actor/mod.rs:191 and :766 say "libghostty-vt does
not surface OSC 9 / OSC 777". True of libghostty, irrelevant to phux: phux already
scans the raw PTY byte stream itself. `Osc133Scanner::feed`
(terminal_actor/osc133.rs:80) is a complete OSC state machine with BEL/ST
terminators, chunk-split handling and a MAX_OSC_LEN bound, and `parse_133` (:158)
simply strip_prefix(b"133;")s and returns None for everything else. Recognizing
`9;4;...` is an added arm in the same function.

WORK:
1. Extend parse_133 -> parse_osc with a Progress(String) mark, or a sibling arm.
   ~30 lines + tests.
2. Mirror the last progress payload on the actor next to `last_title`.
3. Add `progress: &'a str` to regions::Screen (agent_detect/regions.rs:22) and an
   `osc-progress` region; thread it through detect_tick (terminal_actor/mod.rs:1991).
4. Two claude rules using it, plus fixtures.

THE GOTCHA THAT WILL SILENTLY COST YOU A DAY: the scanner is fed at
terminal_actor/mod.rs:2043, which is AFTER the early return at :2036
(`if self.event_sink.is_none() && self.event_subscribers.borrow().is_empty() { return; }`).
Panes with no event subscriber never reach the scanner. The detector runs
regardless of subscribers, so the OSC-9 mirror must be refreshed BEFORE that early
return — same position as `refresh_title()` at :2035. Getting this wrong yields a
signal that works in tests and never fires in production.

No wire change. Nothing in docs/spec/ moves. While here: ADR-0036 closes with "If
libghostty-vt later exposes OSC 9 / OSC 777 ... that can become another source" —
that sentence is obsolete once this lands and should be corrected.

BLOCKED ON the capture bead: whether Claude Code actually emits OSC 9;4 in the
version the fixtures were captured against, and whether
CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1 also suppresses it, is UNVERIFIED. The entire
value of this bead rests on that. Capture before building.
notes: Precondition phux-w7z2.15 is satisfied by captured Claude v2.1.227/228 evidence. Implementing raw PTY OSC 9;4 scan before subscriber early return, detector progress region, Claude working/idle rules and tests.
close_reason: Added bounded raw OSC 9;4 scanning, unconditional no-listener actor mirroring, osc-progress detector region, captured Claude 4;3 working and 4;0 positive-idle rules with blocked priority preserved, explainer support, and edge-semantics documentation. Full CI passed.

title: A declared agent state pins a pane to working forever after the process dies
description:
CORRECTNESS BUG, reachable through documented flags, with no test covering it.
Audit rank 4. Filed as P1 deliberately: this is not polish.

A pane can read `working` forever after the process it describes is dead.

Mechanism:
1. `phux agent set @7 --name x --kind claude --state working` (or PHUX_AGENT_STATE
   through phux-agent-wrap.sh) marks the terminal `declared` in
   crates/phux-server/src/agent_state.rs. ADR-0046 point 8: a declared state
   outranks the detector.
2. The agent hits a permission prompt. The detector derives `blocked`. The write is
   dropped unconditionally at crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs:175
   (`if s.agent_records().is_declared(&wire_terminal_id) { return None; }`). No
   freshness gate, no TTL, no liveness check. `declared` has no timestamp.
3. The agent is SIGKILLed or the pane force-closed, so the wrapper's EXIT trap never
   runs and no `agent clear` is issued. The detector emits
   `AgentDetectEvent::Retract` — AND THAT IS ALSO DROPPED, at
   runtime/client.rs:131, because it short-circuits on `!detector_owns(...)` and
   `note_explicit_set` already removed the terminal from `detector_owned`
   (agent_state.rs:74).

`declared` is cleared by exactly two things: an explicit DELETE_METADATA
(note_explicit_delete, agent_state.rs:99) and terminal reap
(state/agent_tracking.rs:132). Neither fires here.

This is precisely the failure ADR-0046's "Why" section says level-triggering
exists to prevent: "Edge-triggered reporters are lossy... the pane is wedged in a
lie with no path back to truth."

Stated fairly: the shipped phux-agent-wrap.sh leaves `state` unset by default, and
note_explicit_set treats an explicit "unknown" as not-a-declaration, so today's
default integrations do not trip this. It is reachable through documented flags and
is the kind of thing a fleet script does.

NARROW FIX, and this is the whole bead — a bug fix, NO ADR change needed: let
`Retract` clear `declared` as well. A declaration about a process that has exited
is not a declaration about anything. This is herdr's `recent_agent_process_exit`
gate (src/terminal/state.rs:1692) and it closes the wedged-forever half without
introducing any screen-beats-human policy.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE HERE (policy, needs ADR-0046 point 8 amended): letting a
fresh `visible_blocker` override a declared non-blocked state, herdr's
`visible_blocker_overrides_hook` (state.rs:1737). File separately if wanted.

ACCEPTANCE: a test that a declared `working` record is retracted when the process
exits. The AgentRecordArbiter unit tests cover ownership and label preservation
thoroughly but have NO test for a stale declaration outliving its process — the
failure currently has no test to fail.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-09 on branch fix/agent-detection-p1-bugs. Closing on
MUTATION-VERIFIED tests, not on a green CI run.

MECHANISM SHIPPED: liveness-gated WITHDRAWAL to "unknown". Never a delete,
never a derived value written over a declaration. The bead proposed "let
Retract clear declared" and called it a bug fix needing no ADR change. That
turned out to be wrong on the spec: docs/spec/L3.md:335 forbade overwriting a
declared state, :341 forbids deleting a record the server did not author, and
together they were a closed box with no conforming exit. Withdrawing `state`
to "unknown" threads it — the server asserts nothing it derived and the record
survives with the human's name/kind/session — but it is still a write to a
declared state, so it needed one clause of amendment. That was done properly:
L3.md 3.7's first bullet narrowed from "MUST NOT overwrite" to "MUST NOT
overwrite WITH A DERIVED VALUE", plus a new "MAY withdraw" bullet; spec
version 0.7.0-draft.3 with PROTOCOL_VERSION correctly UNCHANGED (no wire
change); ADR-0046 points 8 and 10 amended, new point 11.

EVIDENCE STANDARD, and this is half the fix: withdrawal fires only on POSITIVE
evidence of vacancy — an occupancy query that SUCCEEDED and found no agent —
never on a query that failed. identify.rs's foreground_agent -> Option<String>
conflated those two and is gone, replaced by foreground_occupancy -> Occupancy
{ Unresolved | Vacant{pgid} | Agent{kind,pgid} }. Unresolved touches nothing.
Two confirmations at the recheck cadence are required before any retraction.

TESTS THAT JUSTIFY THIS CLOSURE — both confirmed RED by reintroducing the
defect (restoring `if is_declared { return None }` in drain_retract), then
reverted:

  runtime::client::agent_drain_tests::
    a_retract_withdraws_a_declared_state_but_never_deletes_it   FAIL
  phux-server::agent_detect::
    a_declared_state_does_not_survive_the_death_of_the_process_it_describes
                                                                FAIL (12.9s,
    real PTY, real process, no EXIT trap, no agent clear, pane survives)

The first test previously existed as `a_retract_never_touches_a_declared_record`
— that is, THIS BUG was pinned as intended behavior by a passing test. It was
renamed and inverted deliberately, and its doc comment now points at the
amended L3 bullet.

Supporting guards: withdrawing_a_declaration_twice_broadcasts_once,
withdraw_state_is_byte_idempotent (mutation-verified: stamping any varying
field into the record makes it FAIL, which is the ADR-0046 decision 7
write-rate invariant holding), an_unresolved_occupancy_never_retracts,
a_vacant_pane_retracts_once_and_then_is_silent (20 vacant ticks => 1 retract).

ALSO FIXED, in no bead: withdraw_state now clears `attention` too. Previously
a pane healed to "unknown" while still wearing a red `high` badge.

Docs: docs/consumers/agents.md `agent set`/`agent clear` now document the
declared record's three ways to end; docs/consumers/tui.md section 5.6 says a
killed agent no longer leaves its row painted `working`.

CARRIED FORWARD: phux-w7z2.38 (pi and opencode declare state the same way and
were wedged by this; no longer wedged, now display correctness).
close_reason: Fixed by liveness-gated withdrawal to unknown, plus the L3.md 3.7 spec amendment that makes it legal. Mutation-verified by a_retract_withdraws_a_declared_state_but_never_deletes_it and the real-PTY a_declared_state_does_not_survive_the_death_of_the_process_it_describes; both confirmed RED against the reintroduced defect.

title: Binary-compiled phux skill via include_str! so the printed skill matches the binary
description:
Ship an agent skill that is compiled into the binary via `include_str!`, printed by
`phux skill` (or `phux --skill`), so the instructions an agent reads always match
the binary it is driving.

Today phux ships example skills as loose repo files — examples/skills/phux-agent-cli/SKILL.md
and examples/skills/phux-terminal/SKILL.md. Nothing ties them to the binary. They
document verbs, flags and JSON shapes, and every bead under this epic changes some
of that. An installed phux from a release and a SKILL.md copied from the repo at
some other commit will disagree, silently, in the one document whose entire job is
to tell an agent what the CLI can do. herdr compiles its skill into the binary for
exactly this reason.

Scope:
- `include_str!` the canonical skill markdown at build time; `phux skill` prints it
  to stdout and exits 0.
- Decide what happens to the examples/skills/ copies: either they become the
  compiled source of truth (one file, included, still readable in-repo) or they are
  deleted in favour of the compiled one. Two copies is the bug.
- A test that the compiled skill mentions every top-level verb in the clap tree
  would catch the drift this bead exists to prevent — the same trick
  refdocs::tests::generated_reference_docs_match_the_tree uses for
  docs/reference/cli.md.

Independent of the ADR ratification: the mechanism is worth landing before the new
verbs arrive, so the verbs land into a surface that cannot drift.
notes:
RAISED TO P1 IN WAVE 2. Rationale, from completeness-critique F9: the skill is ALREADY DRIFTING before any new verb ships, and wave 2 just shipped four surface changes on top of it. Measured drift, today: examples/skills/phux-agent-cli/SKILL.md section 6 says phux-mcp exposes 21 strict tools, docs/consumers/mcp.md TL;DR says 22, and crates/phux-mcp/src/tools.rs:213-227 enumerates 22. The skill section 6 parity table omits phux_paste entirely, twice, while mcp.md 3.12 documents it as the PREFERRED verb for multiline text. That drift happened over a surface that changes far less often than the one this epic is changing.

F9 recommendation, verbatim in intent: ship this in the SAME PR as the first new agent verb, not as follow-up. It is not packaging, it is the mechanism that makes the docs a build artifact instead of a hope. That window was already missed once in wave 2 - agent wait and agent send-keys landed and the skill still does not mention them.

CONTENT THE SKILL MUST GAIN, ranked:
1. AN AM-I-INSIDE-PHUX CHECK. The skill lacks one entirely. phux already injects PHUX_TERMINAL_ID and PHUX_SOCKET into every spawned pane at crates/phux-server/src/terminal_actor/spawn.rs:644 and :661. The skill mentions neither, so an agent inside a phux pane cannot learn that it is, or which pane it is, and therefore cannot avoid prompting itself. HIGHEST VALUE LINE AVAILABLE AND IT NEEDS ZERO NEW CODE.
2. phux agent wait is satisfied only by an OBSERVED TRANSITION. Exit 124 means no transition was observed, which is NOT the same statement as the agent is still working. A pane already resting in a target state times out. An LLM will get this wrong without the sentence.
3. INPUT_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN must never be retried under a new id, ADR-0076 point 2, in those words. It is the one rule an agent can violate catastrophically.
4. prompt --wait is the ONLY safe wait shape across two calls, ADR-0076 point 6.
5. wait --until and --regex now match LOGICAL lines, not painted rows, and --output-only exists. The old advice to match on text that appears only in output still stands for panes with no OSC-133 integration.
6. percent-name addressing and its three refusal outcomes, if and when ADR-0075 lands - an LLM that reads exit 2 as retry will loop.
7. snapshot --transcript MOVES the pane, if and when ADR-0078 lands. The skill current invariant list says reads are safe and that becomes false in the same release.
8. Verbs the skill has never mentioned at all: phux agent list, show, explain, phux take and give, phux worktree, phux rec and play, phux signal.
9. One sentence on the percent sigil not being tool-safe, completeness-critique R6: percent is a format specifier in printf and opens a pattern rule in a Makefile, which is exactly where fan-out scripts live. Not a design change, one sentence.

THE DRIFT TEST IS THE POINT: a test that the compiled skill mentions every top-level verb in the clap tree, the same trick refdocs::tests::generated_reference_docs_match_the_tree uses. That test is what stops item 8 recurring.
close_reason: Shipped: skills/phux/SKILL.md is include_str!'d into the binary as crate::SKILL and printed by a new socketless `phux skill` verb (exit 0; a stray --socket is refused with exit 2). Four drift tests in crates/phux/src/help_inventory.rs derive their expectation from the clap tree and the selector parser rather than a second list: skill_names_every_visible_top_level_verb, skill_names_every_agent_subcommand, skill_teaches_every_selector_sigil_the_parser_accepts (exhaustive match on Selector with no wildcard, so a new sigil fails to COMPILE), skill_teaches_the_load_bearing_rules, plus skill_cites_nothing_only_a_checkout_has. The gate already worked in-flight: agent prompt landed during this run and its author added the skill section rather than drifting. Content covers the bead's ranked list: PHUX_TERMINAL_ID/PHUX_SOCKET am-I-inside-phux check, level-vs-edge (agent wait is an observed transition; a level idle is equally true of a crashed pane; 124 != still working), unknown-delivery-is-never-a-retry, watch --until/--timeout, %name and its three refusals plus the printf/Makefile sigil hazard, ls --json unreachable, and the full verb inventory including take/give/signal/rec/play/worktree/skill. examples/skills/ NOT deleted (outside ownership, and linked from docs/CONCEPTS.md + docs/consumers/mcp.md) - recommendation to demote it to an MCP/fleet example is in the handoff. docs/reference/cli.md needs `just docs-gen` by the later docs agent.

title: phux wait --until silently misses soft-wrapped text; add --regex
description:
BUG, not a feature request.

`phux wait --until TEXT` matches against RAW VIEWPORT ROWS. A line the terminal
soft-wrapped is two rows in the grid, so a substring that straddles the wrap point
never matches — the wait silently runs to its 124 timeout even though the text is
plainly on screen. There is no error, no warning, and nothing in the output tells
the caller why. The failure scales with narrow panes, which is exactly the case
agent orchestration hits (split layouts).

herdr treats this as load-bearing enough to rewrite the read source automatically
rather than make the caller ask for it.

FIX (ADR-0077 decision point 1): `wait --until` unwraps before matching, using the
`soft_wrap` row indices from the ScreenState read-surface bead. No new
`Condition` variant is needed for this half — crates/phux-client/src/wait.rs keeps
`Condition::{Text, Idle}` and only the matching input changes.

SECOND HALF, same bead because it is the same matcher:
`phux wait --regex PATTERN` adds `Condition::Regex`. Today the condition vocabulary
is literal-substring or idle-only, which forces callers into polling loops with
external grep for anything structural. Compile once at parse time so a bad pattern
is a usage error (exit 2), never a wait that can never succeed.

ACCEPTANCE: a regression test that a soft-wrapped match succeeds at a pane width
that splits the phrase, and that the pre-fix behaviour would fail it; `--regex`
covered including the invalid-pattern exit path.
close_reason: Landed in the worktree, wave 2. BOTH halves done. Soft-wrap half: crates/phux-client/src/wait.rs now unwraps before matching via phux_core screen unwrapped_rows, so a needle straddling a wrap is found, and rows are matched verbatim when soft_wrap is absent, which is the old behaviour and is detectable rather than guessed. Regression tests contains_matches_across_a_soft_wrap and contains_matches_across_the_history_seam. Regex half: MatchRegex compiles at argv-parse time through a clap value_parser, so an invalid pattern exits 2 before any socket is opened, never a wait that can never succeed. Also landed beyond the bead, and it closes completeness-critique finding F6, transient output scrolling off the viewport between two 150ms polls: wait --tail N scopes matching to the last N logical lines and reads that much history to do it, capped at 10000. Unwrap runs before windowing so a window can never bisect a wrapped run. Third addition, wait --output-only, drops lines the shell marked OSC-133 Input so a wait cannot be satisfied by the echo of the command that started the work, with a pre-flight probe that says so on stderr when the pane carries no marks rather than silently filtering nothing. regex 1 added to phux-client, already a direct dep of phux-server, so no new crate enters the build. No wire change. 31 new tests. EVIDENCE cargo nextest run --workspace 3246 of 3246 passed, docs-check 142 files 0 violations, and a live smoke on a 60-column pane where the pre-fix path timed out at 124 and the post-fix path exits 0.

title: ScreenState read surface: soft_wrap, truncated, title, and snapshot --unwrap
description:
Implement ADR-0077 decision point 1 — the additive half of the read surface, with
no new read-source vocabulary.

phux deliberately does NOT adopt herdr's `visible|recent|recent-unwrapped|detection`
source enum. `--scrollback[=N]` and `--cells` keep their meaning; what herdr
expresses as a source is expressed here as orthogonal modifiers.

Four additive JSON keys on ScreenState:
- `soft_wrap { lines[], scrollback[] }` — per-row wrap indices from libghostty. The
  consumer joins; phux does not pre-join, so a caller that wants raw rows still has
  them.
- `truncated` (bool) and `truncated_reason` (typed string).
- `title` — the OSC title, which ScreenState does not carry today. This is also
  what makes `phux agent explain --file` usable without a separate `--title`, since
  a capture currently has no title at all.

SCHEMA_VERSION STAYS 3. docs/consumers/agents.md 4.1 already rules that adding a
key is non-breaking; do not bump it and do not invent a second document.

Also: `phux snapshot --unwrap` as the CLI-side modifier.

No wire change for this bead. (The harvest bead is the one wire change in ADR-0077,
and it is separate on purpose.)

This is the prerequisite for the `phux wait` soft-wrap bug: the unwrap helper that
`wait --until` needs to match across a wrapped line comes from here, which is why
that bug depends on this bead rather than growing its own copy.
close_reason: Landed in the worktree, wave 2, ahead of ratification bead phux-w7z2.1 which stays open. crates/phux-core/src/screen.rs gained SoftWrap plus optional soft_wrap, truncated, truncated_reason and title, a Default impl, unwrapped_rows / unwrapped_split / rendered_rows / has_soft_wrap_info, and row_window with ROW_WINDOW_ALL, ROW_WINDOW_DEFAULT 80 and ROW_WINDOW_MAX 10000. SCHEMA_VERSION stays 3 as this bead required. crates/phux-server/src/grid/synthesizer.rs populates wrap bits for viewport and history, truncated and title. CLI gained snapshot --tail and snapshot --unwrap, both client-side projections with no wire change. soft_wrap is an Option specifically so absent, meaning an older server, is distinguishable from present-and-empty, meaning nothing wraps. truncated is scoped to requested-window clipping only, so the ADR-0078 harvest must mint its own key. 23 new tests plus a live smoke. EVIDENCE cargo nextest run --workspace 3246 of 3246 passed, just docs-check 142 files 0 violations, refdocs generated_reference_docs_match_the_tree PASS. docs/consumers/agents.md 4.1 and 4.2 and docs/reference/cli.md updated.

title: phux agent prompt on APPLY_INPUT, with ownership re-verification
description:
Implement ADR-0076 points 1-4 and 6. `phux agent prompt TARGET TEXT` is the first
verb in the tree to use APPLY_INPUT (0x14, ADR-0053) — today `send-keys` and
`paste` are both fire-and-forget ROUTE_INPUT, so the acknowledged path has no
caller.

Shape:
- Gated on the ACKNOWLEDGED_INPUT capability with NO silent downgrade to
  ROUTE_INPUT, and no satellite targets (APPLY_INPUT is local-only; a satellite
  target returns UNSUPPORTED_SATELLITE_ROUTE).
- Text and Enter are ONE batch: [Paste(trusted, text), Key(Enter)]. No submit
  delay. Enter must be last: a partial write then drops the submission and leaves
  unsubmitted text, whereas two batches admit an ambiguous text write followed by a
  confident Enter that submits a truncated prompt.
- Each typed error has exactly one reading. INPUT_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN is TERMINAL —
  a same-id retry returns the same cached unknown and a new id is the duplicate the
  design exists to prevent — so the CLI never retries and exits 3 with the
  operation id. Pre-handoff refusals (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, INPUT_LEASE_HELD,
  UNSAFE_PASTE) are honest to retry unchanged. CANONICAL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED is not.
- Ownership is re-verified from the detector's published record (staleness bound
  ~5s per ADR-0046 point 10), NOT from a fresh syscall and NOT from a server-side
  gate. Detection fails safe toward idle, but input must fail safe toward delivery.
  ADR-0076 explicitly rejects a server-side agent-readiness gate on APPLY_INPUT.
- `prompt --wait` subscribes to metadata BEFORE submitting, on one connection, so
  every METADATA_CHANGED after the result is strictly post-write. This is the whole
  ordering argument; do not split it across connections.
- Explicitly NOT built: an activity gate, an `agent_prompt_stalled` error, or a
  server-side "seen" bit. An ACK proves delivery; inferring delivery from
  post-submit behavior is the output-inference oracle ADR-0053 already rejected.

If ADR-0075 lands, the "re-verify the pane still hosts the agent before writing
bytes" rule must be specified in exactly one place shared with `%name`
resolution — see the ratification bead.

ACCEPTANCE: one test per typed error demonstrating the documented reading;
idempotency test reusing an operation_id; a test that a satellite target refuses
rather than downgrading.
notes:
WAVE-2 REVISION OF ADR-0076 CHANGED THIS BEAD. Read ADR/0076-agent-prompt-and-lifecycle-wait.md, not the summary above. Still blocked on ADR-0076 acceptance, which is phux-w7z2.1.

1. EXIT 3 IS GONE FROM THIS VERB. The bead says the CLI never retries and exits 3 with the operation id on INPUT_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN. That collided with crates/phux/src/exit_codes.rs EXIT_PARTIAL_VIEW and with the published meaning in docs/consumers/agents.md 5.2, where 3 means retry is correct - the opposite of what the ADR wanted to say. It is now EXIT 1 with the operation id, and delivery to an unknown occupant moved from 3 to 1 for the same reason. The terminal-ness of INPUT_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN is unchanged and is still the one rule an agent can violate catastrophically.

2. THE ACK OVERCLAIM IS DELETED. The old text said the acknowledgment is the delivery statement, so post-ACK silence is a busy agent, not a lost keystroke. That is not what the code proves. crates/phux-server/src/terminal_actor/spawn.rs:336-341 does write_all plus flush on the PTY MASTER, which is strictly more than ROUTE_INPUT states and strictly less than consumption. The ADR now calls OK a kernel-queue receipt and says so in those words, citing L1 6.2.1. The activity gate is still rejected, but the rejection now rests on ADR-0053 output-inference-oracle argument plus unsoundness in both directions, not on the receipt. NEW in Tradeoffs: a slave calling TCSAFLUSH discards an ACKed batch silently, and the honest recovery is timeout plus agent explain.

3. NEW DECISION POINT ADDED BEYOND THIS BEAD: prompt text containing a raw newline is REFUSED. paste encode converts newlines to carriage returns when the pane has not set DEC 2004, the CLI cannot observe that mode, and the failure is silent N-plication - strictly worse than the double this verb exists to prevent.

4. THE STALENESS BOUND IN THIS BEAD IS FALSE AS WRITTEN. The 5s ADR-0046 bound applies to a DETECTOR-owned record only. phux own Claude shim writes --state on every hook with no bound and no tombstone, and L3 gives a consumer no way to tell the classes apart. The --json document now reports which record the check passed on.

5. UNSAFE_PASTE IS NOT A LIVE REFUSAL. It cannot arise, because TRUSTED skips safety classification. The ADR now names that as a deliberate bypass of the pane untrusted-paste policy on caller-supplied text.

6. SATELLITE TARGETS ARE REFUSED FOR agent wait TOO, not just prompt, with a distinct reason - L3 does not federate.

7. NEW DECISION POINT 7 defines the --json evidence document: delivery, operation_id, agent, pre_submit_state, transition_observed, matched_by, waited_ms, and a degraded-to-polling flag, with a Layer L3 declaration requirement.

8. prompt --wait IS NOW EDGE-GATED, matching the shipped agent wait. Only a POST-RESULT transition satisfies it. The pre-submit level never does. See docs/spec/L3.md 3.7, now normative.

9. FLAGGED BY THE ADR AUTHOR AND NOT WRITTEN INTO EITHER ADR - the percent-name circularity. ADR-0076 ownership re-verification gate is TAUTOLOGICAL for a percent-name target, because the name came from the record it re-reads. The gate is only meaningful for at-N targets, and ADR-0076 still does not cite ADR-0075. One of the two ADRs must own this. It belongs in the ratification bead phux-w7z2.1.

10. ADR-0076 IS 198 LINES against the roughly-150 convention in docs/CONVENTIONS.md. The prescribed remedy is to move the body into docs/architecture and point at it. The natural split is decision points 2 and 7, the error and exit contract and the --json document shape.
