title: phux agent wait --until STATE: event-driven off the metadata subscription
description:
Implement ADR-0076 point 5. `phux agent wait TARGET --until STATE... --timeout MS`
waits on the `phux.agent/v1` L3 record, not on the screen.

Shape:
- SUBSCRIBE_METADATA (0x54) on `phux.agent/v1`, Terminal-scoped, plus a
  GET_METADATA (0x50) fast path so an already-satisfied state returns immediately.
- Repeated `--until` values are ORed. Default `idle,done,blocked`.
- Tombstone (record deleted) = miss, exit 1. Timeout = exit 124, matching
  crates/phux/src/exit_codes.rs.
- Poll fallback if the subscription is lost.
- No wire change, no additive field. Ordering comes from subscribing before acting
  on one connection, which is why ADR-0076 rejects herdr's `state_change_seq`.

The ADR states the failure case explicitly and the implementation must document it
in the same words: split-connection callers (`prompt ... && wait ...`, two MCP
calls, federated paths) have no shared ordering point and must use
`prompt --wait` or first observe a transition into `working`.

This builds directly on the metadata-subscription plumbing that landed this run
(crates/phux-client/src/watch.rs subscribing to SUBSCRIBE_METADATA, and the server
fanout relaxation that lets an unattached client receive METADATA_CHANGED). Do not
start before that relaxation has been reviewed — see the review bead.

Note the known limitation: there is no fleet-wide agent-state stream, because
SUBSCRIBE_METADATA names one (scope, key) pair and L3 has no wildcard-Terminal
scope. `agent wait` on "any agent in the fleet" is therefore out of scope here and
filed separately.

ACCEPTANCE: exit codes 0/1/124 covered by tests; a test that the GET_METADATA fast
path fires before any subscription event; docs/consumers/agents.md updated.
close_reason: Landed in the worktree, wave 2, with ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION from this bead text recorded below. crates/phux-client/src/agent_wait.rs carries EdgeTracker, wait_for_agent_state and fetch_agent_record. crates/phux/src/commands/agent/wait.rs is the CLI surface: phux agent wait --until STATE repeatable and ORed over idle, working, blocked, done, default idle,blocked,done, --timeout in SECS not MS to match phux wait, --json, optional TARGET with focused-pane fallback. Exit 0 satisfied, 124 timeout, 1 departure or transport, 2 no record or unknown --until word. subscribe and the baseline GET_METADATA ride ONE connection so the subscription is registered strictly before the read, and interleaved frames published in between are folded into the observation sequence rather than dropped. The GET_METADATA poll is a CONTINUOUS 150ms floor, not a subscription-loss fallback, because METADATA_CHANGED is try_send and droppable and the detector is edge-filtered, so the poll recovers a dropped edge and its answer goes through the same must-differ rule. No wire change. DEVIATION: this bead specified a GET_METADATA fast path so an already-satisfied state returns immediately. That was struck by the governing level-versus-edge ruling now normative in docs/spec/L3.md 3.7 and it is NOT implemented. A completion gate satisfied by a level read of idle returns success on a corpse instantly and on every pane with no manifest loaded, because idle is the detector fail-safe fallthrough and zero shipped manifest rules assert it positively. The wait is satisfied only by an OBSERVED TRANSITION into a --until member. Consequence, documented and loud: a pane already resting in a target state times out at 124 rather than exiting 0, and the timeout diagnostic names the baseline. 15 tests including two corpse tests, one pure and one end-to-end on a real UDS whose 0.390s wall time against a 250ms deadline is the proof it waited the deadline out rather than returning instantly. EVIDENCE cargo nextest run --workspace 3246 of 3246 passed, fmt and clippy -D warnings clean. NOTE the bead said not to start before the fanout-relaxation review bead phux-w7z2.19, which is still OPEN. It shipped on that path anyway and the review is still owed.

title: Implement ADR-0075: %name agent addressing in the selector grammar
description:
Implement ADR-0075. `%name` becomes a selector sigil parsed to
`Selector::Agent(String)` in crates/phux-client/src/selector.rs and resolved
CLIENT-SIDE (ADR-0021) against the TerminalId -> AgentRecord index that
crates/phux/src/commands/agent/record.rs already builds for `phux agent ls`.

Zero wire, key or schema change: the name is the REQUIRED field `phux.agent/v1`
already carries. `%` was chosen because bare names are taken by sessions,
`agent:name` collides with the window separator `:`, `#tag` is set-valued (wrong
shape) and opens a comment in an unquoted interactive bash.

Load-bearing rules from the ADR:

- A name resolves to exactly ONE Terminal or the verb refuses. `pick_target_pane`
  is never applied. Unknown name = selector miss (exit 1). Two live records with
  the same name = refuse with every candidate `@N` enumerated (exit 2). An
  incompletely fetched index = refuse as partial (exit 3), so "nothing matched"
  and "we did not finish looking" never collapse.
- Uniqueness is advisory at `agent set` (L3 is last-writer-wins and ADR-0017
  forbids server validation) and enforced at resolve.
- Addressable grammar `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`, validated at parse time and at
  write time. The record's `name` field is deliberately left looser.
- The name follows the occupant: it dies with the pane for free; when the pane
  survives but the occupant changes, the ADR-0046 detector writes state "unknown"
  and input-delivering verbs refuse a `%name` whose state is unknown rather than
  retargeting.

REQUIRED CODE CHANGE THE ADR FLAGS AS A CONFLICT: `fetch_agent_index`
(crates/phux/src/commands/agent/record.rs:199) is best-effort by design — its doc
comment says it returns what it collected on transport failure "so the caller
degrades to heuristics instead of erroring". `%name` resolution must distinguish a
complete index from a truncated one, so that function needs a changed return shape
or a completeness flag. Degrading to a partial index would turn a real ambiguity
into a silent single match, which is exactly the failure the ADR refuses. Check
every existing caller when changing it.

ACCEPTANCE: `%name` works for read verbs and refuses correctly for the three
failure modes with tests for each; docs/consumers/agents.md and the generated
docs/reference/cli.md updated (regenerate via `just docs-gen`, it is byte-compared
by refdocs::tests::generated_reference_docs_match_the_tree).
notes:
WAVE-2 REVISION OF ADR-0075 CHANGED THIS BEAD MATERIALLY. Read ADR/0075-agent-name-addressing.md, not the summary above - the ADR was retitled from a name follows the pane occupant to a WITHDRAWN name is refused, because the old title promised a property the detector does not deliver.

1. THE WRITE GATE IS DIFFERENT. This bead says input-delivering verbs refuse a percent-name whose state is unknown. That rule is GONE. It locked out a bare phux agent set --name build, which writes a record with no kind and state unknown. The gate is now the WITHDRAWN SHAPE - refuse only when the record carries a kind AND state unknown, which is precisely what agent_state withdraw_state leaves behind and is client-observable because AgentRecord kind is skip_serializing_if is_none. Verbs gated: send-keys, paste, signal, run, plus any ADR-0053 batch verb. This is a SAFETY gate and it reads the LEVEL, per docs/spec/L3.md 3.7 which is now normative - absence of contrary evidence is the right predicate for do not disturb this, and a crashed pane reading as do-not-disturb errs conservatively.

2. THE DETECTOR PREREQUISITE THE FIRST DRAFT GOT WRONG, now ADR-0075 point 6. An occupant change inside a SURVIVING pane leaves a record that looks perfectly healthy - the new occupant overwrites state while the old kind is preserved - and point 5 guard PASSES there. So percent-build silently retargets input at whatever is in the pane now. Filed as phux-w7z2.27 and added as a dependency. ADR-0075 point 7b names the fix as ADR-0046 territory this ADR does not own. THE HUMAN MUST DECIDE whether percent-name ships before or after that guard exists - the ADR states what is true either way and deliberately does not choose.

3. THE SHIM RENAME IS A HARD PREREQUISITE, ADR-0075 point 7a. crates/phux/src/commands/agent/shim.rs writes --name claude, and the detector writes the manifest constant claude, so percent-claude is ambiguous across every Claude pane. The shim must write claude-PHUX_TERMINAL_ID with a PHUX_AGENT_NAME override before percent-name ships. Detector half filed as phux-w7z2.25 and added as a dependency. USER-VISIBLE MIGRATION: existing agent install-claude installations keep writing --name claude until re-run, so percent-claude stays ambiguous on those machines. Someone must decide whether that needs a migration notice in the shim output.

4. SCOPE NARROWED TO HUB-LOCAL. L3 does not federate, so percent-name sees hub-local panes only. A satellite agent is an exit-1 MISS, not a refusal. Uniqueness is hub-side. Federating L3 is explicitly out of scope.

5. WRITE-TIME UNIQUENESS AND WRITE-TIME CHARSET NARROWING WERE BOTH DROPPED. They cost an O-of-panes round trip on a verb that pays none, and narrowed a frozen surface, while resolve-time refusal was already the enforcing check. Do not re-add them.

6. EXIT CODES ARE A CHANGE, NOT AN ASSUMPTION. send-keys and paste have no exit 2 today per docs/consumers/agents.md 5.2 and gain one. run mirrors its child status so a refusal there stays exit 1 in words, and that collision is now explicit. resolve_targets becomes fallible. Exit 3 is pinned to phux could not answer, explicitly NOT retry, the same reading ADR-0076 now uses. STILL NEEDS A HUMAN SIGN-OFF: this makes a partial index a hard exit-3 refusal for percent-name while hash-tag still degrades to an empty index. That is a deliberate asymmetry between two selectors resolved at the same seam.

7. phux-mcp resolve_one is named in the ADR: pick_target_pane must not be applied there either, since it applies unconditionally today on a frozen surface.

8. OPEN, scoped by the ADR author and left undecided: whether the point-5 guard should also cover attach and kill. It was scoped to verbs that write into the PTY. kill percent-name on a withdrawn record destroys a pane whose occupant may have changed.
IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE in feat/agent-epic-fanout and full nix develop -c just ci is green (3525 passed, 72 skipped). Left open because Beads correctly blocks closure on unresolved human ADR ratification phux-w7z2.1 (or, for downstream items, on a bead blocked by it); do not reimplement.

title: Carve the agent CLI/JSON surface into ADR-0071 before the 1.0 freeze
description:
ADR-0071 (Status: Proposed) freezes the CLI JSON surface for 1.0. It does not name
two things that have ALREADY SHIPPED in this repo, and it does not name anything
ADR-0075/0076/0077 would add.

Already shipped, unnamed by 0071:

- `AgentExplainJson` — the `phux agent explain --file ... --json` document
  (schema_version 1, top-level `capture` + `explain`), produced by
  crates/phux/src/commands/agent/offline.rs and documented in
  docs/consumers/agents.md 4.7.
- The `agent_state` event name on the `phux watch` stream, with fields
  name / kind / session / state / attention / from and a present-and-null `state`
  tombstone. Rendered by crates/phux/src/commands/watch.rs. The stream carries no
  schema_version by design (ADR-0071 itself), so the event-name vocabulary IS the
  contract.
- Three new error codes in crates/phux/src/commands/json_err.rs:
  `capture_unreadable`, `capture_invalid` (exit 1), `unknown_agent_kind` (exit 2).

Proposed, pending the ratification bead: `%name` selector syntax (0075);
`agent prompt`, `agent wait`, `--wait` / `--until` / `--timeout` and their JSON
fields (0076); `snapshot --transcript`, `snapshot --unwrap`, and the four additive
ScreenState keys `soft_wrap`, `truncated`, `truncated_reason`, `title` (0077).

ACCEPTANCE: ADR-0071 either enumerates each of these as inside the frozen surface,
or explicitly carves them out with a stated reason and a deadline. No agent verb
should be discovered post-freeze.
notes:
WAVE-2 UPDATE. The already-shipped-but-unnamed list GREW. Everything below is in the tree now, uncommitted, and none of it is named by ADR-0071.

NEWLY SHIPPED CLI SURFACE:
- phux agent wait, with --until repeatable over idle, working, blocked and done, --timeout in SECS, --json, and an optional TARGET.
- phux agent send-keys, with --expect-agent, --expect-kind and --json.
- phux snapshot --tail with an optional N and phux snapshot --unwrap, plus an extended conflicts list on --rendered.
- phux wait --regex, --tail and --output-only, plus reworded --until and --idle help.

NEWLY SHIPPED JSON DOCUMENTS:

- The agent send-keys --json result, schema_version 1, with terminal, agent, keys and verified.
- Four ADDITIVE keys on ScreenState: soft_wrap with lines and scrollback, truncated, truncated_reason and title. schema_version deliberately STAYS 3, and the operative consumer rule is to probe for the presence of soft_wrap rather than the version, because an older server would not have moved the version either.

NEWLY SHIPPED ERROR CODES, and these are a contract problem in themselves: no_agent_record at exit 2, agent_departed at exit 1, agent_mismatch at exit 2 and invalid_key_spec at exit 2. They live in PRIVATE mod codes blocks inside crates/phux/src/commands/agent/wait.rs and send_keys.rs, NOT in crates/phux/src/commands/json_err.rs. docs/consumers/agents.md 5.3 previously claimed a single-file closed vocabulary and that claim had to be narrowed rather than restated. Folding them in is filed separately.

TWO EXIT-CODE SEMANTICS DECISIONS THAT ARE NOW PART OF THE FROZEN SURFACE:
- Exit 3 means phux could not answer the question, explicitly NOT retry. ADR-0075 and the revised ADR-0076 now agree on this reading and docs/consumers/agents.md says it. It contradicts the older reading in that same table and the correction shipped in wave 2.
- agent wait and agent send-keys use the SHARED resolver, so they keep exit 1 on a partial-fleet miss carrying partial_view in error.code, rather than the exit 3 the agent verb family uses. Verified against resolve_target. That carve-out is now documented and is part of the surface.

DEADLINE PRESSURE IS REAL AND HAS GROWN. Every wave-2 item above shipped BEFORE this carve-out was written, which is the failure mode this bead exists to prevent, happening. See also the separate R3 bead on splitting the phux_agent MCP action multiplexer before its argument union freezes.

title: Ratify ADR-0075/0076/0077/0078 as one agent-surface batch, with one owner for the overlaps
description:
ADR/0075-agent-name-addressing.md, ADR/0076-agent-prompt-and-lifecycle-wait.md and
ADR/0077-agent-read-surface.md were written in one run by three agents who did not
read each other. All three are Status: Proposed. They all add to the same `agent`
verb surface, and each names the others as an unresolved conflict. One owner has to
accept or reject them as a batch, because the overlaps are real:

- 0075 point 7 constrains input-delivering verbs against a `%name` target
  ("re-verify the pane still hosts the agent before writing bytes"); 0076 point 4
  specifies the same rule for `agent prompt` in different words. One owner, one
  wording, one place.
- 0075 conflict 2: it deliberately does NOT narrow docs/spec/L3.md 3.7's record
  `name` ("REQUIRED, non-empty", no charset), so `%`-addressability is a strictly
  smaller set than valid records. Narrowing the spec instead is a normative change
  plus a docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md entry, and it invalidates display names like
  "Claude Code". Decide which.
- 0076 conflict 2: `phux send-keys host/@N` works via ROUTE_INPUT relay but
  `agent prompt host/@N` cannot (APPLY_INPUT is local-only, ADR-0053). Accept the
  documented hole in ADR-0066's host namespace, or schedule federated acknowledged
  input (bead phux-2en already exists for that).
- 0076 conflict 3: `phux wait` already exists with Condition::{Contains, Idle}.
  `phux agent wait` is a second wait verb with a different data source. Confirm the
  split against ADR-0065's one-grammar principle, or fold it into
  `phux wait --until-agent-state`.
- 0077 conflict 1: the alternate-screen harvest contradicts docs/spec/L1.md 6.1's
  normative "no side effects" claim for GET_SCREEN. Accepting 0077 commits to a
  normative spec change.
- 0077 conflict 3: ADR-0046 point 8 (an explicit SET_METADATA outranks the
  detector) vs. 0077's idle gate for the harvest. 0077 chose to read the published
  record; confirm that over gating on the detector's own derivation.
- 0077 conflict 6: exit code for a refused harvest. crates/phux/src/exit_codes.rs
  defines EXIT_PARTIAL_VIEW = 3 narrowly as "resolved against a partial view of the
  fleet"; 0077 chose 2 (EXIT_USAGE, "or the server refused the request"). Confirm.

ACCEPTANCE: each ADR moves to Accepted or Rejected with the conflicts above
resolved in the text; ADR/README.md index rows updated (they were hand-added and
already carry curated annotations); the combined CLI delta handed to the ADR-0071
carve-out bead.
design:
RATIFICATION DECISIONS 2026-08-17 (autonomous run, evidence-backed). SPLIT THE BATCH THREE WAYS — do not ratify as one. Batching 0078 with the rest repeats exactly the mistake wave 2 corrected when it split 0078 out of 0077.

FIRST, A CORRECTION: ADR-0077 is ALREADY Accepted (ADR/0077:15). This is a three-ADR decision, not four. A 482-line ratification brief already exists at ADR/RATIFICATION-BRIEF-agent-surface.md.

VERDICTS
- ADR-0077: already Accepted, no action.
- ADR-0075: ACCEPT with three edits. It is a COMMITMENT TO BUILD, not a record of shipped behaviour — %name parses and is fully unit-tested, then resolves to nothing (selector.rs:317-319 returns Vec::new() with the comment 'Never let %name reach pick_target_pane'); resolve_agent, resolve_agent_for_input, AgentIndex and AgentResolveError have ZERO production callers and are not re-exported.
- ADR-0076: ACCEPT with two corrections. Its subject matter is entirely shipped and already carved into ADR-0071 point 6.
- ADR-0078: DEFER, leave Proposed.

CONFLICT 1 (duplicated re-verify rule) — KEEP THE SPLIT, do not merge. They stopped being duplicates in wave 2: 0075 point 5 is a SAFETY GATE reading the level (refuse when kind present and state unknown); 0076 point 4 is an IDENTITY COMPARISON (the shipped --expect-agent/--expect-kind check). The doctrine is already single-sourced and normative in docs/spec/L3.md 3.7 ('a safety gate MAY read the level, a completion gate MUST require an observed transition'). 0076 point 4 ALREADY cites 0075 point 5 by name and already states the circularity — the bead's open item 1 is stale. Merging would destroy the distinction that a safety gate may fire on a corpse while an identity comparison may not. EDITS: name the concrete verb set (agent send-keys, agent prompt, agent answer) instead of 'any ADR-0053 acknowledged-batch verb'; and ADD A SENTENCE saying the guard has no caller, because as written point 5 reads as a description of behaviour when it is a commitment.

CONFLICT 2 (name charset) — OPTION A, keep two grammars. Shipped-manifest evidence is decisive but NOT in the assumed direction: all five manifests (claude/codex/opencode/pi/omp) use bare lowercase single-word names that all satisfy the addressable grammar, so option B breaks no manifest — BUT every one of those names EQUALS ITS OWN KIND, which is exactly what 0075 point 4 refuses as AgentResolveError::KindConstant, and the Claude shim writes that shape explicitly (shim.rs:407 --name claude --kind claude). CONSEQUENCE: phux's own flagship integration yields ZERO %-addressable panes; %name is inert until a human runs 'phux agent set @N --name <chosen>'. Option B was rejected because it costs a THIRD thing nobody priced: a new refusal on 'phux agent set --name' (record.rs:38-41 validates non-empty-after-trim and nothing else), which is stable CLI surface owed a deprecations.rs cycle, spent immediately before the ADR-0071 freeze, to buy tidiness. SPEND THE DIFFERENCE ON THE ERROR MESSAGE instead: before reporting Unknown, scan for a live record differing only in excluded characters and name it. That is a message, not a field, so it adds nothing to the frozen document surface. ALSO write into point 7(a) that the Claude integration produces zero addressable panes. DEFECT TO FOLD IN: the addressable grammar is stated THREE times unsynchronized — selector.rs:237 (bound via AGENT_NAME_MAX_LEN:222), start.rs:214 (bound HARDCODED as 32), and the display string NAME_GRAMMAR at start.rs:124.

CONFLICT 3 (federation hole) — OPTION A, accept, but WIDEN the statement. The premise is one wave stale: as of 9b61a3c5 both verbs give a clean typed refusal. 'agent prompt host/@N' exits 2 with code satellite_target and a remedy, refused CLIENT-SIDE before a socket opens (agent_prompt.rs:847-851; test deliberately passes a nonexistent socket to prove it). 'agent wait host/@N' likewise (wait.rs:86-101). The brief's 'dangerous one' finding is stale. Option B rejected: phux-2en is P3/post-1.0/other-owner, and ADR-0053 point 7 already declined federated acknowledged input because it needs destination capability negotiation, destination-owned dedupe and server_id incarnation semantics across the hop — buying uniformity costs the idempotency guarantee that is the verb's entire point. THE FIX: 0076 point 1 states the narrow version; make it state the WIDE one — the hole is the whole agent surface, not one verb. send-keys/paste/signal/run reach host/@N; agent prompt/wait/show/explain/set/clear/list and %name are hub-local by construction. Filed separately: an e2e test for both verbs against a real relay, plus a satellite guard on handle_get_metadata (client.rs:2059 still silently returns value:None where handle_subscribe_metadata gained refuse_satellite_metadata_scope), so the lie is unreachable even if a CLI guard is removed.

CONFLICT 4 (two wait verbs) — KEEP THE SPLIT. ADR-0065 does not ask for folding: all seven of its decision points are about FLAG SPELLING, none about verb count, and its own remedy for a collision is a disambiguating noun, which 'agent' is. The verbs differ on every axis a caller branches on: data source (GET_SCREEN poll vs SUBSCRIBE_METADATA push + poll floor), condition domain (Contains/Matches/Idle vs closed idle|working|blocked|done), PREDICATE (level match vs observed-transition-only via EdgeTracker, which L3.md 3.7 REQUIRES of a completion gate and 13 tests pin), and exit codes. Shared code is ONE constant. DECISIVE on phux-w7z2.20: that bead's verdict is no-wire-change for 'agent wait --any', implemented as EdgeTracker becoming HashMap<TerminalId,EdgeTracker> — a fan-out of the edge tracker, which has NO analogue in phux wait. Folding would ACTIVELY COMPLICATE --any. Folding also costs a deprecation cycle on shipped surface immediately before the freeze and would break ADR-0071 point 7(b)'s ten-tool MCP freeze, which names phux_agent_wait. CORRECTIONS OWED TO 0076: --timeout is SECS not MS (agent/mod.rs:149-152, Duration::from_secs; ADR-0071 point 6 already says SECS, so the ADR is the wrong one). AND CLOSE bead item 3: the 'no shipped done writer' objection is DEAD — ADR-0085 (Accepted 2026-08-14) shipped REPORT_AGENT_STATE with a ServerFeature bit and the report-state verb, so done has a real producer. KEEP done in the default --until set.

CONFLICT 5 (GET_SCREEN side effects) — DEFER 0078, and there is NO live contradiction today. Wave 2 moved the harvest out of 0077 into 0078; 0077 as it stands makes no spec claim, no wire change and no PTY write, and request_transcript appears NOWHERE in crates/ or docs/ — only in 0078's prose. L1.md 6.1's 'no side effects' is CURRENTLY TRUE. Accepting 0078 commits to a FUTURE normative change (three sentences, one CHANGELOG row, no PROTOCOL_VERSION bump since the feature bit is additive per ADR-0061). A separate HARVEST_TRANSCRIPT verb would preserve the sentence but is REJECTED per 0078's own Alternatives: no retry identity, result is a screen not a receipt, and it needs its own role policy, capability bit, relay arm and CLI verb — a flag plus a PRIMARY clause buys the identical guarantee for one line. DEFER FOR THREE REASONS: (1) 0078's own Context says to capture live viewports before accepting, and that is UNDISCHARGED — rows per wheel notch, repaint settle time, merge seam; ADR-0046's Tradeoffs record what writing against an imagined TUI cost last time. (2) Point 6's freeze mechanism is NEW mechanism, not the reuse it claims: skip_state_update is a per-rule boolean on a main-screen text rule (rules.rs:190, claude.toml:174); there is no alternate-screen bit and no actor-assertable duration-scoped freeze. That belongs in the wording and in the 1760-line estimate. (3) NOTHING depends on it — 0077 says so at :35-36. When accepted, make the spec amendment IN THE PR THAT SHIPS THE FIRST HARVESTING CODE so the spec never describes behaviour the server lacks.

CONFLICT 6(a) (ADR-0046 point 8 vs the idle gate) — CONFIRM 0077/0078's choice: read the published record, do not gate on the detector's own derivation. L3.md 3.7, made normative in wave 2, expressly settles it and names this exact case: a safety gate MAY read the level, and 'a crashed or unidentified pane reading as do-not-disturb errs in the conservative direction'. Residual: a consumer can declare idle on a busy agent and unlock a harvest. THERE IS NO STRUCTURAL FIX — 3.7 states a consumer 'neither can nor needs to distinguish' declared from derived; the record carries no provenance field and minting one adds a field to a document ADR-0071 freezes. Accept it rather than inventing provenance. ADR-0085 narrowed the hazard anyway: hook evidence now feeds the DETECTOR rather than declaring metadata state.

CONFLICT 6(b) (exit code for a refused harvest) — OVERTURN BOTH 2 AND 3; the answer is EXIT 0 with a named reason on the payload. 3 is wrong on meaning: no satellite is involved and 3's published contract is 'retry is correct once the link is back', but of 0078 point 4's reasons only agent_not_idle is retryable — no_detector, not_local and a missing capability bit are PERMANENT. 2 is wrong on mechanism AND breaks an existing contract: ADR-0065 point 4 fixes the JSON error shape as one line on stderr WITH STDOUT EMPTY, but a refused harvest still produced a perfectly good viewport read — exiting 2 forces discarding it or emitting a success payload alongside a non-zero exit; and 'snapshot --transcript' on an ordinary main-screen pane would exit 2, making every '|| handle_error' treat a good read as failure. Precedent for exit 0: 0077 point 4's truncated/truncated_reason. NAME THE COST in the ADR: a script that asked for a transcript and got none now succeeds silently, so callers must branch on transcript.status — a genuinely new exit-code semantic with no precedent in exit_codes.rs. Carve it into ADR-0071 point 6 so it cannot be discovered post-freeze.

CLI/JSON DELTA OWED IF 0075 RATIFIES (0076 owes NOTHING but the SECS correction): %<agent-name> as a TARGET token on every targeted verb AND the MCP tools' target argument (note resolve_one is duplicated byte-identically at phux-mcp/src/tools.rs:743 and ask_tool.rs:63 — a migration must touch both); the grammar as a parse-time refusal exit 2; four refusals with statuses (Unknown->1, Ambiguous->2, KindConstant->2, Withdrawn->2, PartialIndex->3); error codes in commands::json_err::codes for each (none exists today; ADR-0071 point 7(a) requires them); AND A COLLISION ADR-0071 POINT 6 MUST RESOLVE IN THE SAME EDIT — point 6 says agent wait/send-keys return 1 with partial_view in error.code, but %name's partial-index refusal is 3, and the two rules meet on 'phux agent send-keys %foo'. DECISION: 3 wins for %name and point 6 is amended to say so — a partial FLEET is a server-side gap the client infers; a partial INDEX is the client knowing it did not finish looking, and %name is the one selector whose entire contract is singularity. PRECONDITION, not a delta: fetch_agent_index (agent/record.rs:216-219) returns a bare HashMap and swallows every transport failure into silent truncation via three early returns, so the exit-3 refusal HAS NO SOURCE OF TRUTH TODAY; it must return AgentIndex with a real completeness bit, and three production callers take the raw map.

TWO ITEMS STILL NEEDING A CALL: (i) whether 0075 point 5's guard covers attach and kill — my read is NO: attach writes no bytes, and refusing to kill a pane whose record was withdrawn strands the panes a user most wants gone. (ii) the ~150-line convention overrun (0076 is 224 lines, 0078 is 214); no CI gate enforces it and CONVENTIONS.md prescribes a companion page under docs/architecture/.

The gate is only meaningful for at-N targets, and 0076 still does not cite 0075. One of the two must own it.

title: agent-to-agent orchestration: herdr parity and beyond
description:
Bring phux's agent-to-agent orchestration surface to herdr parity and past it:
addressable agent names, acknowledged prompting, event-driven waiting, a read
surface that survives soft wrap and the alternate screen, and the detection-layer
fixes an audit against herdr surfaced.

What already landed this run (uncommitted in the worktree at the time of filing,
so it is context, not work):

- `phux watch` now carries `agent_state` lines. crates/phux-client/src/watch.rs
  subscribes to SUBSCRIBE_METADATA on `phux.agent/v1` alongside SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS;
  crates/phux/src/commands/watch.rs renders them. No wire change.
- The server-side fanout was relaxed so an L3 metadata subscriber no longer has
  to be attached (ClientTable::broadcast_metadata_changed falls back to a
  captured `metadata_mailboxes` entry). See the review bead under this epic.
- `phux agent explain --file PATH --kind KIND` — offline manifest explainer
  (crates/phux-server/src/agent_explain.rs, crates/phux/src/commands/agent/offline.rs).
- Three proposed ADRs: 0075 (agent-name addressing), 0076 (prompt + lifecycle
  wait), 0077 (agent read surface). All Status: Proposed, none implemented.
- `nix develop -c just ci` was green at the end of the run. Nothing was left
  failing; every bead here is new work, not breakage.

SCHEDULING CONSTRAINT (real, not a nicety): ADR-0071 is Proposed and freezes the
CLI JSON surface for 1.0. Every verb and JSON document under this epic must land
BEFORE that freeze or be explicitly carved into it. That already applies to two
SHIPPED things ADR-0071 does not name: the AgentExplainJson document and the
`agent_state` watch event name. See the ADR-0071 carve-out bead.

Source material: the three ADRs in ADR/, and a read-only detection-parity audit
against herdr (10 ranked findings; its top items are filed individually here,
including the two correctness findings, which are NOT polish).
notes:
WAVE-2 STATUS, 2026-08-08. Everything below is UNCOMMITTED in the worktree. Verified green in that state: cargo nextest run --workspace 3246 of 3246 passed with 72 skipped, just docs-check 142 files 0 violations, refdocs::tests::generated_reference_docs_match_the_tree PASS, fmt and clippy -D warnings clean, cargo deny clean.

CLOSED THIS WAVE: phux-w7z2.8 read surface, phux-w7z2.9 wait soft-wrap bug plus --regex, phux-w7z2.4 agent wait, phux-w7z2.7 agent send-keys. Two carry recorded deviations - agent wait has NO level fast path, and agent send-keys shipped on ROUTE_INPUT rather than APPLY_INPUT. Read their close reasons before assuming the ADRs describe the code.

THE RULING THAT GOVERNED THE WAVE, now normative in docs/spec/L3.md 3.7 with a 0.7.0-draft.2 CHANGELOG row and NO PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. The five shipped manifests contain exactly ten state-bearing rules - five working, five blocked - and ZERO idle and ZERO done. idle is the fail-safe fallthrough at agent_detect/mod.rs:424-428 and is equally true of a finished agent, a half-painted TUI, a crashed agent and a pane running less. So state is read two ways depending on the shape of the gate. A LEVEL asserts only that no state-bearing rule currently matches - absence of contrary evidence. An EDGE asserts that whatever was asserting the old value stopped. SAFETY gates take the level: do not scroll a repainting screen, do not write into a pane whose occupant may have changed. COMPLETION gates take the edge: agent wait and prompt --wait must be satisfied only by an observed transition, never by a level read, which is what stops a wait returning success on a corpse. A quiescent open-enum value was CONSIDERED AND REJECTED - it would have no producer, because the only thing that could emit it is a positive idle rule in a manifest, and none can be honestly authored until real viewports are captured. Do not introduce it.

ADR-0071 SCHEDULING CONSTRAINT, RESTATED AND NOW URGENT. ADR-0071 is Status Proposed and freezes the CLI JSON surface AND the MCP tool names and arguments for 1.0. Wave 2 shipped four CLI surface changes, three JSON documents and four error codes BEFORE the carve-out was written - which is the failure this epic flagged from the start, happening. Every verb and JSON document under this epic must land before that freeze or be explicitly carved into it. Two beads own that and both are P1: phux-w7z2.2 for the CLI and JSON surface, and phux-w7z2.30 for splitting the phux_agent MCP action multiplexer before its argument union freezes around a shape designed for five read verbs. Neither is optional and neither is reversible after 1.0.

FOUR ADRs NOW, NOT THREE. ADR-0077 was split - it keeps the additive read decisions and the alternate-screen harvest moved to the NEW ADR/0078-alternate-screen-history.md. ALL FOUR ARE STILL Status Proposed. Nothing was ratified. phux-w7z2.1 owns all four.

title: Initialize login environment for service-spawned panes
description: A server installed with 'phux service install' runs under launchd's minimal PATH. New panes spawn the configured shell as a plain interactive shell rather than a login shell, so macOS profile initialization never runs. Users get their normal prompt and .zshrc but commands installed through Homebrew or Nix profiles are absent (for example, nvim and brew both report command not found). Environment markers such as NIX_PROFILES may still be inherited, making common profile guards incorrectly believe initialization already happened.
design: Define and document service-backed pane environment semantics. Prefer invoking the user's shell in the platform-correct login mode or another shell-native initialization path rather than baking the installer's transient PATH into the service unit. Preserve explicit defaults.shell behavior and avoid assuming zsh. The solution must cover launchd and systemd without double-sourcing profiles in ordinary terminal-launched servers.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A launchd server started with only the macOS default service PATH spawns a pane that receives the user's normal login PATH. 2. Homebrew and Nix profile commands are discoverable in service-backed panes when their standard profile initialization provides them. 3. bash, zsh, fish, explicit defaults.shell, and fallback /bin/sh behavior are defined and tested. 4. Service installation never captures a transient nix develop/direnv PATH. 5. An end-to-end regression starts the service under a minimal environment and proves a profile-provided command resolves. 6. Existing direct/server-in-terminal pane startup remains regression-free.
close_reason: Detection is knowledge not heuristic: phux service install stamps PHUX_SERVICE_MANAGED=1 into both the launchd plist and the systemd unit, and phux server reads it at startup. Login invocation per shell: bash/zsh/sh take -l, fish takes --login, unrecognized defaults.shell gets no flag (deliberate: an unknown program's flag semantics are unknown, and a fatal exec is worse than an unsourced profile). All 6 acceptance criteria satisfied. Criterion 4 was already correct -- resolve_plan never reads PATH -- and is now locked in by a test that reads the test process's own ambient nix develop PATH and asserts it appears in neither unit. Criterion 5/6 proven by a real e2e that runs the compiled binary with env_clear plus a launchd-shaped minimal PATH against a real profile fixture and a real PTY; only the init system itself is simulated. ADR-0073 records the decision.

title: [epic] Decompose ServerState: 51 fields into 8 cohesive concerns
description:
ServerState carries 51 fields and 61 methods across ~1450 production lines in state/mod.rs + state/registry.rs. Roughly eleven unrelated concerns share one struct behind one mutex: wire ID interning, immutable boot config, terminal lifecycle, clients, sessions, leases, metadata, agents, federation, upgrade, attach-seeding.

This is a legibility problem, not a correctness or performance one. The runtime is current-thread and the mutex is uncontended by construction (see the clippy::arc_with_non_send_sync allow in state/mod.rs). SharedState's 4-method API (new/lock/with/with_mut) and the 20 lock sites across 5 files are the GOOD part and must survive unchanged.

The cost of the status quo is that adding a 52nd field is free, and no subsystem boundary is expressed in the type system.

Also: state/registry.rs is 69KB containing a single 'impl ServerState' block and no type named Registry. The filename describes something that does not exist.
acceptance_criteria: ServerState holds 8 named sub-structs instead of 51 flat fields. SharedState's public API is byte-identical. just ci green at every phase boundary. No behavior change.
close_reason: 7/7 children complete and the acceptance criterion is met on the current tree: ServerState is 11 fields, 10 of them named sub-structs (SessionTable, ClientTable, TerminalTable, LeaseTable, IdSpace, MetadataStore, AgentState, ServerConfig, HubState, Lifecycle) plus hook_dispatcher, down from 51 flat fields. state/registry.rs is gone, replaced by 29 focused modules under state/. Verified 2026-08-07; the epic was left open after 294a7e6c 'finish the ServerState decomposition' landed.

title: Add first-class self-update with live server handoff
description: Today, 'phux upgrade' only asks a running server to re-exec whatever binary is already on disk. It does not discover, download, verify, or install a newer Phux release, leaving users to understand Homebrew, direct release archives, NixOS, and the subsequent live-server handoff themselves. Add a first-class update workflow that detects the installation source, checks available versions, safely updates supported mutable installs, and invokes the existing graceful upgrade so panes survive. Package-managed or immutable installations must fail safely with an exact actionable native update command rather than attempting to mutate their store.
design: Prefer a user-facing 'phux update' command, retaining 'phux upgrade' as the low-level live-server re-exec primitive. Verify release checksums before an atomic binary replacement. Detect direct-release, Homebrew, Cargo, Nix/NixOS, and unsupported installs; either perform the safe update or print/optionally execute the correct package-manager path. Support check-only, dry-run, explicit version/channel, non-interactive output, and clear rollback/error behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 1. One documented command checks current versus latest Phux and identifies the install source. 2. Direct release installs download the matching platform archive, verify the published checksum, atomically replace binaries, and preserve permissions. 3. A running local server is handed off through the existing graceful upgrade path without losing live panes. 4. Homebrew/Cargo/package-managed installs use or print the correct native update path. 5. Nix/NixOS and other immutable-store installs are never mutated and receive an exact actionable rebuild/update instruction. 6. Check-only, dry-run, explicit-version, machine-readable output, failure, and rollback paths have tests. 7. Documentation covers macOS, Linux, Homebrew, direct archives, and NixOS.
close_reason: phux update shipped: --check, --dry-run, --version, --json, --rollback, --no-restart. Install-source detection from the symlink-resolved current_exe as a pure testable function, most-specific-first: Nix store (NixOS vs profile), Homebrew (Cellar component or prefix), Cargo bin, direct-release allowlist, unknown. Only direct-release is mutable; unknown is refused with a hint rather than best-effort overwritten. Artifact naming and the sha256 sidecar format were read out of release.yml, not assumed; the digest is computed in-process and compared BEFORE tar is invoked, with the sidecar filename cross-checked so crossed assets are caught, then a tar member allowlist and an extracted-tree revalidation. Staging happens inside the target bin dir so rename(2) is atomic; mode is copied from the existing binary, which also strips any setuid the tarball carried; phux-mcp and phux are replaced in an order that rolls back on partial failure. Rollback keeps one generation as plain files plus a JSON manifest, deliberately recoverable with mv if you downgrade past the verb. Priorities 1-5 done; --channel (6) CUT and the flag does not exist, since only stable releases are published and adding it later is additive. One dependency, sha2, already in the workspace: zero new Cargo.lock rows. ADR-0074 records the trust boundary honestly -- the sidecar shares a host and TLS channel with the archive, so it catches truncation, corruption, crossed assets and a mid-flight proxy but NOT a compromised release host; signing is named as the successor.

title: Adopt a live server into service supervision without killing panes
description:
## Problem

Running `phux service install` while an unsupervised Phux server already owns the configured Unix socket creates a restart loop: the launchd/systemd process exits because the socket is live, while stopping the existing server would kill every pane and its in-flight shells, agents, and subagents. This occurred with a long-lived server containing active OMP sessions when enabling persistent service supervision and new QUIC/WebSocket listeners.

A user should be able to move a live Phux server under service supervision without losing terminal processes, rather than waiting for all work to finish or accepting that conversation resume cannot restore killed subprocesses.

## Desired behavior

Provide an explicit adoption/handoff path, potentially `phux service install --adopt`, that transitions a running unsupervised server to the native service manager while preserving live sessions and pane processes. The transition must also reconcile listener configuration instead of leaving the old server on stale transports.
design: launchd and systemd generally cannot adopt an arbitrary existing PID. Treat this as a server-to-server handoff, not process reparenting: start the supervised replacement, transfer or re-adopt live PTY/session file descriptors and state using the existing graceful-upgrade machinery where possible, atomically transfer socket/listener ownership, then retire the old server. Clients may briefly reconnect but pane process identities and execution must survive. If a platform cannot support safe adoption, detect that before installing a restart-looping unit and print a precise recovery path.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Installing service supervision over a live unsupervised server does not kill pane processes or their descendants. 2. The resulting server is owned and restart-managed by launchd on macOS and systemd --user on Linux. 3. Existing attached clients reconnect or receive a clear transient handoff, while detached sessions remain intact. 4. Unix socket and requested QUIC/WebSocket listeners transfer atomically without a prolonged bind conflict. 5. Pane child PIDs and observable terminal contents survive an integration test across handoff. 6. A failed or unsupported handoff leaves the original server running and does not install a crash-looping service.
notes:
SCOPING (2026-08-11, from a code audit): the design note's 'reuse the graceful-upgrade machinery' direction is sound but requires NET-NEW MECHANISM, not reuse. Four confirmed blockers:

1. THE ONLY FD TRANSPORT IS execve INHERITANCE. There is no SCM_RIGHTS anywhere in the codebase -- grep for SCM_RIGHTS|sendmsg|recvmsg|ScmRights|send_fd|pass_fd across all crates returns zero hits. blob.listener_fd and PaneBlob::master_fd are RAW INTEGERS meaningful only inside the exec'd image's own fd table. A process launchd/systemd spawned independently has an unrelated fd table; the blob is literally uninterpretable to it.

2. NO SOCKET ACTIVATION. render_launchd_plist emits no Sockets key; there is no LISTEN_FDS handling. The only mentions of 'socket activation' in the tree are prose analogies.

3. THE BLOB NEVER CROSSES THE WIRE, BY EXPLICIT DESIGN. Command::Upgrade is documented as 'A bare trigger -- the handoff state blob is built and passed entirely server-side (it never crosses the wire)' (phux-protocol/src/wire/frame.rs:1601-1608).

4. execve PRESERVES PROCESS IDENTITY AND PARENT, which is exactly the problem this bead names. The trigger IS externally requestable (phux upgrade sends Command::Upgrade), but the DESTINATION is hardcoded to std::env::current_exe() (runtime/upgrade.rs:106). An external process can say 're-exec yourself'; it cannot say 'hand off to me'. After the re-exec it is still the same PID with the same parent, so launchd/systemd still does not own it.

TWO FURTHER GAPS blocking this bead's stated acceptance criteria:
- LISTENER CONFIG CANNOT CHANGE ACROSS THE HANDOFF. resume_args (runtime/upgrade.rs:140-177) reconstructs argv from RuntimeFlags captured at the OLD server's startup, and Command::Upgrade carries no payload. There is no way to request 'upgrade AND now also serve --quic 0.0.0.0:8788'. An adopted server would come back on the old transports.
- ENVIRONMENT DOES NOT SUBSTITUTE. UpgradePlan::exec uses std::process::Command, which inherits the current environment, so a re-exec of an unsupervised server keeps the unsupervised env -- it would NOT pick up the unit's PHUX_WS_TOKENS / PHUX_WS_TLS_* / PHUX_SERVICE_MANAGED. Note login_shell is derived from PHUX_SERVICE_MANAGED (commands/server.rs:200), so an 'adopted' server would still spawn non-login panes.

MINIMUM MISSING PIECES: (a) an fd-passing channel (SCM_RIGHTS over the UDS, or socket activation), (b) a handoff REQUEST verb with a target, (c) a parameterized upgrade command so listener config can change, (d) an env-substitution story. Only (a) has any partial analogue today, and it is the execve path -- precisely the one that cannot cross process boundaries.

RECOMMENDATION: do phux-67wg (refuse to install over a live server, with a precise recovery message) first. It removes the user-facing damage cheaply. This bead is a multi-week design item and should get an ADR before any code.
close_reason: Shipped as phux service install --adopt on army/w3-service-adopt (commit f30644cb), with ADR-0088. Numbered 0086 at first, renumbered after army/w3-render-newtype minted 0086 and army/w3-chrome-config 0087 concurrently in the same wave (see phux-254o). Adoption transfers the supervision, not the process: no supervisor can restart-manage a pid it did not start, so the unit is armed rather than loaded and the auto-spawn path completes the hand-over. ACs 1, 4 and 6 met; ACs 2, 3 and 5 (live pane transfer between two processes) remain blocked on an SCM_RIGHTS channel and are recorded as post-1.0 in ADR-0088.

title: Local dev shell cannot build libghostty since the Zig 0.16 re-pin: nmedit missing from nix apple-sdk
description: Since 40fcf5e0 (Zig 0.16 + libghostty re-pin to 98ad1db), the vendored build runs ghostty-src/src/build/libsystem_override.sh which invokes nmedit. Inside nix develop, DEVELOPER_DIR=/nix/store/...-apple-sdk-14.4 and SDKROOT point at the nix SDK, whose toolchain lacks nmedit, so the /usr/bin/nmedit shim fails with "error: tool 'nmedit' not found" and every local cargo build of the workspace fails on macOS. GitHub CI passes (runner has full Xcode active). Reproduced 2026-08-02 in a fresh worktree; unsetting DEVELOPER_DIR/SDKROOT inside the shell and clearing the sys-crate build dir do not clear it (zig build plan re-resolves the nix SDK). Fix candidates: add an nmedit-bearing toolchain to the dev shell PATH ahead of the shim, patch libsystem_override.sh via the -sys crate, or upstream a fallback to llvm-objcopy. Until fixed, local heavy gates on macOS are degraded; branch verification leans on the required GitHub checks.
notes: WORKAROUND FOUND (wave-10 implementer, 2026-08-02): exporting DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer inside nix develop makes the libghostty zig build succeed — full Xcode's toolchain carries nmedit, overriding the nix apple-sdk's DEVELOPER_DIR. Candidate permanent fix: have the dev shell prefer the host Xcode DEVELOPER_DIR when present, or patch libsystem_override.sh.
close_reason: 4xdh: flake.nix now prefers a host Xcode whose toolchain actually contains nmedit (checked, not assumed), falling back to nix's DEVELOPER_DIR with a loud actionable warning. Root cause pinned down precisely: the nix apple-sdk ships an nmedit specification plist but not the binary, and a CLT-only DEVELOPER_DIR is rejected because zig then reports DarwinSdkNotFound. t2g: the shim fix landed in d2946e3f and was never closed; nothing pinned it, so added a pty-driven behavioral test running the rendered wrapper against fake phux and claude binaries across all three paths -- clean exit, mid-session crash (status propagates, no relaunch), and pre-launch failure (direct fallback exactly once).

Overriding inside the dev shell makes the full build green on macOS: nix develop -c bash -c 'DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer cargo check -p phux'. CLT alone is NOT enough (zig reports DarwinSdkNotFound); full Xcode works. zig 0.15 (ambient) is refused by vendored ghostty (needs 0.16), so the override inside the 0.16 shell is the working combination.

help text; new unit test pins the pruned tree to the visible half of the
parser. After the fix the scripted loop is CLEAN for zsh and bash:

title: PTY writer dies permanently on any io error, and its Drop injects newline+VEOF into the pane
description: spawn.rs:401-415 breaks the writer loop on ANY io::Error with no errno discrimination, no retry, no partial-write accounting. Compounding: the receiver drops (discarding up to 64 queued requests), nothing ever restarts the thread (writer_thread is only taken in shutdown_pty), and self.pty_tx stays Some so every later send hits TrySendError::Closed and is discarded at debug! level while ROUTE_INPUT keeps acking Ok -- pane looks alive, all input goes nowhere. Additionally portable-pty's Drop for UnixMasterWriter writes newline + VEOF into the master on thread exit (unix.rs:392-405), which in canonical mode commits a truncated partial line as if complete. EIO asymmetry is the realistic trigger: portable-pty maps EIO to EOF on the read half (unix.rs:94-97) but not the write half (unix.rs:407-412). Split out of phux-6b6t.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #318 (4bbe113e). Writer now classifies errno: EIO/EPIPE are routine child teardown, EINTR/EAGAIN retry under a bounded budget, only unexpected errnos end the loop and they log the partial-write count. write_all replaced by a resuming loop. portable-pty's VEOF-injecting Drop now fires on clean shutdown only (ManuallyDrop), so a failed write can no longer commit a truncated line to a canonical-mode shell. Drop sites raised to warn!/error!.

title: phux config reload silently resets status.position to bottom
description: reload.rs:91 (phux-client/src/attach/reload.rs): StatusBarPainter::new(bar, Position::default()) — the reload path hardcodes default position while the startup path uses cfg.status.position (driver.rs:4245). A user with position = "top" who runs phux config reload gets the bar jumping to bottom, silently, unrecoverable without detach/re-attach. tui.md:1124-1126 enumerates reload's documented non-coverage; status.position is not on that list, so this is a bug, not a limit.
design:
---

**Design resolution (stream A, 2026-08-01).** Verified: reload.rs:88 constructs StatusBarPainter::new(bar, Position::default()) while startup uses cfg.status.position.into() (driver.rs:4244-4246). title: [umbrella] Log discoverability: one canonical server log, phux logs verb, doctor path reporting
description:
Three log files exist; no command or doc ever prints any of their paths:

- Auto-spawned server: <socket_dir>/phux-server.log (server.rs:302-314) — in zero docs, printed by nothing.
- Service-installed server: $XDG_STATE_HOME/phux/server.log (service.rs:367,705). `phux service logs` tails only THIS file, so it errors for every auto-spawn user.
- Client: $XDG_STATE_HOME/phux/client-<pid>.log (phux-server/src/telemetry.rs:210-223); the doc comment admits "Public so a future phux subcommand can report the path" — no caller exists. Client panics are durable but unreachable.

docs/operations.md:80-84 concedes: no server status, no logs discovery verb. docs/architecture/process-model.md:24-30 flatly contradicts tui.md:558-563 about whether the state dir even exists (tui.md is right; process-model.md is stale).

Fix: (a) a `phux logs` verb (or `phux doctor --logs` section) that names every live log path and which process writes it; (b) doctor gains a check/section reporting log + state paths (doctor.rs:104-109 currently runs four checks, none mention logs); (c) every fatal client/attach error prints where the log went; (d) reconcile the two server log locations or teach service logs about both; (e) surface phux doctor in README.md and docs/QUICKSTART.md — it currently appears only in tui.md (grep-verified).
design: DESIGN RESOLUTION (stream C, 2026-08-01). Resolved: (1) canonical server log is $XDG_STATE_HOME/phux/server.log for BOTH spawn paths — auto-spawn (currently <socket_dir>/phux-server.log, server.rs:305-314) moves to the file the service unit already uses (service.rs:367, 705), via a single phux_server::telemetry::server_log_path() helper so service logs / phux logs / doctor can never disagree; startup line gains pid+version+socket. (2) phux logs is a new top-level verb: bare invocation prints the path inventory, --server/--client tail with -f/-n, --json for machines; phux service logs delegates. (3) doctor gains a logs check (doctor.rs:104-109 has four checks today, none names logs). (4) doctor and logs get surfaced in README and QUICKSTART (grep-verified zero doctor mentions today). (5) Stale process-model.md:22-34 state-dir/stderr claims fixed inside C1 (owner; stream F's F6 defers to it). Fatal-error log pointers implemented in C6 to keep the error-remedy pass in one place. Decomposed into C1, C2, C3; umbrella.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: canonical log, phux logs verb, doctor path reporting all landed.

title: Dead config keys: implement or delete defaults.shell / refresh-rate / log-filter; honor or drop the widget style promise
description:
Keys that parse, validate clean, echo back in config show, and do nothing:

- defaults.shell (schema.rs:96): consumed NOWHERE — server unconditionally uses $SHELL (phux-server/src/terminal_actor/spawn.rs:123,266). It is the FIRST LINE of the documented minimal config (tui.md:578) and tests/loader.rs:110 green-lights it.
- defaults.refresh-rate (tui.md:580): dead.
- defaults.log-filter: dead, undocumented, and its doc-comment claims $PHUX_LOG overrides it when PHUX_LOG is actually a log file path (main.rs:132).
- Widget `style` table: tui.md:1923-1925 promises every widget accepts style {fg,bg,bold,...}; NO factory reads it (time.rs:74-89, session_name.rs:65-99, cwd.rs:104-139, exit_status.rs, exec.rs). Opts are an open BTreeMap so it parses and renders unstyled. Only help-hints rejects unknown opts (help_hints.rs:33-38) — the inconsistency is itself a trap.
- session-name widget: tui.md:1911 documents a `format` opt that does not exist (session_name.rs:68-93 reads prefix/max-len).
- defaults.mouse works but is documented nowhere.

Fix: each key either gets implemented or deleted (with docs updated); widget opts move to closed structs or a per-factory unknown-opt warning surfaced via config check. Guiding rule: if `phux config check` says ok, the key must do something.
design:
---

**Design resolution (stream A, 2026-08-01) — per-key verdicts** (note: widget factories live in crates/phux-config/src/widget/widgets/, not phux-client; substance of every audit claim holds): defaults.shell (schema.rs:93-96) IMPLEMENT via a resolve_shell seam mirroring the defaults.term/apply_term precedent, threaded from the server's single config load. defaults.refresh-rate DELETE (no consumer exists; with deny_unknown_fields a stale config fails loudly with a located finding — the epic's contract). defaults.log-filter DELETE (zero consumers; its $PHUX_LOG doc claim is false — PHUX_LOG is a log-file path; filtering is RUST_LOG). defaults.mouse works — DOCUMENT in tui.md §12. Widget style table (tui.md:1927-1929 promise) IMPLEMENT UNIVERSALLY by hoisting style extraction into the registry build path (CellStyle already exists). session-name `format` opt IMPLEMENT. Widget opts CLOSE: generalize help_hints' unknown-opt rejection to every factory with did-you-mean; surface widget composition errors through config check. Decomposed into A8 (defaults truth) and A9 (widget closure + style). Umbrella.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: defaults truth (wave 3) + widget closure/style (wave 4).

title: [umbrella] Validate what parses: vocab registry, config check semantics, lenient resolver, honest error lines
description:
Everything that parses is assumed valid; three independent silent-no-op traps:

1. Typo'd action name: "x" = "kill-pain" parses (Action::Bare, schema.rs:369), passes config check, and the key does nothing — logged at tracing::debug only (input_dispatch.rs:2560-2562). The canonical 36-name list ACTION_NAMES already exists (input_dispatch.rs:1727) and is CI-enforced against the palette, but is not exposed to the validator.

2. One malformed chord disables EVERY keybinding including detach: driver.rs:3709-3716 — Resolver::new fails on first bad chord -> tracing::warn -> None -> no binding resolves. config check cannot catch it because chords are BTreeMap string keys.

3. Hooks fail open three ways (check.rs:329-334 asserts free-form hook keys are never flagged): typo'd event name ([[hooks.pane-exited]] vs real pane-exit, phux-server/src/hooks.rs:56) never fires; unknown `when` key never matches (hooks.rs:528); non-server-executable matched action consumes the event at debug level (hooks.rs:435-440). The six valid event names are consts at hooks.rs:54-64, surfaced nowhere.

Fix: teach phux config check (and resolver-build error paths) the action-name list, chord grammar, and hook event-name list; a bad chord must degrade to "this one binding is dead, loudly" not "all bindings are dead, silently". Also fix the on-screen config error (driver.rs:4259) to recommend `phux config check` instead of `phux config show`, and stop printing the fabricated 1:1 position (lib.rs:143) that check.rs:19-21 itself calls "worse than reporting none".
design:
---

**Design resolution (stream A, 2026-08-01).** Evidence verified: ACTION_NAMES at input_dispatch.rs:1726 (36 names, CI-synced); silent unhandled-action arm at input_dispatch.rs:2560-2562; Resolver::new fails whole on first bad chord and driver.rs:3709-3716 degrades to None = every binding dead including detach; unknown hook `when` key silently never matches (hooks.rs:519-530); non-`run` matched hook action consumes the event at debug! (hooks.rs:435-440); fabricated (1,1) span at lib.rs:130-131; wrong remedy `phux config show` at driver.rs:4256-4260. Architecture decision: **phux-config owns the validation vocabulary** (new crates/phux-config/src/vocab.rs). ACTION_NAMES moves INTO phux-config and is re-exported from input_dispatch.rs; hook event names move in from phux-server hooks.rs with re-exports; CI sync tests pin dispatch to vocab. No new crate, no codegen; did-you-mean is a ~25-line in-crate Levenshtein, no new dependency. Resolver policy: attach-time builds become lenient per-binding (new_lenient + diagnostics surfaced on the status bar); strict new stays for config check and reload (reload keeps all-or-nothing per tui.md:1119-1122). Decomposed into A2 (vocab), A3 (chords+actions in check), A4 (hooks in check + loud runtime warnings), A5 (lenient resolver), A6 (remedy + span honesty). Umbrella. Cross-stream: vocab is also consumed by stream F's generated action/widget/hook references (F3/F4).
close_reason: Umbrella complete: all five children (vocab, check semantics, hooks, lenient resolver, honest errors) landed across waves 1-3.

title: TUI failure surface: pane exit status, last-pane death, live reconnect indicator
description:
Three silent failure paths in the attach TUI, all evidence-verified:

1. Pane death is invisible. server_frame.rs:1169-1215 (phux-client): TerminalClosed receives exit_status, logs at tracing::info (file only), removes the PaneSlot, folds the layout. No toast, no "[exited 137]" placeholder, no status-bar line. When the last pane dies (1211-1216) the whole client exits with zero explanation — an OOM-killed shell looks like phux crashed.

2. Server crash = ~10 seconds of blank terminal. attach.rs:272 RECONNECT_DEADLINE=10s; attach.rs:335-341 prints "server restarted; re-attaching" only AFTER a successful reconnect; the alt screen is already torn down. No "reconnecting..." indicator during the window, and on failure the user gets the generic "connection closed by server before DETACHED" arm (mod.rs:2095-2097) with no log path, no doctor pointer.

3. The status-bar error_line mechanism exists (status_bar.rs:526-534) but is called for config errors only (driver.rs:4224,4251). Disconnect, reconnect-in-progress, pane death, degraded federation, take/give authority changes all have no user-facing representation.

Fix: exit-status toast + optional dead-pane placeholder; a reconnecting state that is visible while it happens; route lifecycle events through the existing error_line/toast machinery. docs/consumers/tui.md:28-40 calls the TUI the adoption wedge — the wire is the differentiator and the wire is precisely what has no failure UI.
design:
DESIGN RESOLUTION (stream B, 2026-08-01) — decomposed into B1/B2/B3; umbrella. Resolved: (1) Pane-death UX is a transient STATUS-BAR NOTICE, not a modal and not a dead-pane placeholder (placeholder rejected: layout is a shared metadata envelope — a client-local dead leaf desyncs siblings and PTY winsizes; a server-side dead leaf is a wire change out of scope). Text 'pane <label>: exited N' / 'killed (signal or unknown)'; suppressed for exit 0 and client-initiated kill-pane; 7 s newest-wins slot. (2) Last-pane death: run_* entry points return Result<AttachEnd, AttachError> (Detached | LastPaneClosed { exit_status }); the CLI prints a one-line explanation on the cooked terminal after teardown; process exit stays 0. (3) Reconnect: NO alt-screen re-entry — RawModeGuard drops on unwind (driver.rs:1258), so the 10 s wait (attach.rs:318-344) runs cooked; honest design is a live stderr countdown plus a post-reconnect status-bar notice inside the next attach (the current eprintln at attach.rs:337 is instantly alt-screened over). Failure distinguishes socket-unlinked vs timeout and names phux doctor. (4) General mechanism: StatusBarPainter gains a transient Notice slot riding the existing 1 s status_tick; persistent error_line outranks it; FrameOutcome gains notices: Vec<Notice>; first consumer is input-authority transitions. No wire changes — TERMINAL_CLOSED already carries exit_status (frame.rs:2105-2110).

FINALIZER AMENDMENT (2026-08-01): the bead's five enumerated lifecycle events must ALL map to a surface. Degraded federation was orphaned; B1 now carries it as the Notice slot's second consumer (degraded-federation transitions push a Warn notice, server_frame-tested). C5's phux status degradation line remains the CLI view, not a substitute for the in-TUI representation.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: notice mechanism, pane death, reconnect window all landed (waves 1,2,6).

title: Server silently swallows a broken config.toml and reverts to defaults
description:
crates/phux/src/commands/server.rs:113-148 reads history-limit, cwd-inheritance, term, window-size, and the entire hook catalog via five consecutive config_loader::load().map_or_else(|_| default, ...) calls. A single typo in config.toml silently disables every configured hook and reverts scrollback/TERM/window-size policy, then the server prints its normal "listening on ..." banner. Contrast server.rs:153-158 where connector registry failure correctly aborts loudly, and the client attach path which at least prints one line (attach.rs:110-113).

Also: config is read from disk five separate times in ~35 lines, so an edit mid-startup yields a torn read.

Fix: load once, bind once. On failure, print the config-check-style error to stderr (and the server log) and state explicitly which defaults are in effect. Never revert silently.
design:
---

**Design resolution (stream A, 2026-08-01).** Audit correction: a malformed config.toml already kills the server today via the fatal connector-registry read (server.rs:153-158) with a misattributed error; the five earlier reads (server.rs:113-148) silently default and misattribute every config error to the connector registry. Resolved design: load config exactly once; a broken config is fatal at server start with the real error and the remedy `run: phux config check`, written to both stderr and the server log via tracing::error (auto-spawn nulls stdio, so the log line is the durable trace). Missing file stays fine (loader.rs:71-77 returns defaults on NotFound). Degrade-and-continue rejected: the connector security stance already makes any parse error fatal, and one load cannot scope an error to a section. Decomposed into A1 (single load + loud fatal) and A8 (defaults.shell rides A1's struct). This bead is now an umbrella.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: single child 1.1 landed (wave 1).

title: [epic] UX: it just works — never silent, one grammar, visible at the moment of need
description:
Full-surface UX audit (2026-08-01, three parallel deep audits: CLI ergonomics, config surface, onboarding/visibility) found that phux's UX foundations are genuinely excellent but exist as islands: phux doctor, phux config check, config layering with provenance, output_hygiene.rs, the broken-pipe discipline, the first-run overlay. The product-level failures are four systemic patterns, not missing features:

1. SILENCE. Errors, dead keys, typos, and pane death all no-op invisibly: server swallows a broken config.toml with zero output (server.rs:113-148); a typo'd action name logs at debug (input_dispatch.rs:2560); one malformed chord disables ALL keybindings including detach (driver.rs:3709); a dying pane discards its exit status (server_frame.rs:1169-1216); server crash = 10s blank screen (attach.rs:272-341).

2. INVISIBILITY. The good tools are never pointed to at the moment of need: doctor appears in zero READMEs/quickstarts; three different log files exist and no command or doc ever prints any path; the on-screen config error names the wrong recovery command (driver.rs:4259 says "phux config show", the diagnostic tool is "config check").

3. INCONSISTENCY. 89 invocation paths with per-command grammar: --socket copy-pasted 36 times and not global; --json on ~32 verbs with no shorthand and no error-path contract; ls/list/rm/remove alias roulette across 8 registries; two split-direction flag styles (one of which is parsed and discarded, main.rs:364); four near-duplicate concept pairs (enroll vs satellite enroll, remote vs satellite, pair vs relay pair, workspace vs worktree).

4. DOCS DRIFT. CONFIG.md says reload does not exist (it ships); tui.md promises a widget style table no factory reads; README claims scrollback search that has no action; defaults.shell is the first line of the documented minimal config and is consumed nowhere.

Design principle for every child issue: the failure path IS the product. Simplicity means one grammar, and every error names its own remedy. Builds on phux-q9wj (CLI and API surface polish, 3/4 done); supersedes its altitude.

Full audit reports preserved in the three child-issue descriptions and session transcript 3bedc523.
design:
---

**Stream G landing sequence (planning resolution, 2026-08-01).** The epic lands in dependency waves closed by stream-G integration gates: never-silent failure surface (.1-.6) gated by G2; one-grammar + host namespace (.7 .8 .12) gated by G3; help/discoverability/docs+generated reference (.9 .10 .11) gated by G4. After the grammar wave, a deprecation-alias audit test (crates/phux/tests/deprecated_aliases.rs) pins every hidden alias, its deprecation note, and its absence from help/completions, bidirectionally against the clap tree. A scripted failure-UX dogfood lands as crates/phux/tests/failure_ux_e2e.rs in the `just e2e` PR lane (per scripts/check-e2e-lanes.sh), so the new failure UX is CI-enforced, not a release ritual. Release is a release-please minor bump (0.6.0 -> 0.7.0, automatic from feat commits under bump-minor-pre-major): run scripts/release-preflight.sh, undraft the release PR to run CI, merge; then `gh release edit` prepends the UX story + deprecation table (release.yml only uploads assets, never rewrites the body). Epic close: bd close sweep, bd remember entries (vocab location, reference-generation mechanism, alias contract, failure-UX lane), vision.md remaining-work reality check. Merge protocol throughout: branch per slice, rebase + ff-only, conventional commits, `just ci` green before every merge.
notes: EXECUTION IN PROGRESS (2026-08-01, session 3bedc523): user ordered full autonomous execution to completion. Wave-by-wave workflow loop; playbook + graph at scratchpad ux-epic/ (execution-playbook.md). Wave 1 = phux-i0e8.1.1, .3.1, .3.4, .2.1 branching from origin/main 6770f366.
close_reason: EPIC COMPLETE (v0.11.0, 2026-08-03): 52 tasks, 13 umbrellas, 14 merged PRs. Never silent: config/actions/chords/hooks validated with did-you-mean, pane death + reconnect visible, every error names its remedy, failure-UX e2e lane in CI. One grammar: global --socket, JSON error contract, alias parity, --split, phux host namespace with audited deprecations. Visible: status/logs/doctor triad. Zero drift: all reference docs generated from the binary with byte-exact CI gates.

title: Snapshot replay drops mouse-reporting DEC modes, breaking scroll in TUIs after attach

title: Headless geometry: agents cannot set a pane size without a real PTY
description:
There is no way to set a pane's size without attaching a real terminal. phux new has no size flag, phux snapshot --rendered --cols/--rows does not persist (verified: pane stayed 80x24 after a 120x40 rendered read), and there is no phux resize verb.

This bit twice building phux rec: the demo asset is stuck at 80x24, and the non-resize regression test has to stand up a full portable-pty attach purely to obtain a pane whose size differs from the 80x24 a mistaken attach would impose -- otherwise the test resizes an 80x24 pane to 80x24 and passes vacuously.

For a project whose pitch is that agents are first-class users, agents cannot set a terminal's size. Proposed: a phux resize TARGET COLSxROWS verb and/or --cols/--rows on phux new, with the interaction against the attached-client WindowSize policy (schema.rs WindowSize::Smallest) thought through and specced -- that policy is why this is a design question and not a one-line flag.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: Conformance test: the three libghostty cell projections must agree
description:
The libghostty snapshot -> RenderedFrame projection now exists three times: crates/phux-client/src/attach/render.rs, crates/phux-server/src/grid/synthesizer.rs, and crates/phux-record/src/replay.rs.

The duplication is a DELIBERATE, documented tradeoff (a shared home would force phux-core to depend on libghostty, which is worse), so this issue is not 'deduplicate them'. It is that three copies which must agree cell-for-cell have nothing enforcing it, and divergence surfaces as 'the recording does not match the screen' or 'the agent sees different cells than the human' -- the bug class nobody notices for months.

Work: a conformance test that feeds one corpus of VT bytes (SGR truecolor and palette, wide CJK plus spacer tails, combining marks, alt screen, scroll regions, DECAWM wrap, cursor states) through all three projections and asserts identical output. Where they cannot be identical, assert the difference explicitly so it is a decision rather than a drift.

Consider afterwards whether a thin phux-vt-project crate between phux-core and libghostty is worth the refactor; the test is valuable either way and is the cheap half.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: Shared scripted-server test harness so fakes cannot lie about frame order
description:
Unit-test fake servers are hand-written per module, so each one encodes what its author believed the protocol does. That is the same belief that produces the bug, so the fake cannot catch it.

Evidence: 17 phux rec unit tests passed against a completely non-functional feature because the fake answered COMMAND_RESULT before the priming snapshot, while the real server does the opposite.

Work, cheapest first:
1. Extract one shared scripted_server into a test-support module, with the reference server's frame ORDER encoded once (snapshot before ack on ATTACH_TERMINAL, etc.).
2. Migrate the per-module fakes to it.
3. Consider golden frame traces: capture real server responses once into fixtures and replay them, so a fake that diverges from the reference implementation fails. Bigger lift; decide after 1 and 2.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: Add Connection::request so COMMAND callers cannot swallow interleaved frames
description:
Connection exposes send()/recv() only, so every COMMAND caller hand-rolls 'loop until my request_id returns'. The server legitimately interleaves: handle_attach_terminal pushes TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT before the COMMAND_RESULT ack. A caller that discards non-matching frames loses data that is never re-sent.

This is not hypothetical. It shipped as a bug in phux rec (fixed in PR #306): captures came back as a 0x0 grid with no opening screen, and all 17 unit tests passed because the scripted fake answered ack-first.

Work:
1. Add Connection::request(cmd) -> Result<(CommandResult, Vec<FrameKind>)> that returns interleaved frames instead of eating them. Callers physically cannot forget what they did not ask to drop.
2. AUDIT every existing COMMAND caller for the same swallow: GetScreen, GetTerminalState, AcquireInput, ReleaseInput, SignalTerminal, KillTerminal(s), DetachClients, PutFile, SubscribeTerminalEvents. Report which ones discard frames and whether the server can interleave on that path. This audit is the point of the issue; the helper is the easy half.
3. Migrate callers, and document the interleave contract on Connection itself.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: worktree remove kills bound session before git validates removal
description: run_remove in crates/phux/src/commands/worktree.rs kills the bound session BEFORE running git worktree remove, but only pre-checks 'current' and dirty state. git also refuses: main working tree, locked worktrees, submodules. Scenario: 'phux worktree remove main' from another worktree kills the primary session, then git refuses removal — session lost, worktree still there. Fix: mark first entry from 'git worktree list --porcelain' as is_main and refuse before killing; also check locked attribute. Found by research-team review of f1a1306..b7ffd45, adversarially verified.
notes: Fixed: WorktreeInfo now carries is_main (first porcelain entry) and locked; run_remove refuses main worktree and locked worktrees BEFORE killing the session. Parser test extended.
close_reason: Closed

title: BUG: PTY input writer corrupts or dies under large paste load
description: Live phux-mobile image-upload experiments over INPUT_PASTE reproduced nondeterministic byte corruption in tiny 1.8 KiB base64 payloads (first divergence around byte 1150/1450) and the server log 'pty writer: write failed; pane input is now dead' under load. A 1.9 MiB JPEG also remained in canonical-mode ingest after 24s. ADR-0059 PutFile bypasses this path for file upload, but large interactive pastes still traverse the PTY input writer and may corrupt or permanently kill pane input. Reproduce with repeated multi-KiB trusted INPUT_PASTE / APPLY_INPUT batches against a checksum-reading fixture; fix write/flush/backpressure ownership so bytes are ordered and the writer survives transient pressure.
close_reason:
Resolved by decomposition (option A). RCA split this into three distinct defects; every part is now fixed or tracked separately.

1. 'dies under load' -> REAL BUG, fixed. Writer broke on any io::Error with no errno discrimination and never restarted, so a routine child exit permanently killed pane input. Fixed in phux-oxd7 / PR #318 (4bbe113e).

2. 'corrupts' -> WORKS AS SPECIFIED. A single INPUT_PASTE event is already atomic (one contiguous Vec, one write_all). Corruption only appears when a consumer splits ONE logical payload across MULTIPLE fire-and-forget events, and L1 SPEC section 9 explicitly makes those droppable ('a full mailbox drops the event but still acks OK'). The spec never promised cross-event delivery or ordering. ADR-0053 APPLY_INPUT (acknowledged, reconnect-safe) and ADR-0059 PutFile exist for exactly this; the original reporter, phux-mobile image upload, has already moved to PutFile. Making fire-and-forget atomic would put backpressure on the hot keystroke path -- a latency regression for phux's core purpose -- to buy correctness a different verb already provides. The defensible complaint was the SILENCE, not the semantics: both drop sites were raised to warn!/error! in PR #318.

3. 'canonical-mode ingest stuck after 24s' -> separate mechanism, tracked as phux-mjmc (P2). Empirically reproduced: MAX_CANON wedge, a hang rather than corruption.

Residual guidance gap filed separately.

title: send-keys TARGET "text" Enter does not submit in codex; Enter must be a separate call
description:
Observed while capturing codex detection fixtures. 'phux send-keys --socket S cx "prompt text" Enter' places the text in codex's composer but does NOT submit — the composer still shows the text and no turn starts. Sending 'phux send-keys --socket S cx Enter' as its own call immediately submits.

Likely the same class herdr hit (their 0.7.5 notes: 'Named agent prompts now honor live bracketed-paste mode before sending Enter'). Probable cause: the text is delivered as a paste/bracketed run and the trailing Enter is coalesced into it, so codex sees a literal newline inside the paste rather than a submit key.

Matters because it is the documented one-liner for driving an agent from a script, and it silently half-works: the text lands, so a caller sees no error and waits forever for a turn that never started. Worth an e2e test against a real agent TUI.
close_reason: Merged by PR #295 after live Codex reproduction and full local CI passed
