title: 97 wire discriminants are hand-allocated consts, so a duplicate tag is not a compile error
description:
Found 2026-08-17 by the phux-5xtz registry-gate sweep. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-CONSEQUENCE INSTANCE of the identifier-collision class that has now bitten four times (two ADR-0086 files, a reintroduced manifest key, and two branches claiming spec CHANGELOG 0.8.0-draft.4).

THE HAZARD: crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/frame/mod.rs declares ~97 u8 wire discriminants as individual const items, NOT as an enum. So two branches independently allocating the same tag produce NO compile error, NO test failure, and NO gate failure — and unlike an ADR number or a CHANGELOG row, a duplicate here is a PROTOCOL BREAK that ships. Coverage today is partial and accidental: rustc's unreachable_patterns fires only for tags that appear in the decode match, and not at all for spec-reserved consts no arm uses yet (e.g. TYPE_SPAWN_PROCESS). Contrast PhysicalKey and ErrorCode, which are #[repr(u32)] enums where rustc catches duplicates outright — the discriminant consts are the outlier.

COMPOUNDING IT: docs/spec/appendix-reserved.md is literally the 'pick your next number here' file, and the message-ID and feature-bit tables in appendix-reserved.md, L1.md, L3.md and proto.md are ungated on the ID column — the impl-status gate resolves each row's NAME against a const but never reads its ID, so two branches both claiming 0x18 pass every check in the repo.

TWO FIXES, not mutually exclusive: (a) CHEAP AND IMMEDIATE — instantiate the new check_registry_rows helper (landed in phux-5xtz, scripts/check-docs.sh) against the spec ID tables; the agent reports this is a row_re + rank_fn pair away with no new machinery. (b) STRUCTURAL — make the discriminants an enum or add a compile-time uniqueness assertion so rustc owns it, which is what already protects ErrorCode. (b) is the real fix; (a) is worth doing first because it is nearly free.

Deliberately NOT bundled into phux-5xtz: that bead's scope was the doc registries, and touching wire discriminants needs its own review.

title: Cross-cutting cleanup pass over the 2026-08-16/17 eight-agent batch
description:
Filed retroactively 2026-08-17 to give a tracked home to a /simplify pass that was run without a bead (a process miss — this repo requires the bead before the code). CONTEXT: eight commits (f3bb7a86..61167c28) were written by eight INDEPENDENT agents who never read each other's work and landed in one batch, which is the condition that breeds duplicated helpers and parallel error-rendering paths. A four-angle review (reuse / simplification / efficiency / altitude) was run over the combined 3671-line diff, then applied in three file-disjoint lanes.

WHAT THE REVIEW FOUND, and what shipped:
- RenderPool had TWO entry points (begin / begin_generation) where choosing wrong is SILENT GRID CORRUPTION, guarded only by a doc comment; collapsed to one, Option state removed, the interleaving-rule test deleted. render_pool.rs 347->289.
- The generation token was threaded as a separate positional parameter through eight render methods, pushing render_at_letterboxed over clippy's arg limit; replaced by a ReplicaWalk struct. too_many_arguments allow DELETED, 38 test call sites simplified, TEST_GENERATION removed from the tree.
- TWO agents wrote the SAME user-facing armed-supervision paragraph (service.rs + doctor.rs) for the same bead, already drifted (semicolon vs period), each pinned by its own test. Now one const, both surfaces assert it verbatim.
- FRAME_TOO_LARGE's peer-visible message was constructed in two modules with only one pinned by a test; now one constructor in phux-protocol.
- metadata_broadcast was extracted from metadata_set but metadata_set still inlined the same two statements; rewired, one fanout implementation for three callers.
- The hub link grew a SECOND three-way transport write dispatch beside send_frame; collapsed to one send-then-condemn path via send_bounded.
- The SPEC section 14 fatal-close assertion existed in three private helpers under three names; promoted to phux-server-testkit.
- phux agent start parsed the ENTIRE plugin tree twice on its default path; one walk now.
- Kind-resolution helpers were pure functions over a phux-plugin type living in a CLI module; moved to phux-plugin so other consumers can reach them.
- The hermetic test env was hand-copied in two builders (which is why the idle backstop had to be added twice); one table now, and the backstop moved onto AutoSpawnedServer, the type that defines the hazard.

TWO INTENTIONAL BEHAVIOUR FIXES shipped with their own tests: doctor's dropped unit_supervises socket guard restored (it would warn about a marker armed for a different profile/socket), and the unclaimed-kind fallback canonicalised.

SHIPPED AS: 3ee24148 (render), 98ff18bb (server), 901ae39b (cli) — one ci-full green over the batch, 3913 tests, zero retries, no .snap.new produced. Follow-ups filed separately rather than fixed here.
close_reason: Delivered as commits 3ee24148 / 98ff18bb / 901ae39b, all pushed to main after one green ci-full (3913 tests, zero retries, no snapshot churn). Deferred items were filed as their own beads rather than folded in.

title: ADR-0071's 1.0 freeze does not name the shipped 'phux agent report-state' verb
description:
Found 2026-08-17 during the ADR-0075/0076/0078 ratification analysis. This is a LIVE breach of the freeze, not a hypothetical.

THE FACT: 'phux agent report-state TARGET STATE' is a shipped, documented CLI verb. Declared at crates/phux/src/commands/agent/mod.rs:115-121 (value_parser working/blocked/done). Documented in docs/reference/cli.md:188 and :399-404, docs/consumers/agents.md:531, and crates/phux/src/help_inventory.rs:103. But grep -n 'report.state' ADR/0071-what-phux-1-0-commits-to.md returns NO MATCH.

CAUSE — a date gap, not an oversight: ADR-0071 was last edited 2026-08-13 (cc9084d7); ADR-0085 shipped report-state on 2026-08-14. ADR-0071 point 7(c) requires anything ratified out of ADR-0075/0076/0078 to be carved into the freeze, but ADR-0085 was not on that list, so nothing forced the amendment. This is precisely the 'no agent verb is discovered post-freeze' failure point 7(c) exists to prevent, arriving through a door 7(c) does not cover.

WORK: (1) add 'agent report-state' to ADR-0071 point 6's verb list — it has no --json and no MCP tool, so it is a one-line addition. (2) WIDEN point 7(c) from 'ADR-0075/0076/0078' to 'any ADR that adds consumer surface', which is the structural fix.

VERIFIED NOT BREACHED (so do not re-file these): AgentExplainJson IS named at ADR-0071:105-106; the agent_state watch event name IS named with its full field list at :121-128; the three error codes capture_unreadable/capture_invalid/unknown_agent_kind are named at :128-132; point 7(b)'s ten-tool MCP freeze is accurate — exactly ten phux_agent_* tools exist. Bead phux-w7z2.2's first section is therefore stale and closeable: all three of its 'shipped but unnamed' items were absorbed into point 6 by commit 8d06829c on 2026-08-09, the day it was filed.

title: Extend the collision gate to spec CHANGELOG version rows, not just ADR numbers
description: Found 2026-08-17 in the merge queue, one batch after phux-254o landed the ADR-index collision gate. Two parallel branches (w1/frame-too-large and w1/rename-notify) BOTH claimed spec CHANGELOG row 0.8.0-draft.4. This is exactly the failure shape phux-254o was filed for — parallel branches silently claiming the same identifier with no textual conflict against main — but the new adr-index-sync gate only covers ADR/README.md rows, so it did not catch this one. It surfaced as a rebase conflict at integration (better than silence, because both branches insert at the same table anchor) but only because both touched the same file; a per-branch gate would have caught it before the merge queue and saved a gate cycle.\n\nWORK: extend scripts/check-docs.sh with a changelog-version-unique gate asserting that docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md version rows are unique and strictly descending (newest at top), matching the adr-index-sync gate's style. Note the existing spec-version-sync gate only checks that the TOP row matches PROTOCOL_VERSION — it says nothing about duplicates or ordering further down. Also worth considering per phux-254o's own reasoning: any other tracked file where a sequential identifier is hand-allocated (ADR numbers now covered, spec CHANGELOG rows this bead, manifest keys still uncovered) belongs in the same gate family.
notes: DEEPER FIX 2026-08-17 (altitude review), superseding the shallow version of this bead: do NOT hard-code a second instance. scripts/check-docs.sh:588 currently encodes a PATTERN — 'a shared append-only registry needs uniqueness + ordering enforced so parallel branches conflict textually' — as a single hard-coded instance for ADR/README.md. Verified adjacent hole: gate_spec_version_sync (check-docs.sh:663) parses ONLY the head row and compares it to PROTOCOL_VERSION; it has no duplicate-version check and no monotonicity check, so two branches both landing 0.8.0-draft.4 produce two rows and the gate passes clean — which is exactly what happened in this session's batch. FIX: extract check_registry_rows <file> <row-regex> <direction> <label> enforcing (a) no duplicate key, (b) key ordering in the given direction, (c) referent resolution where the row carries a link. Instantiate TWICE: ADR/README.md (ascending, link-resolving) and docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md (descending, no link). CONTRIBUTING.md's new paragraph already generalizes the RULE to 'any other shared registry' — the script should follow it there, so the third collision surface does not have to be learned and hard-coded a third time.

title: Session-seed panes broadcast no PaneSpawned, so server-wide event followers miss headlessly-created sessions
description: Found 2026-08-16 while verifying phux-w7z2.20's wire-change claim. Both AgentEvent::PaneSpawned broadcast sites live inside handle_spawn_terminal (crates/phux-server/src/runtime/attach.rs:1799 and :1898). The FIRST pane of a new session is seeded by seed_session_with_pty_and_colors and broadcasts nothing, on two paths: (a) attach CreateIfMissing (runtime/attach.rs ~680), (b) headless CREATE_SESSION (runtime/commands.rs ~2236-2246) — which is exactly how phux new / phux worktree / an orchestrator creates an agent session (create_session_via_metadata, phux/src/commands/new.rs:325). Consequence: any server-wide event follower (the fleet-inbox sidebar roster, the future phux agent wait --any) misses sessions created after it attached until a Dirty leaks out. Fix: broadcast_event(.., AgentEvent::PaneSpawned) after seeding on both paths — server-side only, no wire change (PaneSpawned already exists; additive emission is compatible per ADR-0061; add a spec CHANGELOG draft entry if the spec enumerates emission sites). Regression test: drive handle_client with a subscribed server-wide watcher, create a session headlessly via CREATE_SESSION, assert PaneSpawned arrives. This also shrinks phux-k0cw.7's poll to a pure safety floor.
notes:
CROSS-REF 2026-08-16: phux-q7ks landed rename broadcasts (branch w1/rename-notify). Its agent independently confirmed the remaining gap is CREATE-side only: create_named_session broadcasts nothing. This bead's seed-pane PaneSpawned broadcast is the event-layer fix for the same gap; landing it removes the last push-coverage hole for session lifecycle (death=PaneClosed, rename=METADATA_CHANGED, create=this).
SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-17 (altitude review): this bead CANNOT be implemented as 'call metadata_broadcast in two more places'. Verified: CREATE is genuinely uncovered — runtime/client.rs:2182 handle_session_create_metadata writes the RESULT to SESSION_CREATE_RESULT_KEY, so a subscriber of phux.session.create/v1 learns nothing about the session existing — and DESTROY has no metadata write at all. The shape chosen for rename does not generalize: create's payload is a REQUEST JSON, not a state transition, and destroy has no write to intercept. So this needs a session-lifecycle EVENT (the AgentEvent::PaneSpawned broadcast this bead already proposes) or a server-written roster key — not the metadata_broadcast tool. Stated here so the next agent does not reach for the wrong one.
close_reason: a new session's seed pane is now announced via AgentEvent::PaneSpawned on both the attach CreateIfMissing and headless session.create paths

title: service status leaks launchctl stderr and contradicts itself on an armed unit
description:
Observed on a real machine 2026-08-16, immediately after 'phux service install --adopt' (phux-m3ot, ADR-0088).

'phux service status' prints the correct armed explanation, then follows it with raw launchctl output that contradicts it:

  unit  /Users/phall/Library/LaunchAgents/com.phux.server.plist
  state armed - installed with --adopt and waiting for the running server to exit

  The server holding this unit's socket is unsupervised and keeps its panes.
  Supervision begins at the next login, or at the first phux command after
  that server exits. phux service uninstall cancels it.

  Bad request.
  Could not find service "com.phux.server" in domain for user gui: 501
  installed, but the init system is not running it.

Two defects in those last three lines:

1. 'Bad request.' and 'Could not find service ... in domain for user gui: 501' are launchctl's own stderr, surfaced verbatim. A user cannot tell whether phux failed, launchctl failed, or nothing failed.

2. The state is not an error at all. An armed unit is BY DESIGN written-but-not-loaded, so launchctl not knowing about it is the expected, correct observation - it is what 'armed' MEANS. Reporting it as though something is wrong directly contradicts the paragraph three lines above, and 'installed, but the init system is not running it' reads as a fault when it is the intended state.

The armed path should either skip the launchctl liveness query entirely (nothing is loaded, by construction) or translate its not-found result into the armed vocabulary rather than passing the error text through.

Adjacent question worth answering while in there: 'phux doctor' reports all checks passing and says nothing about supervision being armed-but-not-active. ADR-0080 made a crash-loop reportable precisely because an invisible supervision state is how a broken server passed for a working one. An armed-and-pending unit is a similar in-between state a user would want surfaced.
close_reason: phux service status renders armed state in phux vocabulary; doctor warns on armed-but-inactive supervision

title: The first-five install lane leaks daemonized servers; phux-whhd only cleared the nextest lane
description:
Found 2026-08-16 while cleaning the dev box. Eight orphaned servers were alive from a single run window (Aug 15 17:13:21-17:18:21), all of the shape:

  <tmpdir>/prefix/bin/phux server --socket <tmpdir>/runtime/first-five.sock --session home --daemonize

They are from the 'first five minutes' install/smoke lane, which installs phux into a temp prefix and starts a daemonized server there. The tempdirs are gone or orphaned; the servers outlive them and hold PTYs indefinitely.

Why this is NOT already covered by phux-whhd: whhd was closed on 2026-08-15 after measuring 'zero stray servers after a full cargo nextest run --workspace', repeated four times including under 16 synthetic CPU burners. That measurement was correct AND the leak is real -- they are different lanes. The nextest lane is clean; this install lane is not. The bead's scope was implicitly narrower than its title.

Also observed, and worth keeping: of ten orphans killed, nine died on SIGTERM and one did not. The survivor (started Aug 11 05:51) predates the server's SIGTERM handler and needed SIGKILL. So 'phux kill --server' / signal-based cleanup only works for servers built after that handler landed -- any pre-handler daemon still alive on a developer box is immortal by design and must be SIGKILLed.

Fix direction: the lane that spawns these needs the same --exit-after-idle backstop phux-nbam added (PHUX_AUTO_SPAWN_EXIT_AFTER_IDLE), or an explicit teardown. Per phux-nbam's finding, the backstop is opt-in and nothing opts in -- this lane is a concrete caller that should.
close_reason: first-five e2e lane now reaps its daemonized server and arms --exit-after-idle 600 backstop

title: [bug] RENAME_SESSION notifies nobody: the handler returns before metadata_set
description:
Found 2026-08-15 during the phux-k0cw recon (PR #478); filed rather than fixed because it is server-side and outside that branch's scope.

THE GAP. crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs (around the rename handler, ~:2337-2361) returns BEFORE calling metadata_set, so renaming a session writes the new name without broadcasting a METADATA_CHANGED. No subscriber learns about it.

Session lifecycle coverage today, for a client subscribed server-wide:
- DEATH  — covered. PaneClosed reaches every EventScope::Server subscriber (crates/phux-server/src/state/client_table.rs:350).
- CREATE — covered only indirectly. create_named_session (crates/phux-server/src/runtime/commands.rs:2203) broadcasts nothing, so a headlessly-created session surfaces when its seed pane first emits Dirty.
- RENAME — covered by NOTHING. This bead.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. Before the cross-session sidebar this was invisible: peer session names were read once at attach and only shown inside a modal the user had just opened. ADR-0089 puts peer session names in always-on chrome (the 'spaces' roster), so a rename now leaves a stale name on screen indefinitely — the roster confidently displays a name that no longer exists.

phux-k0cw.7 works around it client-side with a session-graph poll. Fixing it here would make that poll cheaper or unnecessary, so the two beads should be considered together: if this lands first, .7 may shrink to create-only coverage.

REPRO: attach a client, rename a session from another shell (phux rename <old> <new>), observe no METADATA_CHANGED on the first client and a stale name in its roster.
acceptance_criteria: Renaming a session broadcasts to subscribers of the affected key, so an attached client's session roster and pickers show the new name without a poll or a re-attach. A regression test drives a rename against a subscribed client and asserts the notification.
close_reason: an applied session rename now broadcasts METADATA_CHANGED to L3 subscribers of phux.session.name/v1

title: Move the peer subscription sweep after the first paint of a session switch
description:
Deferred out of phux-k0cw.5 (deliberately, not overlooked).

The peer sweep (sync_foreign_layout_subscriptions + sync_foreign_agent_subscriptions) runs during bootstrap, BEFORE the first paint. A session switch tears down every server-side subscription (the server drops them with the attach) and rebuilds every driver local from empty, so a switch now puts N session GET/SUBSCRIBE pairs plus M per-pane pairs on the critical path of the switch itself.

That is the wrong place for it precisely BECAUSE of what this epic is for: the whole point of the roster is fast, frequent session switching. Making the switch pay for the roster's freshness up front is self-defeating.

FIX: move the sweep to just after the first paint completes, so the new session renders immediately and peer state fills in behind it. The zones already tolerate arriving late — zone 1 holds at zero rows until the first full fold, and zone 3 renders nothing until a roster entry exists.

Not urgent: correctness is unaffected and the frames are small. It becomes user-visible when the session count is high, which is exactly the population this feature targets.
acceptance_criteria: The peer sweep is issued after the first paint on both bootstrap and session switch; a switch's time-to-first-paint does not scale with the number of peer sessions or their panes.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-16 on branch fix/peer-sweep-after-first-paint. PR: https://github.com/phall1/phux/pull/484

DESIGN. The sweep is carried from bootstrap to the ADR-0029 §2 drain — the single place the recv arm paints per batch — by a new 'peer_sweep_pending' flag in main_loop. Deferring to the drain rather than to a paint (drained.level != None) is deliberate: a batch that paints nothing still means the burst is drained, and gating on a paint that a quiet attach may never produce would strand the roster empty for the whole session. The in-loop session-graph sweep clears the flag when it fires in the same batch, because it is the same call against a fresher graph; the send-once 'subscribed' set dedupes the SUBSCRIBE half but nothing dedupes the GET. The per-pane agent sweep needed no deferral of its own — it hangs off these layout replies, so it lands later by construction. One flag covers bootstrap AND session switch because a switch re-enters main_loop through the same bootstrap.

TEST, and the trap it exposed. New e2e crates/phux/tests/fleet_sidebar_e2e.rs, registered in the justfile e2e recipe (just e2e-lane-check requires that of every #[ignore]d e2e binary).

The assertion is the peer's state HISTOGRAM ('!1'), not its roster row, and the first draft got this wrong. session_roster deliberately gives an undescribed peer a row with zero counts — 'this space exists' is the roster's whole job — so a row-level assertion passes against a client that never swept at all. Watched an early draft do exactly that with BOTH sweeps stubbed out. Only the counts require the peer's fetched layout plus its panes' fetched agent records, which is the chain this bead moved.

Test setup notes for whoever touches this next: no JSON surface exposes a session id (ls, status, snapshot all omit it), so the test does not hardcode 'the peer is session 2'. It runs a headless 'phux spawn --target @<peer pane>', which resolves the owning session itself and persists the peer's layout under the right key, then scans candidate ids to confirm a layout naming that pane exists. A plain attach does NOT persist a layout — persistence needs a layout mutation — which is why the spawn is there.

VERIFIED TO DISCRIMINATE, not assumed to: passes against the pre-deferral driver, passes against the deferred one, fails when the deferred send alone is stubbed. That last run settled a real question — the in-loop graph sweep does NOT happen to cover a plain attach, so this send is load-bearing rather than a redundant second path.

NOT MEASURED. The acceptance line 'a switch time-to-first-paint does not scale with the number of peer sessions or their panes' is satisfied structurally (no peer frame is sent before the drain) and is not asserted as a wall-clock bound. A timing assertion on a shared runner would be a flake generator; phux-5wxp.2 was filed this session for exactly that failure mode elsewhere.

WHY A PR RATHER THAN A DIRECT PUSH, which CLAUDE.md would also allow for locally gated maintainer work: main moved three times during this session — release-please's dad855f7, then 51234cd0 (predictive echo), then the phux-jx39 split series through 8504f778 — all from another agent session working in a sibling worktree. Each move costs a rebase plus a full ci-full re-run to keep the local gate honest.

BLOCKED ON A REBASE, 2026-08-16: 024bde0f split attach/driver.rs into a module directory, so this change no longer applies as written — main_loop moved out of the single file this edit targets. The change itself is small and structural (one flag, one deferred call site, one flag-clear) and needs re-applying against the new module layout, not redesigning.
close_reason:
Merged 2026-08-16 via PR #484, rebase-merged as c0c80011. All four required checks green (check 3m35s, test 9m56s, commitlint 15s, classify changes 5s); just ci-full green locally on the same tree (3852 unit + 61 e2e + 3 perf).

Shipping in v0.21.0 (release PR #479), listed under Performance.

The acceptance line about time-to-first-paint not scaling with peer count is met structurally — no peer frame is sent before the repaint drain — and deliberately not asserted as a wall-clock bound; see the notes for why, and phux-5wxp.2 for the flake that argument is grounded in.

title: hub_relay_federation: a dead satellite's panes leak into the aggregate under load
description:
Fifth member of the phux-5wxp load-dependent flake family.

SIGHTING
  crates/phux-server/tests/hub_relay_federation.rs:727
  aggregated_list_merges_local_and_satellite_terminals_and_degrades
  https://github.com/phall1/phux/actions/runs/31900880043/job/95051408327
  Failed on PR #449, whose entire diff is one file in phux-client.

PROVEN NOT CAUSED BY THE BRANCH
  `cargo tree -p phux-server` contains ZERO occurrences of phux-client, and the
  test references phux_client zero times. A phux-client change cannot reach
  phux-server. This is not the usual "looks unrelated" inference -- there is no
  edge in the graph.

SYMPTOM
  The assertion is 'dead satellite must contribute no panes'. The snapshot
  contained one:
    TerminalInfo { id: Satellite { host: SatelliteHost("down"), id: 1 }, ... }
  alongside the expected Local and SatelliteHost("sat") panes. So the hub
  aggregated a pane from the satellite the test deliberately left unreachable.

SHAPE
  The test polls the aggregate in a loop with sleep(100ms) until the live
  satellite's pane appears, then asserts on that snapshot. Two candidate
  mechanisms, and they are distinguishable:
   a) the hub had not yet marked "down" unreachable when the snapshot was
      taken, so its entry was still being served from a pre-failure cache --
      i.e. the poll exits on the LIVE satellite's arrival, which says nothing
      about whether the DEAD one has been reaped yet. The loop's exit condition
      does not cover the thing the next assertion tests. That is taxonomy shape
      3 (the barrier does not prove what the assertion needs).
   b) a genuine ordering bug where a dead satellite's relayed panes are not
      evicted from the aggregate.
  (a) is much more likely given the loop structure, and would make this a test
  defect rather than a product one. Check whether the hub exposes an
  observable "satellite marked down" signal to gate on instead -- per the
  epic's shape-3 note, the correct barrier is a following operation whose
  result proves the state transition already happened.

NOTE: nextest retries mask this class on main. See phux-501l, which was failing
on main for an unknown period behind TRY 1 FAIL / TRY 2 PASS before anyone
looked.
close_reason: hub federation harness now holds the dead satellite's ephemeral port so it cannot be reassigned mid-test

title: last_pane_death_surfaces_its_exit_status: client exits EPIPE instead of the explained TERMINAL_CLOSED ending
description:
New member of the phux-5wxp flake family, sighted on PR #448 (a workflow/docs-only branch that touches zero Rust, so the branch under test cannot be the cause -- consistent with the rest of the family).

SIGHTING
  crates/phux/tests/failure_ux_e2e.rs:570 last_pane_death_surfaces_its_exit_status
  https://github.com/phall1/phux/actions/runs/31892291744/job/95030285613
  Failed 3/3 nextest retries (TRY 3 FAIL), so it is not a single-shot blip.
  main was green on the same lane 10 minutes earlier (41c032ca, run 31891834392).

SYMPTOM -- and note it does NOT match any of the four taxonomy shapes cleanly
  The client exits NON-ZERO instead of ending as explained:
    phux: attach failed: attach loop io error: Broken pipe (os error 32)
  Expected: the seed pane's `exit 7` rides TERMINAL_CLOSED to the client, which
  exits 0 and prints "the last pane exited 7".

WHY IT IS ITS OWN SHAPE
  Shape 2 in the taxonomy ("pane dies before the collection window closes")
  surfaces as an 'early eof' on a read. This is EPIPE, which is a WRITE to a
  socket the peer has already closed. The test is *about* the last pane dying,
  so the server self-exit is expected and correct here -- the defect is that
  the client's attach loop treats a post-close EPIPE as a hard io failure
  rather than as the normal end of an ended session. That looks like a real
  ordering bug in the client shutdown path, not a test timing bet: the client
  must drain TERMINAL_CLOSED before the socket dies, and nothing appears to
  guarantee that ordering.

BEFORE DIAGNOSING AS SCHEDULING (per the epic's standing instruction)
  Run the tailscale probe: PHUX_TAILSCALE=/nonexistent/tailscale. It has
  already explained one member of this family. Note this sighting was on a CI
  nix devshell with no tailscale, which is the configuration the agent_events
  member was GREEN in -- so if the probe does not flip it, that is itself a
  signal this is a different cause.

NOTE ON SCOPE
  Found while repairing the release pipeline (#446, #448). Deliberately not
  fixed there: a client shutdown race is not a drive-by inside a release PR.
notes:
CORRECTION after checking main directly: main is NOT clean. On run 31891834392 (41c032ca) this test failed TRY 1 and passed TRY 2 -- the run went green only because nextest retried it. So the defect is present on main and is being masked by the retry policy, not confined to any branch. On PR #448's runners it failed 6/6 across two independent runs, which suggests the race is load- or runner-dependent in how reliably it reproduces, not in whether it exists.
MECHANISM HYPOTHESIS + ENTRY POINTS (for whoever picks this up)

The EPIPE is a WRITE to an already-closed socket, and the sequence that makes
that inevitable is:
  1. seed shell runs 'exit 7'
  2. server closes the terminal, emits TERMINAL_CLOSED
  3. that was the LAST pane, so the server reaps the session and self-exits,
     closing the UDS
  4. the client, still processing TERMINAL_CLOSED, writes one more frame and
     hits EPIPE

Step 4 is the bug: on the last-pane path there is nothing sequencing the
client's final write against the server's self-exit, so whether the run is
green depends purely on which side wins the race.

Note the error vocabulary already distinguishes this class and this case falls
through the gap: crates/phux-client/src/attach/outcome.rs has
AttachError::Disconnected -- 'The server closed the connection without sending
DETACHED. Distinguished from a clean detach so the CLI can surface server went
away vs you detached.' A read-side EOF lands there. A WRITE-side EPIPE instead
collapses onto AttachError::Io (outcome.rs:32), which the CLI prints as a hard
failure. An ended session is not an IO failure.

Writes are not in the driver -- 'grep -n send_frame|write_frame driver.rs'
returns 0. They go through crates/phux-client/src/attach/connection.rs, where
every write maps errors with AttachError::Io (lines 1051, 1053, 1078, 1099,
1133). That mapping is where a post-close EPIPE should be reclassified, but the
ordering fix is the better one: do not write at all once the session has ended.

The expected ending is crates/phux/src/commands/attach.rs:1185
  'phux: session ended: the last pane exited N'
RUN DATA after attempting a fix (peer-gone tolerance on the 5 inbound-arm writes). The fix is NOT demonstrated to work -- do not assume it is fixed:

  #448 run 1      no client fix    3/3 FAIL
  #448 run 2      no client fix    3/3 FAIL
  #448 re-run     no client fix    PASS
  #449 run 1      WITH fix         2/3 FAIL
  #449 runs 2-6   WITH fix         5 x PASS (first try)

The fix is present in a run that still failed twice, and absent from a run that
passed. That is a flake firing in BURSTS ON PARTICULAR RUNNERS, not a fix
taking effect. Five consecutive green runs prove nothing against that baseline
-- any future 'it passed N times' claim needs the same scrutiny.

NOT REPRODUCIBLE ON macOS: 25 consecutive runs with 12 CPU hogs saturating the
box, 0 failures. This hardware does not lose the race. Only CI's Linux does, so
CI is the only instrument -- and each measurement costs ~9 minutes.

DIAGNOSTIC NOW IN PLACE (PR #449). Socket write errors name the frame they were
carrying: 'sending frame type 0xNN: Broken pipe'. This exists because the
message was previously identical for all ~30 client->server writes, which is
what allowed two wrong diagnoses. NEXT OCCURRENCE WILL NAME ITS OWN ORIGIN.

CRITICALLY -- the diagnostic also tests a hypothesis nobody has checked: it
wraps ONLY UdsWriter::send. If a failing run shows a bare 'Broken pipe' with NO
frame named, the EPIPE is not a socket write at all (stdout? terminal ioctl?
AttachError::Io covers those too per its own doc comment) and this whole family
of fixes is aimed at the wrong thing. Check that FIRST on the next sighting.

REJECTED APPROACH, do not retry without reading this: pushing the tolerance
down into Connection::send would cover all ~30 sites at once, but Connection is
used by phux-mcp, send_keys, snapshot, watch, layout_ops, agent_wait and state.
Swallowing write errors there would make 'phux send-keys' report success on a
keystroke that never left the process.
GROOMED 2026-08-16 (autonomous run): PARKED deliberately. The frame-naming diagnostic (PR #449) is in place and the next CI sighting will name the origin frame or falsify the socket-write hypothesis. macOS cannot reproduce (25/25 green under saturation); each CI measurement costs ~9min. Correct move is to wait for one more named sighting before spending another fix cycle. Do not attempt blind fixes.

title: Parallel branches can silently claim the same ADR number or manifest key
description:
Third occurrence of the same failure shape in three waves.

Wave 3: army/w3-render-newtype and army/w3-chrome-config independently created two DIFFERENT ADR-0086 files. Wave 2: phux-w7z2.21 reintroduced the visible-working manifest key that phux-w7z2.18 had just deleted.

In both cases git reported ZERO conflicts, because the branches touched disjoint files or disjoint lines. Nothing in the repo catches it: just docs-check validates frontmatter, status vocabulary and links WITHIN a tree, and has no cross-branch view at all. It was caught both times only because a human orchestrator happened to be reading the reports.

This is a structural hazard of the multi-agent fan-out that CONTRIBUTING already documents, not bad luck, and it gets more likely as wave size grows.

Note the honest difficulty: a per-branch CI gate cannot see sibling branches, so 'add a check' is not obviously the fix. Candidate directions, none yet chosen:
- an allocation convention (reserve the number in a tracked file before writing the ADR)
- an integration-time sweep the integrator runs across all candidate branches
- a non-colliding identifier scheme for ADRs (the ADR number is a human-facing citation, so this trades one cost for another)
- accept it and make the conflict LOUD rather than silent: if every ADR added a row to a single index file at a deterministic sort position, a same-number collision becomes an ordinary textual conflict. ADR/README.md already nearly does this; wave 3's two branches DID textually conflict on the row after 0085.

The last option is the cheapest and may already be most of the answer.
notes:
GROOMED 2026-08-16 (autonomous run): decision is the bead's option 4 — make the collision LOUD, not gated. Every ADR must add its row to ADR/README.md's index at the deterministic sort position (same for manifest keys if a registry file exists); add a docs-check that every ADR/NNNN-*.md has exactly one index row and index numbers are unique/dense, so a same-number claim on two branches becomes an ordinary textual conflict at integration. No cross-branch CI attempted.
SEQUEL 2026-08-17: the gate landed, and one batch later the SAME collision shape appeared on a surface it does not cover — two parallel branches both claimed spec CHANGELOG row 0.8.0-draft.4. Filed as its own bead to extend the gate family to CHANGELOG version rows. This validates the bead's premise (it is a structural hazard of fan-out, recurring, not bad luck) and shows the defense needs to cover every hand-allocated sequential identifier, not just ADR numbers.
close_reason: new adr-index-sync docs gate pins every ADR to one sorted ADR/README.md row so number collisions conflict loudly

title: Make remote pairing attempts diagnosable at default log level
description: A physical iPhone QR pairing failure could not be correlated on the server. The default log proves listeners started but successful WebSocket admission is DEBUG-only and source/device are omitted; TLS/upgrade/auth failures collapse into generic accept failed. Add privacy-safe stage and peer context for TLS WebSocket pairing attempts at the default operational level, including generic token rejection and authenticated admission, without ever logging credentials or distinguishing secret validity to the client. Bound log-spam risk and preserve the generic 401 response.

title: [epic] The load-dependent test-flake family: one taxonomy, four known members
description:
Four distinct load-dependent flakes have been sighted in one day, by five different agents, none of them caused by the branch under test. Filing them individually was making every agent re-derive the same taxonomy, so this epic holds it once.

MEMBERS:
  phux-m64c  agent_detect::a_declared_kind_never_gains_a_state_derived_from_a_different_occupant
  phux-285q  phux_3uv_acked_incremental::acked_incremental_converges_and_seq_is_monotonic (sighted twice)
  (new)      terminal_actor::tests::pane_kill_lets_foreground_process_flush_before_death
  CLOSED     the agent_events cluster -- root-caused and fixed, see below

THE ONE THAT WAS SOLVED, because it is the template. agent_events looked like a load flake for weeks. The actual cause was ENVIRONMENTAL: phux_config::overlay::detect() shells out to the tailscale CLI when it is on PATH, stalling server startup ~286ms BEFORE the accept loop runs, which ate the head start a seed's sleep was betting on. CI's nix devshell has no tailscale, so it degraded to a fast route probe and was green there while failing on developer machines. Proven with PHUX_TAILSCALE=/nonexistent/tailscale flipping it deterministically. Fixed by replacing the timing bets with real barriers; the underlying startup cost is phux-c6g6.

SO: BEFORE DIAGNOSING ANY MEMBER AS A SCHEDULING FLAKE, run the tailscale probe. It is one command and it has already explained one of these.

THE TAXONOMY -- four shapes, and they are not interchangeable:
1. The pane dies too early. A seed's 'sleep N' expires before the assertion runs.
2. The pane dies before the collection window CLOSES. A short seed sleep racing a 15s WIRE_RECV_TIMEOUT. Surfaces as a confusing 'early eof' rather than anything about the feature, because the pane exits, the session is reaped, and the server self-exits.
3. The event fires before the observer is registered. CRITICAL SUBTLETY: a barrier anchored on the client having SENT a frame is INSUFFICIENT when that frame gets no reply. SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS and SUBSCRIBE_METADATA have no reply frames, so send_frame returning proves only that bytes left the client. The correct barrier is a FOLLOWING command whose CommandResult you wait for -- the per-connection frame loop handles frames in order, so that result proves the subscribe ahead of it is installed. Reference idiom: crates/phux-server/tests/agent_asked.rs.
4. The probe perturbs what it measures. Polling liveness by opening connections to a server whose idle timeout is under test resets that timeout on every poll. Gate on something non-perturbing -- socket-file absence proved better than a connect probe, and is the stronger assertion anyway since the unlink only happens on the graceful shutdown path.

Two tests in the SAME FILE have had different shapes. Do not pattern-match.

RULES FOR ANY MEMBER:
- Never lengthen a sleep. That is a slower flake, not a fix.
- Never poll by connecting to the thing whose lifetime you are measuring.
- Prove the fix with 20+ repetitions UNDER FULL PARALLEL LOAD, not in isolation -- isolation hides every flake in this family.
- If the cause is ambient, decide between making the test independent or making it SKIP with a stated reason, and say which in the test's doc comment. A test that passes only on CI trains people to ignore red output, which is how the real failures here get missed.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE NOW THAN LAST WEEK: main accepts direct pushes from maintainers with local 'just ci-full' as the only gate. A flake that aborts a local run is no longer a nuisance -- per phux-yb1m it can abort 'just ci' before the doc and deny gates ever execute, which is exactly how two branches reached CI with rustdoc errors after a locally-green run.
notes:
SHAPE 5, found by phux-m64c and materially different from the other four: ONE DEADLINE PAYING FOR TWO UNRELATED THINGS.

The test's deadline covered both the thing under test (the detector converging -- bounded, fast) AND an ambient precondition (the seed pane's child process getting scheduled at all -- unbounded, not the subject). Caught in a trace:

  T+0.00s  TerminalActor started
  T+0.50s  agent-detect: identified kind=claude
  T+0.81s  agent-detect: derived matched=<none>   <- blank grid, fail-safe idle
  T+7.77s  pty read n=7                           <- the pane's FIRST byte
  T+8.00s  test gives up

Server, actor and detector were all correct and on time. The freshly spawned /bin/sh did not run for 7.8 SECONDS under ambient load. The detector scanned a blank grid, published the fail-safe idle, and then had nothing to re-scan -- a permission dialog paints once, so wants_screen is false forever after.

THE TELL: failures came in BURSTS that tracked ambient machine load, and never appeared under synthetic CPU-only load. A flake that clusters rather than scattering is usually waiting on something the machine schedules, not something the code races.

THE FIX SHAPE: make the pane signal that it has painted (a shell BUILTIN like ': > path' -- forks nothing, so the process group leader and agent identification are untouched), and start the deadline from there. The deadline value is UNCHANGED; it now measures only the subject. A pane that never paints fails against its own separate, generous budget with a message naming the environment. That is strictly better than raising the number, which would have hidden a real detector regression behind an ambient one.

HOW TO PROVE A FIX OF THIS SHAPE -- borrow this, it is the best technique produced today. Prepend 'sleep 9' to the fake agent to make the starved child DETERMINISTIC, then run the counterfactual: 8 of 9 cases failed on pre-fix main, 9 of 9 passed with the barrier. That converts an unreproducible flake into a mutation test.

ALSO ESTABLISHED: the tailscale hypothesis was RULED OUT for this member, with numbers -- 20/20 pass with PHUX_TAILSCALE=/nonexistent and 20/20 without. Run the probe, but do not assume the last root cause is this root cause. Startup cost was real (~130ms) and simply not the delayed party, since the deadline starts after socket connect.

RESIDUAL, deliberately not changed by m64c: a_kind_change_never_leaves_a_stale_kind_beside_a_live_state needs codex's paint inside DEPARTURE_DEADLINE. Much less exposed -- codex is exec'd from an already-running, already-scheduled process rather than posix_spawn'ed cold -- so it was left rather than widen the blast radius. Worth revisiting if it ever fires.

NEW SIGHTING for the family: hub::link::tests::ssh_transport_drains_stderr_past_the_pipe_buffer_without_stalling failed once at 10.15s against a 10s deadline, despite nextest.toml already reserving threads for that cluster. That is shape 5 too on its face -- a deadline covering ssh process startup as well as the drain being tested.
WAVE-THREE PASS 2026-08-15 (branch army/w3-test-health). All four open members fixed; details live in each child. Three things this epic should absorb.

1. A SIXTH SHAPE, and it is the one that most deserves to be called out because the taxonomy currently has no slot for it: THE WINDOW BELONGS TO THE PRODUCT, NOT THE TEST. phux-axos's remaining exposure is that the assertion requires a foreground process to run its SIGHUP handler inside PANE_KILL_GRACE = 500ms -- a shipped constant. No barrier can fence a window the product itself defines, and lengthening it changes shipped behavior to suit a test. The only honest moves are runner-level isolation (`threads-required = 'num-cpus'`, already applied) and a failure message that names the environment. Distinguishing this from shape 5 matters: shape 5 says "the deadline is paying for something that is not the subject, so split it", and if you try that here you find there is nothing to split -- the ambient cost is INSIDE the subject's window. When you meet one of these, say so and stop; do not keep looking for a barrier.

2. THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS A DIAGNOSTIC TOOL, not just a proof. phux-m64c introduced it as "prove the fix". Used on phux-dnhf it did something better: prepending `sleep 9` to the fake agent reproduced the integrator's recorded failure string CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER, poll count and all ("phux: wait timed out after 34 polls"). That is what separates "I fixed a flake of this shape" from "I fixed THE flake that was reported", and it is cheap. Run it before writing the fix, not only after.

3. WHERE THE FAMILY'S EVIDENCE ALREADY LIVES. `.config/nextest.toml` is not runner config, it is a lab notebook -- it already carries the measured root-cause analysis for pane_kill, agent_detect and the ssh_transport cluster, including which mitigations were tried and rejected (`pty-serial` only serialises group members against EACH OTHER, so it does nothing for load coming from the rest of the pool). Two of this wave's beads asked questions that file already answers. Read it before diagnosing any member.

METHOD NOTE FOR FUTURE MEMBERS: the repetition command this wave was handed, `cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'test(name)' --test-threads 1 -j1`, IS INVALID -- nextest rejects it with "the argument '--test-threads <N>' cannot be used multiple times" because `-j` is an alias for `--test-threads`. It fails fast and loudly on a bare run, but inside a loop whose output is grepped for PASS/FAIL it produces a silent 20-for-20 of nothing. Drop the `-j1`.

NEW SIGHTING filed as phux-5wxp.1: spatial_e2e::spatial_cli_persists_topology_and_preserves_attached_focus, FLAKY 2/3 in a clean `just e2e` on an unrelated branch under fleet load. Worth noting that the lane's `--retries=2` turns this into a FLAKY line rather than a failure, so it is invisible to anything reading exit codes.

MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE USED, for reuse: 24 synthetic CPU burners alongside the existing fleet load gave a sustained load average of 66 -> 158 on this box. Under that, 20 consecutive serial runs of all four members: 80/80 green. Four full-parallel `cargo nextest run --workspace` runs (3773 tests), one at load 171 and one at 121-168: green, with zero leaked servers.

NEW TAXONOMY SHAPE ADDED 2026-08-17, from phux-vbnr: 'THE FIXTURE'S PRECONDITION IS A LEASE, NOT A RESERVATION.' Distinct from shape 3 (barrier does not prove what the assertion needs) — in this shape the barrier is SOUND and the assertion never depended on ordering; the fixture handed out a resource it did not hold. Concretely: free_port() binds 127.0.0.1:0, reads the number, and DROPS the listener, so the number is leased not reserved; with no .await between spawn_satellite() and the next free_port(), the spawned task has not run and the live port is STILL UNBOUND when the dead one is drawn, so the kernel can hand back the same number and ONE satellite answers under TWO names. Diagnostic signature: two entries that should be distinct carry the SAME id and the SAME shape (here both 80x24, pane id 1), and the failure lands on the FIRST loop iteration with no backoff — a genuine ordering flake would need at least one retry. Anywhere a test draws a port/path/name this way is a candidate. NOTE both of the bead's original candidate mechanisms were RULED OUT with evidence: handle_get_state_federated has no cache, queries every link live per request, and tags panes from relay.host() never from the response, so a 'down'-tagged pane REQUIRES a successful dial and cannot come from a stale cache; and the aggregation code is correct, so there is no product defect.

title: agent start has a third hand-rolled APPLY_INPUT that does not know about InputNotWritten
description:
Found while verifying phux-w7z2.53 (which turned out to be already-done). Not covered by phux-w7z2.60, which introduced the distinction this file is now blind to.

crates/phux/src/commands/agent/start.rs carries its own hand-rolled Command::ApplyInput builder (apply_input()) with its own classification function (submit_error()), used by phux agent start. It is the THIRD implementation of acknowledged input delivery. The canonical one is phux-client's agent_prompt::apply_input_once plus the shared classify()/ApplyVerdict; ask.rs::deliver_answer was already folded onto it in 8d06829c (#410).

THE DEFECT: submit_error()'s catch-all _ arm treats any unrecognised ErrorCode as wrote_nothing: false. phux-w7z2.60 (363cb2eb) added ErrorCode::InputNotWritten = 207 for paths PROVEN never to have written a byte, where resending is safe. start.rs does not know that code, so it buckets a provably-not-written failure with the genuinely ambiguous ones.

The direction of the error is CONSERVATIVE, which is why this is P2 rather than P1: the user is told not to resend when resending would in fact have been safe. That loses the recovery path w7z2.60 exists to provide, but it cannot cause double-typed input. Do not 'fix' it in the optimistic direction without proving each path, or the failure becomes harmful instead of merely unhelpful.

THE REAL FIX is not to add a 207 arm to submit_error(). It is to fold start.rs onto the shared classify()/ApplyVerdict the other two verbs already use, so the next error-code addition cannot leave a third reading behind. That is exactly the drift phux-w7z2.53's epic is about; the bead simply named the wrong file, because ask.rs had already been folded before the bead was written.

CHECK WHILE THERE: whether any OTHER caller classifies input-delivery outcomes independently. Two were known; a third was found by accident. A grep for Command::ApplyInput construction sites is the cheap way to find a fourth.

ACCEPTANCE: one classification path for acknowledged input across every verb, or a written statement of why start.rs must differ. If they merge, w7z2.60's not-written/unknown asymmetry must survive -- if a path cannot be PROVEN never to have written, it stays unknown.
close_reason: Removed agent start hand-rolled APPLY_INPUT construction and ErrorCode table. It now uses phux-client agent_prompt::apply_input_once/ApplyVerdict, so INPUT_NOT_WRITTEN is proven non-delivery and unwinds the provisional bind while unknown outcomes retain it. Audit found no fourth production client constructor. just ci-full passed; integrated and pushed.

title: just ci runs doc after test, so any test flake silently skips the rustdoc gate
description:
Found by the integrator after it bit twice in one session.

CI's 'check' job runs RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --all-features. That gate is NOT covered by 'cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings', which is what everyone runs and what this repo's own agent docs name as authoritative. Two branches passed full-workspace clippy, fmt-check, docs-check and their test suites locally and then failed CI on it:

  phux-j1zj    -- four private-intra-doc-links errors: public docs on telemetry linking [LOG_ROTATE_THRESHOLD_BYTES] and [file_writer], both private items.
  phux-w7z2.59 -- identical defect, [MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_CLIENT].

Both fixed at integration by demoting the links to plain code spans.

THE STRUCTURAL PART, which is the actual bug: 'just ci' DOES include the doc recipe, so in principle a local run covers it. But the recipe order is

  ci: fmt-check lint docs-check formula-check font-check e2e-lane-check zig-pin-check install-surface-check test deny doc

-- 'doc' runs AFTER 'test'. just aborts on the first failing recipe, so on any machine where a test flakes, the doc gate NEVER EXECUTES. This repo currently has several load-dependent flakes, so that is not hypothetical: it is exactly how the j1zj failure reached CI despite a local 'just ci'.

The same shape produced the other local-green/CI-red failure this session: a dead_code allow placed on one enum variant, correct on macOS and failing on Linux where the other variant is the unconstructed one. Different mechanism, same class -- a gate the author did not think to run, or could not run, on their machine.

FIX OPTIONS, weigh them:
1. Move the cheap static gates (doc, deny) BEFORE 'test' in the ci recipe. Costs nothing on a green run and means a flaky test can no longer mask them. Simplest, and probably right.
2. Add the rustdoc invocation to whatever the docs name as the authoritative local lint, so 'clippy + doc' are always run as a pair.
3. Both.

ALSO WORTH DOING: private-intra-doc-links is a rustdoc lint that could be enabled at the crate level so it surfaces in ordinary 'cargo doc' rather than only under RUSTDOCFLAGS in CI.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE IS DRIFT, NOT DESIGN -- which makes the fix a restoration rather than an invention. The ci recipe's OWN COMMENT already documented the intended order: 'mirrors ci.yml's check job step for step -- fmt, clippy, rustdoc, deny, docs-check, ...'. The recipe line had drifted away from its own comment so deny and doc sat after test. ci.yml's real check job confirms the documented order: fmt, clippy, doc, deny share one build, in a job SEPARATE from test.

Fixed on branch army/yqvj-ci-gate-order:
  old: fmt-check lint docs-check formula-check font-check e2e-lane-check zig-pin-check install-surface-check skill-contract test deny doc
  new: fmt-check lint doc deny docs-check formula-check font-check e2e-lane-check zig-pin-check install-surface-check skill-contract test

Comment added stating the invariant (test-independent gates precede test) and citing this bead so it cannot drift again silently. Incidental win: lint and doc are both --all-features, so making them adjacent removes a second full all-features rebuild the old ordering forced.

ci-full and precommit checked and NOT affected. ci-full runs the now-fixed ci in full before the real-server lanes. precommit is a deliberately partial fast loop that never included doc/deny by design ('run this until clean, then just ci once as the final gate'), so it is not the same shape. No genuine inter-recipe dependency was broken -- doc and deny do not consume test output.

SECOND HALF ALSO DONE: #![deny(rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links)] added to the 9 crates already carrying #![deny(missing_docs)]. The lint is warn-by-default, so it was already firing silently under plain cargo doc; the crate-level deny makes it fail loudly there rather than only under CI's RUSTDOCFLAGS. Scoped to this ONE lint rather than the rustdoc::all group, since it is the only one that has bitten this repo and denying the group risked surfacing unrelated pre-existing noise. Binary and test-scaffolding crates left alone, matching their existing opt-out of the missing_docs regime.

Verified both ways: RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc clean, AND plain cargo doc clean, confirming the new deny breaks nothing today.

NOTE the first 'just ci' run hit a live instance of exactly this bug class -- phux_3uv_acked_incremental failed under load and aborted the run before doc/deny were reached. Filed as phux-285q.
close_reason:
Landed on main as 685cb5a0 'fix(ci): run doc and deny before test so a flaky test can't mask them'.

ROOT CAUSE WAS DRIFT, NOT DESIGN. The ci recipe's own comment already documented the intended order -- 'mirrors ci.yml's check job step for step: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, deny, docs-check, ...' -- while the recipe line had drifted so deny and doc sat after test. ci.yml's real check job confirms it: fmt, clippy, doc, deny share one build in a job SEPARATE from test. So the fix is a restoration to what the file already claimed, with the invariant now written down and this bead cited so it cannot drift silently again.

Incidental win: lint and doc are both --all-features, so making them adjacent removes a second full all-features rebuild the old ordering forced.

ci-full and precommit checked and NOT affected. precommit never included doc/deny by design ('run this until clean, then just ci once as the final gate'). No genuine inter-recipe dependency was broken.

SECOND HALF, the durable part: #![deny(rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links)] added to the 9 crates already carrying #![deny(missing_docs)]. That lint is warn-by-default, so it was ALREADY firing silently under plain cargo doc; the deny makes it fail where developers actually look rather than only under CI's RUSTDOCFLAGS. Scoped to that one lint rather than the rustdoc::all group, since it is the only one that has bitten this repo and the group would surface unrelated pre-existing noise. Verified clean both with and without the CI flags.

The agent's first 'just ci' run hit a live instance of exactly this bug class -- phux_3uv_acked_incremental failed under load and aborted before doc/deny were reached. Filed as phux-285q, now under the flake epic phux-5wxp.

This mattered more than its P2 suggests: main accepts direct pushes with local just ci-full as the only gate, so a flake that aborts a local run no longer merely annoys -- it silently skips gates that used to be caught by required checks. Two branches reached CI with private-intra-doc-links errors after locally-green runs, which is how the bug was found.

title: PHUX_NO_AUTO_LISTEN is a dead kill switch, and every server start shells out to tailscale twice
description:
Found while diagnosing the agent_events environment dependence (army/agent-events-env). Not a test problem -- a production startup-cost and dead-switch bug.

crates/phux-server/src/runtime/mod.rs:1101, auto_overlay_addr passes &phux_config::overlay::detect() as an ARGUMENT to auto_overlay_addr_from. Rust evaluates arguments eagerly, so detect() runs BEFORE the 'disabled' and '!default_profile' gates inside that function ever look at it and discard the result.

TWO CONSEQUENCES:

1. PHUX_NO_AUTO_LISTEN does not do what its name says. Setting it does not avoid the detection cost; it only discards the answer afterwards. Confirmed empirically -- the failing test still failed with the variable set. A kill switch that does not kill is worse than no kill switch, because someone will set it, measure nothing, and conclude the cost is elsewhere.

2. Every phux server start on a machine with the tailscale CLI on PATH pays TWO synchronous shell-outs for ONE answer -- once for the WS listen address and once for QUIC. phux_config::overlay::detect() shells out to 'tailscale ip -4' (crates/phux-config/src/overlay.rs:25-72). Measured at 143ms per call on the reporting host, so ~286ms of the server's startup, on the current-thread runtime, BEFORE the accept loop runs. CI never sees it because the nix devshell has no tailscale binary and detect() degrades to a fast UDP CGNAT route probe.

That stall is what made agent_events fail on developer machines and pass on CI: the server pre-seeds the pane (starting the seed's clock) and only THEN computes the listen addresses, so the pane spoke ~130ms before anyone was listening. Those tests are fixed independently on army/agent-events-env by replacing the timing bet with a real barrier -- they no longer depend on this either way. This bead is the underlying cost.

FIX, self-contained: short-circuit the disabled / non-default-profile gates BEFORE calling detect(), and compute it once for both ports rather than twice. Deliberately left out of the test branch because it would not have fixed those tests (they run in the default profile with no env var set) and mixing the two would have muddied a clean test-only diff.

WORTH CHECKING WHILE THERE: whether the detection belongs before the pre-seed at all. runtime/mod.rs:965-985 pre-seeds the pane and then computes listen addresses; doing the network detection first, or moving it off the startup path entirely, would remove a class of startup-order surprise rather than just this instance.
notes:
CORROBORATION, plus a correction to how deterministic the symptom is.

I observed agent_events::subscribed_client_receives_command_and_cwd_events failing DETERMINISTICALLY in isolation on clean origin/main from my shell. A second agent, in its own worktree, saw the SAME test PASS in isolation on clean main, and instead saw agent_events fail 3/10 under load on its branch and 1/10 on clean main -- with a DIFFERENT panic site: agent_events.rs:108 'first server-to-client frame must be ATTACHED', not the line 262 command_started assertion I hit.

Both are true and both point AT this bead rather than against it: whether overlay::detect() stalls depends on whether the tailscale CLI is on PATH in that shell/worktree, so one defect presents as deterministic in one environment and load-dependent in another. That is the signature of an environmental timing dependency, and it is why the fix on army/agent-events-env replaces the timing bet with a barrier instead of tuning a number.

TWO FOLLOW-ONS:

1. The agent_events.rs:108 panic is a DIFFERENT failure point from line 262 and may be a second timing bet, on the ATTACH handshake itself. army/agent-events-env reports barrier-fixing all three tests in the file; whoever integrates it should confirm the :108 shape is covered, and give it its own barrier if not.

2. subscribed_client_receives_title_bell_and_pane_closed_events shares the shape and exposure -- flagged independently by both agents.

Nobody should describe that test as 'deterministically failing' without naming the environment: deterministic where tailscale is on PATH, load-dependent where it is not.
close_reason:
Landed on main as 14429d94 'fix(server): gate overlay detection before it runs, and run it once'.

The eager-argument bug is now structurally impossible rather than merely avoided: auto_overlay_addr was split into a pure auto_overlay_gate_open(disabled, default_profile) -> bool that calls nothing, and resolve_auto_overlay_ip(gate_open, detect: impl FnOnce() -> Vec<IpAddr>) that invokes detect ONLY when the gate is open. Passing detection as a closure rather than a value is what makes the fix hold -- the old code passed &detect() as an argument, which Rust evaluates before the callee's 'if disabled { return None }' ever runs.

Also memoized: one detect() per server start, shared by the WS and QUIC ports, and skipped entirely when explicit overrides already answer both. Previously twice per start.

MEASURED, A/B on a host with tailscale on PATH: the old eager double-call took 203.5ms; the new gated path with the gate closed takes 42ns. Individual 'tailscale ip -4' invocations measured 60-220ms, consistent with the ~143ms this bead reported.

PROVEN, not reasoned: a new test closed_gate_never_calls_detect spies on the closure passed to the real production seam and asserts it is never invoked when the gate is closed. Companions cover the open-gate mirror case and the disable-env gate directly. The wall-clock A/B was run and then DELETED before committing, since a timing test would violate this repo's no-wall-clock test discipline -- measure to learn, do not commit the measurement.

Docs needed no change: PHUX_NO_AUTO_LISTEN is absent from the CLI reference and its ENVIRONMENT block, and ADR-0081 and docs/operations.md already described the 'suppresses it entirely' behaviour this fix now actually delivers.

RECOMMENDED FOLLOW-UP, not implemented and worth its own bead if anyone wants it: move the overlay lookup BEFORE the pre-seed, or run it via spawn_blocking in parallel. runtime/mod.rs currently pre-seeds the pane, then resolves listen addresses, then accepts -- so any cost there sits between 'session exists' and 'server reachable', which is precisely the startup-order window that produced the agent_events flake this bead spun out of. Caching the overlay address across restarts is a further option, since it rarely changes.

title: The server never emits DETACHED with a reason on shutdown or fatal-error close
description:
Split out of phux-l83x (PR #435), which gave DETACHED its reason and message fields and wired the reference server to state REQUESTED and SESSION_KILLED. The remaining half was deliberately NOT done, and proto.md 7.2 now carries a 'partial' impl-status marker saying so rather than leaving the gap silent.

WHAT IS MISSING: the server never emits SERVER_SHUTDOWN, REPLACED, PROTOCOL_ERROR or INTERNAL_ERROR. Shutdown and the eight fatal ERROR-then-close paths in crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs drop the transport with no DETACHED at all.

That matters because of what phux-ijuj changed at 0.7.0-draft.5: ERROR is now non-fatal at the receiver, so a connection ends by DETACHED plus transport close AND BY NOTHING ELSE. A fatal path that closes without a DETACHED gives the consumer an unexplained transport error where the spec promises an explained ending. proto.md 9 is normative about this -- 'a fatal error MUST be followed by DETACHED { reason: PROTOCOL_ERROR } and transport close' -- so this is a conformance gap, not a feature request.

WHY IT WAS NOT SELF-CONTAINED, which is the real content of this bead:

1. crates/phux-client-ffi currently returns BridgeError::protocol('DETACHED arrived outside an active ATTACH phase'). So emitting DETACHED { PROTOCOL_ERROR } on the PRE-HELLO fatal paths would turn a clean version-mismatch refusal into a bridge protocol error -- strictly worse for the consumer than the silent close it replaces. The FFI's phase model has to accept a pre-attach DETACHED first, and that is a consumer-side decision with its own compatibility surface.

2. The shutdown broadcast is best-effort by nature: it races root_token.cancel() against the writer tasks. Sending it reliably means ordering the broadcast ahead of cancellation, or accepting that some consumers get the close without the reason. Decide which, and say so in the spec rather than letting it be incidental.

ACCEPTANCE: either the four reasons are emitted on their paths and 7.2's 'partial' marker is removed, or the marker is amended to state precisely which reasons the reference server will never emit and why. Do not leave 'partial' meaning 'nobody looked yet'.

Note REPLACED depends on role takeover, which is unimplemented -- that one may be legitimately out of scope until takeover exists.
close_reason: Fatal connection endings now emit ordered ERROR then DETACHED(PROTOCOL_ERROR) then close; root cancellation gives live clients a bounded DETACHED(SERVER_SHUTDOWN) drain. The FFI accepts DETACHED before HELLO/ATTACH, and Unix/WebSocket/native tests pin the ordering. just ci-full passed; integrated and pushed.

title: doctor and service now have two legacy-unit predicates; one should own it
description:
Two branches landing in the same queue each produced a way to answer 'is this installed unit running the corrected restart policy', and they answer it differently.

phux-dsg1 rewrote doctor's supervisor_unit_is_legacy to parse actual VALUES (restart_is_failure_only, restart_is_throttled, plus plist/systemd value extraction) instead of substring-matching directive names. That fixed two real false-passes: 'ThrottleInterval 0' and 'Restart=always' next to a stray SuccessfulExit mention both previously read as 'corrected'.

phux-l1yx introduced reconcile_unit, whose Reconcile::Current variant is DEFINED as 'applying the policy patch is a byte no-op'. That is a stronger and more drift-proof formulation: there is no separate predicate to fall out of sync with the generator, because the generator and the reconciler emit the policy block from the same shared launchd_policy_lines()/systemd_policy_lines(), and a test pins reconcile(render(plan)) == Current for both managers.

So the tree will have two predicates for one question. The second is better on the merits -- it cannot drift from the generator by construction, which is exactly the failure mode the first one just got fixed for -- but consolidating is a real design decision, not a rebase chore:

- doctor deliberately keeps its own duplicated path so it can report on units THIS BUILD WOULD NO LONGER GENERATE. That reasoning is documented at legacy_service_unit_path and it is why the duplication exists at all. A reconciler keyed to the current generator may not be able to describe a unit shape the generator no longer emits.
- doctor must not acquire a dependency that makes it fail where it currently warns. Its server-health check is a Warn that exits 0 on purpose (phux-nvi2).
- dsg1 added tests that cross-check supervisor_unit_is_legacy against the REAL render_launchd_plist / render_systemd_unit output, so detection cannot silently drift from generation. Whatever survives must keep that guarantee.

ACCEPTANCE: one predicate owns the question, or a written statement of why two are correct and what keeps them agreeing. If they merge, the surviving one keeps dsg1's value-parsing behaviour and its generator cross-check tests, and doctor's report-on-old-shapes capability is preserved or the loss is explicitly accepted.

Do NOT do this as part of a merge-conflict resolution. Both branches are correct as written; this is follow-up work.
close_reason: Landed on main as 626a82e1 'chore(doctor): keep the legacy-unit predicate, and pin why it must diverge from reconcile'. Outcome was NOT the bead's premise: the two predicates must diverge; the duplication is pinned by a guard test rather than removed.

title: 21 open beads carry neither rc-1.0 nor post-1.0, so the 1.0 cut line is undecidable
description:
The tracker DOES have a release-milestone vocabulary — the labels rc-1.0 and post-1.0 — but it is not applied to everything. Of 89 open/in-progress beads: 35 are post-1.0, 33 are rc-1.0, and 21 carry neither. For those 21 nobody can answer 'is this in 1.0' without re-reading ADR-0071.

The unlabelled set is not incidental. It includes the ENTIRE phux-g60k server-lifecycle epic (bd30, dsg1, gyza, l1yx, nbam, whhd, y1dq, l83y) plus fwwa, w1om, e2c0, l83x, a5xj, j1zj, huhi, x8g4, pw7a, rc7f, ed8j and 7k11. Several of those touch surfaces ADR-0071 point 1 explicitly freezes:

- phux-l83y: phux service install --print fails on unsupported platforms, contradicting ADR-0055. That is CLI grammar and exit-code behaviour, inside the freeze.
- phux-dsg1: doctor's three server-health conditions are mutually exclusive. Consumer-facing verb behaviour.
- phux-gyza: a dev-profile binary installs a unit that hijacks the default profile's label. Documented file/socket locations, inside the freeze.
- phux-fwwa / phux-w1om: missing MCP tools. MCP tool names and arguments are inside the freeze, and a tool that does not exist at 1.0 can only be ADDED later — additive, so these are genuinely deferrable, but that should be a recorded decision rather than an absent label.

ACCEPTANCE: every open bead carries exactly one of rc-1.0 or post-1.0, and the criterion used is written down (proposal: rc-1.0 if it changes a surface ADR-0071 point 1 freezes, or if leaving it makes a frozen surface wrong; post-1.0 otherwise, since additive change stays legal within a major). A docs-check or bd query gate that fails on an unlabelled open bead would keep it true.
notes:
TRIAGE DONE. All 21 unlabelled open beads now carry exactly one of rc-1.0 / post-1.0, and every open bead in the tracker is labelled (verified: 'bd list --status open,in_progress --exclude-label post-1.0,rc-1.0' returns empty).

CRITERION USED, derived from ADR-0071:

rc-1.0 when EITHER
  (a) it changes a surface ADR-0071 point 1 freezes -- CLI grammar, exit codes, --json documents, config schema, action/hook/widget vocabulary, MCP tool names and arguments, documented file and socket locations; OR
  (b) leaving it undone makes one of those surfaces WRONG at the moment of the freeze (a documented behaviour the code contradicts, a defect a 1.0 user would hit); OR
  (c) it is required to cut the release at all (release machinery, CI gates).

post-1.0 otherwise, on the specific ground that ADR-0071 point 1 makes --json documents additive-only WITHIN a major and the same holds for new MCP tools and new config keys. Adding a tool or a key after 1.0 is legal and non-breaking, so its absence at 1.0 is not a regression -- which is exactly what ADR-0071 point 5 means by naming out-of-scope work so its absence is not read as one.

ASSIGNMENTS AND THE REASONING THAT IS NOT OBVIOUS:

rc-1.0: g60k and its whole tree (bd30, l1yx, dsg1, y1dq, whhd) -- service install/uninstall/status/doctor are consumer CLI surface and file locations, both frozen. l83x -- normative spec contract. a5xj -- user-visible defect. e2c0 -- ADR-0080 is cited from frozen-surface code and docs; an ambiguous citation is a documentation defect at freeze time. j1zj -- an always-on server that grows an unbounded log is a 1.0 problem precisely because service install is what makes servers long-lived. x8g4 -- build footgun. 7k11 -- release atomicity is a precondition for cutting anything. fwwa -- additive by rule, but in flight and will land before the freeze.

post-1.0: huhi (new config key, additive), w1om (new MCP tool, additive), pw7a (new UX surface), rc7f (explicitly speculative -- 'if it comes back'), ed8j (test coverage, no consumer surface).

REMAINING HALF: the acceptance also asks for a gate that keeps this true. Not done here, deliberately -- the tracker lives in a Dolt DB and .beads/issues.jsonl is a passive export, so a CI gate reading it would be checking a snapshot that can be stale, which is a gate that lies. Filed separately rather than shipped wrong.
close_reason: Labelling half done: all 21 unlabelled open beads triaged, every open bead now carries exactly one of rc-1.0/post-1.0, and the criterion is recorded in this bead's notes. The gate half is deliberately not shipped -- a CI check reading the passive .beads/issues.jsonl export would be checking a possibly-stale snapshot and could fail in both directions. Split to phux-axdt with the two shapes that would actually work.

title: No MCP tool for attach or detach, the #2 verb by real usage
description:
Surface-coverage audit, 2026-08-11. Cross-referencing the three consumer surfaces -- CLI (~93 commands), TUI actions (36, docs/reference/actions.md), MCP tools (32, crates/phux-mcp/src/) -- against actual invocation frequency from shell history.

'attach' is the second most-used verb (17 invocations counting the 'a' alias, behind only 'ls' at 22). It has a CLI verb and a TUI action (switch-session). It has NO MCP tool.

So an agent can spawn a pane, kill one, send keys, paste, signal a process group, watch for output, snapshot, and drive the whole agent surface -- but cannot attach or detach a client. phux_ls, phux_kill, phux_new, phux_spawn, phux_send_keys, phux_watch, phux_signal all exist; phux_attach and phux_detach do not.

Given phux-w7z2 (agent-to-agent orchestration, P1 epic) is about agents driving phux, an agent that cannot attach is a real hole in that story -- it can manipulate panes but cannot take a seat at one.

DESIGN QUESTION TO ANSWER FIRST, not obvious: what does 'attach' mean for an MCP client with no terminal? The CLI attach starts a full TUI renderer. An MCP attach probably means the L1 subscription half -- ATTACH_TERMINAL and the frame stream -- without any chrome. If that is the answer, this is closer to 'expose the subscription' than 'expose attach', and should be named accordingly. Decide before implementing.

Related: phux_watch already does something subscription-shaped, so check whether this is a gap or a naming problem before adding a tool.
close_reason: Merged as #434. Shipped phux_detach only; the live-attach half was declined with the reason agent_tools.rs already documents -- a raw live ANSI stream has no request/response shape and cannot ride tools/call's single text-content-block envelope. That rationale is now written into docs/consumers/mcp.md so the next person gets the answer instead of the gap. phux_detach takes session (optional) and confirm (required true), and returns the SERVER-ACKED count rather than an echo, so 0 means nobody was attached -- success, not a miss. confirm is unconditional per phux_kill's precedent, not because it destroys data but because it forcibly ejects a live client without consent. Deliberately distinct from the interactive self-detach, which stays TUI-only because it acts on the caller's own attachment. Implemented over the wire via DETACH_CLIENTS rather than adding --json to phux detach, keeping the diff out of the phux binary and its generated CLI reference.

title: One shared guard for tests that spawn a real phux server
description:
Eleven test files under crates/phux/tests/ each hand-roll a byte-identical ServerGuard:

  impl Drop for ServerGuard {
      fn drop(&mut self) { let _ = self.child.kill(); let _ = self.child.wait(); }
  }

(spatial_e2e:44, run_wait_e2e:78, rec_e2e:76, upgrade_e2e:50, play_e2e:140, plugin_agent_bench_e2e:29, workspace_archive_e2e:28, resize_e2e:61, agent_record_e2e:51, idle_exit_e2e:138, failure_ux_e2e:147.) The shape is CORRECT -- SIGKILL on unwind plus an --exit-after-idle 600 wall-clock backstop -- and the rationale is written out verbatim in each file. The problem is that it is copied eleven times, so the two files that deviate deviate silently. See phux-whhd for which.

NO SHARED GUARD EXISTS TO ADOPT. crates/phux-server-testkit/ is an IN-PROCESS toolkit (spawn_server* run ServerRuntime on a LocalSet; no OS process is created, and those are not the leak). It contains not a single impl Drop -- all 85 call sites hand-write teardown. It is also not reachable from crates/phux tests: phux's dev-deps deliberately exclude phux-server-testkit, and adding it would pull phux-server + phux-relay into phux's test build, which that crate's Cargo.toml doc comment explicitly exists to prevent.

WHAT THE SHARED GUARD MUST DO:
1. Own a real Child when possible, and ALWAYS pass --exit-after-idle -- the one backstop that survives a SIGKILLed runner.
2. For the auto-spawn shape with no Child, take the pid from 'phux status --json' (SO_PEERCRED at connect time; status never auto-spawns, so the cleanup cannot create what it is reaping). Blocked on phux-a1b for a real backstop there.
3. Use SIGKILL, or SIGTERM only after phux-1wka lands. Today SIGTERM is strictly worse than SIGKILL -- less certain and buys nothing, because there is no handler.
4. Prefer libc::kill over Command::new("kill") so failures are observable rather than swallowed by a let _ inside a Drop.
5. POLL FOR ACTUAL EXIT before the TempDir drops. Drop::drop runs before the struct's fields drop, so today the tempdir is unlinked racing the dying server.
6. Live where crates/phux/tests/* can reach it -- realistically crates/phux/tests/common/ (accepting the per-binary recompile, small for ~150 lines) or a new phux-cli-testkit crate.

Note that phux-pimp (a first-class stop verb) collapses steps 2-5 into one subprocess call. Worth sequencing after it if it is close.

Parent: phux-g60k.
notes: CORRECTION: 'phux-a1b' in the description is a mistyped id. The intended reference is phux-nbam (Auto-spawned daemons get no --exit-after-idle, so a leaked one is immortal).
close_reason: Added crates/phux/tests/common shared real-server lifecycle helpers and migrated direct-child, auto-spawn, service, stale-socket, crash-injection, and first-five-minutes harnesses. Direct children use observable libc SIGKILL and wait/reap before socket/tempdir teardown; auto-spawn captures status --json PID, requests first-class shutdown, falls back through signals, and polls actual exit.
