Added the missing 600s idle backstop to service_login_shell_e2e while preserving explicit idle-lifetime tests. just ci-full passed: 3,772 workspace tests, 59 real-server journeys, latency gates, docs, fleet smoke.

title: Auto-spawned daemons get no --exit-after-idle, so a leaked one is immortal
description:
maybe_auto_spawn_server (crates/phux/src/commands/server.rs:399-450) fork-execs 'phux server --socket ... --session ... --daemonize' and NEVER passes --exit-after-idle (argv built at server.rs:425-445). It also deliberately drops the Child (server.rs:447-449: 'we deliberately don't keep the Child around; the server is its own lifecycle now').

So an auto-spawned daemon has no owner AND no timed backstop. It lives until its last pane dies -- and the last-pane self-exit is armed only after a client attaches (runtime/client.rs:563-566), so a daemon that never served a client never self-exits either.

This is the structural root of phux-whhd. Every 'phux server' child spawned explicitly by a test carries --exit-after-idle 600 as the survives-a-SIGKILLed-runner backstop; the auto-spawn path cannot, because nothing passes it.

FIX OPTIONS:
(a) Have auto-spawn inherit an idle limit from an env var or config key, defaulting to none in production but settable by tests and by anyone who wants an ephemeral server. ADR-0063 already establishes --exit-after-idle as the ephemeral-lifetime mechanism, so this is extending an existing seam, not inventing one.
(b) Leave production alone and give tests a supported way to request it.

Do NOT simply default auto-spawn to a finite idle timeout -- ADR-0063 and server_idle_exit.rs::without_the_flag_an_unattended_server_stays_up deliberately pin that an unattended server stays up. Changing that is a product decision, not a test-hygiene fix.

Parent: phux-g60k.
close_reason: Fixed in #427 (3c7a838a). PHUX_AUTO_SPAWN_EXIT_AFTER_IDLE gives an auto-spawned daemon an idle backstop, as an opt-in seam rather than a new default: ADR-0063 pins that an unattended server stays up, and making auto-spawn finite would change the multiplexer contract. The value is parsed by the parent and passed as --exit-after-idle so a leaked server shows its bound in ps; parent and child pin the same 1..=86400 range. Two e2e cases cover the auto-spawn path, which no existing test could reach (no Child to wait on, no argv to influence). Unblocks phux-y1dq.

title: A dev-profile binary can install a service unit that hijacks the default profile's label
description:
ADR-0080 introduced profiles so a development binary cannot touch the installed one's sessions -- socket, runtime, and state dirs are all profile-scoped, and the isolation is deliberately automatic rather than opt-in.

service install does not participate. resolve_plan (crates/phux/src/commands/service.rs:400-436) never consults is_default_profile. A dev-profile binary running 'phux service install' writes a unit whose socket and log paths point at the phux-dev locations, but under the SAME single launchd label com.phux.server (service.rs:24) / the same systemd unit name.

So a dev install silently replaces the production unit with one that supervises a dev-profile server. Nothing guards it and nothing warns.

FIX: either scope the label/unit name by profile, or refuse to install from a non-default profile without an explicit override. Scoping the label is more in the spirit of ADR-0080's automatic isolation, but it is the more invasive change since the label is also what uninstall and status resolve against -- decide deliberately.

Note phux doctor already reports a non-default profile as a warning (ADR-0080), so the diagnostic half exists; it is the install path that ignores it.
close_reason: Fixed in #427 (3c7a838a). Launchd label and systemd unit name are now profile-scoped via launchd_label_for/systemd_unit_for; the default profile keeps the bare names so an already-loaded job stays addressable across the upgrade. ServicePlan carries the resolved profile so renderers stay pure. ADR-0080 amended to state that the service unit is scoped alongside the runtime and state dirs.

title: Reconcile a legacy supervisor unit in place, without killing panes
description:
The fix phux-bd30 asks for, scoped against what the code actually allows.

GOAL: bring an installed unit up to the ADR-0080 policy (SuccessfulExit:false / Restart=on-failure, throttled) without restarting the server, so a user with a legacy unit is not choosing between a bad policy and losing every pane (phux-nvi2).

THREE OBSTACLES, all confirmed:

1. THE FLAGS ARE NOT RECOVERABLE. --quic, --listen, --restore, --hub, --socket live only in the rendered unit (ServicePlan, service.rs:121-162). Nothing parses a unit back into a ServicePlan. A blind 'phux service install' re-run renders a unit with all of them DROPPED, silently removing the operator's QUIC/WS listeners and hub mode. So reconcile needs a unit->ServicePlan parser, or a persisted plan record, before it can safely rewrite anything.

2. THE RELOAD IS DESTRUCTIVE. See phux-nvi2. Rewriting the unit FILE is harmless; it is 'launchctl bootout'/'systemctl enable --now' that kills panes. A reconcile that rewrites the file and does NOT reload gives the correct policy on next restart, which is the honest non-destructive option and is probably the right default. Say so in the output.

3. CONTENT IS DETERMINISTIC BUT INPUTS ARE MACHINE-SPECIFIC. The renderers are pure over ServicePlan and byte-stable (environment_order_is_stable_across_renders, service.rs:1147-1153), so a diff IS meaningful in principle. But resolve_plan (service.rs:400-436) bakes in std::env::current_exe(), PHUX_WS_TOKENS / PHUX_WS_TLS_* read from the INSTALLING PROCESS's environment, default_socket_path() (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR-dependent), and a profile-scoped log path. Re-rendering from a different shell -- a nix develop session, a dev profile -- produces a legitimately different unit, so a byte-diff reports false positives.

RECOMMENDED SHAPE: a semantic diff restricted to the restart-policy keys, which is what supervisor_unit_is_legacy already gestures at, plus value checking (phux-dsg1). Rewrite only those keys, preserve everything else in the file verbatim, do not reload, and tell the user the new policy takes effect at the next server start.

phux-bd30 suggests 'phux update' should do this automatically. That is defensible ONLY with the non-destructive shape above; an automatic reconcile that reloads would kill panes during an update with no prompt.
close_reason: Merged as #433 with phux-bd30. New phux service reconcile [--print] rewrites ONLY the restart-policy directives of an installed unit, preserving every other byte -- so the flag-loss problem is structurally impossible rather than carefully avoided, because no ServicePlan is built and no path re-derived. Reconcile::Current is DEFINED as the patch being a byte no-op, so there is no separate legacy predicate to drift; generator and reconciler share launchd_policy_lines()/systemd_policy_lines() and a test pins reconcile(render(plan)) == Current. launchd patching tracks nesting depth so only the top-level dict is a candidate, and an unclassifiable value shape is REFUSED, because a half-rewritten plist launchd silently declines to load is worse than the legacy policy. Per-platform honesty: systemd hot-reloads via daemon-reload and the command says the policy is in force; launchd cannot, so it prints that the policy is NOT active yet, that it self-activates at next login, and what forcing it now would cost. It never reloads on macOS. Its ADR was renumbered 0083 during integration after colliding with #429's rename to 0082.

title: doctor's three server-health conditions are mutually exclusive, and the legacy-unit one is untested
description:
crates/phux/src/commands/doctor.rs::check_server_health (~211-264) evaluates three conditions with EARLY RETURNS, so they are mutually exclusive: crash-loop (~214) beats legacy-unit (~231) beats version-skew (~249). A crash-looping host with a legacy unit never learns about the legacy unit -- and per phux-67wg, a legacy-unit host is exactly the kind that crash-loops, so the two conditions co-occur precisely when the report is least useful.

Second defect, same area: supervisor_unit_is_legacy (doctor.rs:271-278) is two substring probes over raw file text, not a comparison against what this binary would render:

  let throttled    = body.contains("ThrottleInterval") || body.contains("RestartSec");
  let failure_only = body.contains("SuccessfulExit")   || body.contains("Restart=on-failure");
  !(throttled && failure_only)

Any unit containing both markers passes REGARDLESS OF VALUES. 'ThrottleInterval 0' passes. 'Restart=always' alongside a stray 'SuccessfulExit' string passes. It checks for the presence of words, not for the policy.

Third: supervisor_unit_is_legacy, legacy_service_unit_path, and check_server_health have NO unit tests at all. The ADR-0080 detection logic is entirely untested, while the unit RENDERING it is supposed to detect has 17 tests. The detection is the half that runs on users' machines.

FIX: report all applicable conditions rather than the first; check values not just key presence; add the missing tests. Note legacy_service_unit_path (doctor.rs:285-302) deliberately duplicates the path logic from service.rs -- keep that, it is documented, but the duplication means a path change needs both edited.

DO NOT ship doctor's current hint as-is; see phux-cq31.
notes: CORRECTION: the description references 'phux-cq31', which was a mistyped id and does not exist. The intended reference is phux-nvi2 (doctor tells you to fix a legacy unit with a command that kills every pane).
close_reason: Merged as #430. check_server_health split into an impure gatherer plus a pure server_health_checks returning Vec<Check>, so co-occurring conditions all surface -- the crash-loop and legacy-unit pair are one causal story per ADR-0080/phux-67wg, and reporting only the first withheld the reason. supervisor_unit_is_legacy rewritten to parse VALUES rather than match directive names, fixing two false-passes (ThrottleInterval 0, and Restart=always beside a stray SuccessfulExit). legacy_service_unit_path made profile-aware, fixing a regression #427 introduced when it profile-scoped the unit names. 0 -> 20 tests, including detection cross-checked against the real render_launchd_plist/render_systemd_unit output so it cannot drift from generation. One CI-only failure fixed in integration: the LegacyManager dead_code allow was on the Systemd variant, which is correct on macOS but fails on Linux where Launchd is the unconstructed one; moved to the enum so it covers whichever variant the target leaves dead.

title: Two ADRs are both numbered 0080, and docs-check has no uniqueness gate
description:
ADR/0080-retire-the-ci-metrics-store.md and ADR/0080-socket-lifecycle-and-instance-isolation.md are both Accepted and both numbered 0080. Every 'ADR-0080' reference in beads, docs, and code comments is therefore ambiguous -- and the two ADRs are about completely unrelated things (CI observability vs socket lifecycle/supervision), so a reader following a reference can land on the wrong one with no signal that they have.

scripts/check-docs.sh gates ADR 'Status:' vocabulary (gate_adr_status, ~line 481) but has NO gate for number uniqueness, which is why 'just docs-check' reports 147 files 0 violations against this.

TWO UNITS OF WORK, do both:
1. Renumber one of them. The socket-lifecycle ADR is the one referenced by ADR-0081, docs/operations.md, phux-bd30, phux-j1zj, phux-mk37, and crates/phux/src/commands/service.rs, so renumbering the CI-metrics one is the cheaper edit. Update every inbound reference.
2. Add an adr-number-unique gate to scripts/check-docs.sh so this cannot recur. Register it in the gate list (~line 45) and the dispatch (~line 853), following the shape of gate_adr_status.
close_reason: Merged as #429. ADR/0080-retire-the-ci-metrics-store.md renumbered to 0082 -- chosen by COUNTING references (socket-lifecycle had ~28, ci-metrics 3), not assuming. Eleven inbound edits across nine files, four of which (.github/workflows/ci.yml, stress.yml, justfile, scripts/ci/summarize-job.sh) sit outside crates/docs/ADR and were only found by widening the sweep to the whole repo. New gate_adr_number_unique in scripts/check-docs.sh names BOTH offending files on collision; proved it fires with a temporary fixture before committing. The gate earned itself within the hour: phux-l1yx had independently created a second ADR/0082, and the gate caught it at integration -- renumbered to 0083.

title: DETACHED is a unit variant, so the spec's fatal-error contract is only half implemented
description:
docs/spec/proto.md ~580-592 specifies DETACHED { reason: DetachReason, message: str }, and proto.md ~743 makes it the normative fatal signal: 'A fatal error MUST be followed by DETACHED { reason: PROTOCOL_ERROR } and transport close.'

FrameKind::Detached (phux-protocol/src/wire/frame.rs ~2025-2031) is a UNIT variant. It carries neither field. The gap is acknowledged in its own doc comment.

Consequence: a consumer cannot read WHY it was detached. This matters more now that phux-ijuj made ERROR non-fatal at the receiver -- DETACHED plus transport close is the ONLY termination signal a consumer is allowed to act on, so it is now load-bearing and it is missing its payload.

Requires a wire change (additive TLV fields on 0xC2), a docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md entry, and a client-side surface for the reason. Related: phux-ijuj.
close_reason: Merged as #435. DETACHED gained reason and message as two additive optional TLV field ids; PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 0.7.0, landed as 0.7.0-draft.7. NO ServerFeature bit, and that is the considered answer: ADR-0061 names an additive field id decoders skip by length as a capability form in its own right, DETACHED is server->client, and its decoder has drained unknown field ids since 0.4.0 -- verified by test, with the reason-less encoding asserted byte-identical to the legacy empty body. Deliberate divergence flagged: an unrecognised DetachReason decodes as UNSTATED rather than hard-failing like ErrorCode, because rejecting the one frame a consumer may act on would convert an explained ending into an unexplained transport error and would make every future reason allocation a fleet-wide break. Remaining half -- the server still never emits SERVER_SHUTDOWN/REPLACED/PROTOCOL_ERROR/INTERNAL_ERROR -- split to phux-u3et with both blockers recorded; proto.md 7.2 carries a 'partial' marker meanwhile.

title: Spawn bootstraps a pane at 80x24, then the client's reflow resize throws the checkpoint away
description:
handle_spawn_terminal (runtime/attach.rs ~1144) builds the pane actor at a hardcoded 80x24 (runtime/commands.rs ~288) and never resizes it. It then runs a full native checkpoint capture and publishes BOOTSTRAP_BEGIN/CHUNK/READY for that grid.

The client, on TERMINAL_SPAWNED, computes reflow_panes (client/attach/server_frame.rs ~1669 for new-window, ~1332 for split) and sends TERMINAL_RESIZE per changed leaf. The dims always differ from 80x24, so handle_resize's no-op guard never fires and invalidate_all_native_cursors drains the binding that was just installed.

Net effect on EVERY pane creation: one full generation capture is computed, published, and immediately tombstoned, followed by a second capture for the real geometry. Wasted work plus an extra round trip on the interactive path.

This was the guaranteed trigger for phux-rv52. That bug is CLOSED by the tombstone fix in terminal_actor::handle_native_history -- the race is now answered benignly and the client degrades that pane instead of dying. This bead is the remaining efficiency/cleanliness half; it is NOT a correctness fix, and it does not remove the race (any SIGWINCH or peer-client resize during history load reproduces it).

The contrast to copy is the aggregate attach path: attach.rs ~2099 calls apply_attach_viewport BEFORE any bootstrap, so geometry has settled by the time a binding exists.

OPEN QUESTION that has to be answered first: for split-pane the new pane's tile is a fraction of the client's viewport, and layout is computed client-side. Determine whether the server can know the target geometry at spawn time at all, or whether the fix is instead to defer the native bootstrap until the first TERMINAL_RESIZE settles.
close_reason: Landed on main as c0ad143e 'fix(server): spawn panes at the geometry the client already knows'.

title: Test suite leaks auto-spawned servers
description: Observed ~20 orphaned 'target/debug/phux server' processes after repeated 'just test' runs, each holding a PTY on a temp socket whose directory is long gone. tests/stale_socket_recovery.rs was one source (its Drop guard called 'phux kill --server', which is not a real flag, so cleanup silently no-opped) and is fixed by reading the pid from 'phux status --json' and sending SIGTERM. Other auto-spawning tests may have the same shape -- there is no 'stop the server' verb for a daemonised auto-spawn, so every such test has to hand-roll it. Worth auditing, and worth considering a first-class shutdown verb or a shared test guard.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-08-11 -- one premise in this bead is WRONG, and the real leak set is different from what it assumed.

PREMISE CORRECTION: 'git log -S "kill --server" -- crates/phux/tests/' returns NOTHING, and stale_socket_recovery.rs has exactly one commit (a9342b7b). The broken 'phux kill --server' cleanup existed only in the working tree before that commit; what is on main is ALREADY the fixed pid-from-status version. So that file was never a source of leaks on main.

THE ACTUAL LEAKS. Only crates/phux/tests/* can leak OS processes -- the ~46 phux-server test binaries and the relay tests use phux-server-testkit, which runs ServerRuntime in-process on a LocalSet and creates no phux server process. Those are not the leak, and they shut down correctly on panic (the oneshot Sender drops during unwind).

Of the 13 files that create a real server, 11 carry a correct Drop guard AND --exit-after-idle 600, and are #[ignore]d. The leaks are the exceptions:

1. stale_socket_recovery.rs -- NOT #[ignore]d, so it runs in the default 'just test' pool, matching the observed symptom. Two auto-spawned daemons per run. Its Drop guard is right in shape but has four defects: (a) its load-bearing comment claims 'the server's shutdown path is what unlinks the socket' for SIGTERM, which is FALSE -- there is no SIGTERM handler (phux-1wka), so the choice of SIGTERM over SIGKILL is strictly worse today, less certain and buying nothing; (b) it never waits for exit, and Drop::drop runs before fields drop, so the TempDir is unlinked racing the dying server; (c) if 'status' fails AFTER connecting, the JSON error contract puts the document on stderr and leaves stdout EMPTY, so from_slice on stdout fails and the guard silently returns -- the same silently-no-opping class this bead was filed about, relocated; (d) no backstop is structurally possible, because auto-spawn never passes --exit-after-idle (phux-nbam).

2. service_login_shell_e2e.rs -- also NOT #[ignore]d, also default pool. It is the ONLY Shape-A guard with no --exit-after-idle backstop (argv at :142-144). Its seed command exits promptly, but last-pane self-exit is armed only after a client attaches and none ever does, so a missed Drop leaks a permanent daemon.

3. failure_ux_e2e.rs:373-426 broken_config_makes_server_start_loud -- spawns a bare Child at :385 with NO Drop guard. Its own panic message says 'killing it' but nothing does; std::process::Child's Drop does not kill. Only --exit-after-idle 30 mitigates.

LATENT: workspace_archive_e2e.rs:130-140 runs 'phux new' against a guarded socket. If that server dies mid-test, 'new' auto-spawns an unguarded, backstop-less replacement no Child owns.

WORK IS SPLIT OUT: phux-y1dq (one shared guard), phux-nbam (auto-spawn backstop), phux-1wka (SIGTERM handler). This bead should become the audit-and-migrate task once those land.
MEASURED 2026-08-15 on branch army/w3-test-health (base 69289db4). THE LEAK THIS BEAD WAS FILED ABOUT NO LONGER REPRODUCES.

Stray `phux server` processes owned by this worktree after a full `cargo nextest run --workspace` (3773 tests, 3773 passed): ZERO. Repeated four times across the session, including one run at load average 171 and one deliberate full-parallel run under 16 synthetic CPU burners (load 121 -> 168): still zero. `just e2e` (59 real-PTY e2e tests + 3 perf gates) measured separately: zero before, zero after.

WHY: the three beads this one's own audit split out have all landed. phux-y1dq gave every real-server test a shared `common::AutoSpawnedServer` guard that captures the pid from `status --json`, tries `phux kill --server`, escalates SIGTERM -> SIGKILL, and WAITS for exit. phux-1wka added the SIGTERM handler that makes the graceful path real. phux-nbam added `PHUX_AUTO_SPAWN_EXIT_AFTER_IDLE`. All three audited leak sites are remediated: stale_socket_recovery.rs uses the shared guard; service_login_shell_e2e.rs now passes `--exit-after-idle 600`; failure_ux_e2e's broken-config case is `#[ignore]`d behind `just e2e`.

TWO PREMISES IN THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION ARE NOW WRONG, on top of the one the 2026-08-11 audit already corrected:
* "there is no 'stop the server' verb for a daemonised auto-spawn" -- `phux kill --server` exists and the shared guard uses it (kill_server_e2e covers it).
* "phux kill --server ... is not a real flag" -- it is.

WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINED, and is now fixed on this branch:

1. The auto-spawn backstop was opt-in and NOTHING opted in. `PHUX_AUTO_SPAWN_EXIT_AFTER_IDLE` was referenced only by idle_exit_e2e, which sets it to test itself. Every other auto-spawning test still produced a daemon with no owner AND no timer, so a test process killed before its Drop guard ran leaked something immortal. That is not hypothetical -- three such daemons were found alive on this box, from OTHER worktrees, dated 2026-08-12, still holding PTYs on `tempfile` sockets whose directories had already been removed (`.tmpHTjIkA` gone entirely, `.tmpmRn0A0` emptied). Their argv is the tell: `--session default --daemonize` with no `--exit-after-idle`, i.e. auto-spawn, on a `.../phux.sock` path matching stale_socket_recovery's fixture.
   FIX: the `test`, `e2e` and `test-cargo` lanes in the justfile now export `PHUX_AUTO_SPAWN_EXIT_AFTER_IDLE=600`. Deliberately NOT a justfile-wide `export` -- that would also reach `install-dev`, `rebuild` and the `cargo run` recipes and put an idle bound on a developer's own server, which ADR-0063 says must not happen.

   REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, worth recording: `[env]` in `.config/nextest.toml` would have been the better home (it covers a bare `cargo nextest run` too). cargo-nextest 0.9.136 in this dev shell DOES NOT SUPPORT IT -- it warns `ignoring unknown configuration key: env` and silently drops it. Verified against three spellings (`[env]`, `[profile.default.env]`, per-override `env = {}`); all three are rejected. If nextest is ever bumped to a version that supports it, move the variable there and drop the justfile plumbing.

2. `failure_ux_e2e::broken_config_makes_server_start_loud` held a bare `std::process::Child` whose panic message says "killing it" while nothing killed anything -- `Child::drop` does not kill. If the audited silent-start regression ever came back, the very run that caught it would have leaked the daemon it caught. Now owned by `common::ServerProcess`, whose Drop SIGKILLs a survivor and unlinks the socket.

RESIDUAL (deliberately not changed): the latent `workspace_archive_e2e` case where a `phux new` against a dead guarded socket auto-spawns an unguarded replacement is now bounded by the lane-level backstop above rather than by a guard. That is the right trade -- adding a second guard for a path that should never execute costs more than it buys.
close_reason: Audit-and-migrate complete on army/w3-test-health. Measured ZERO stray phux servers after a full cargo nextest run --workspace (3773 tests), repeated four times including at load average 171 and under 16 synthetic burners; zero around just e2e too. The original leak is already fixed by phux-y1dq, phux-nbam and phux-1wka. Two premises in the description are now stale: phux kill --server does exist, and there IS a stop verb for a daemonised auto-spawn. Remaining gaps closed here: the auto-spawn backstop was opt-in and nothing opted in (test/e2e/test-cargo lanes now set PHUX_AUTO_SPAWN_EXIT_AFTER_IDLE=600 in the justfile, deliberately not a global export), and failure_ux_e2e's broken-config case held a bare Child whose Drop does not kill (now a common::ServerProcess). Recorded that nextest 0.9.136 in this dev shell silently ignores an [env] table, which is why the variable lives in the justfile.

title: Server log rotation is startup-only
description: ADR-0080 added size-based rotation of server.log, but it is checked once, at server start (telemetry::rotate_if_oversized). A single long-lived, chatty server can still exceed the 8 MiB threshold within one run. Bounding that needs a rolling appender. Deferred until there is evidence it matters -- the growth actually observed came from many short-lived generations, which startup rotation does bound.
close_reason: Landed on main as 58625c34 'fix(server): rotate server.log while the server is live, not just at start' (#437). ADR-0080 updated with the 2026-08-12 note.

title: Distinguish definitely-not-written input failures from delivery_unknown
description: The acknowledged input handoff currently maps some full/closed/no-PTY conditions into INPUT_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN even when the server can prove no PTY write began. That forces callers to stop rather than safely retry. Audit the handoff boundary and return a typed definitely-not-written refusal wherever proof exists, reserving delivery_unknown for writes whose outcome is genuinely indeterminate.
acceptance_criteria: Every pre-write rejection is typed as safe-to-retry/nothing-written; delivery_unknown is emitted only after the result becomes indeterminate; tests pin the boundary.
notes: phux-w7z2.58 (9685cf39) reshapes the surface this bead audits: the per-request completion Sender is now terminal_actor::WriteCompletionSink, a one-shot callback whose Drop reports WriteCompletion::Failed. Cases D/E/F/G from verify-input-lane.md (pane mailbox full/closed, no PTY, actor destroyed with the request queued) all now land on that Drop, in one place, so the typed NotWritten sibling this bead asks for is a variant on WriteCompletion plus a mapping in acknowledged::completion_result — noticeably smaller than when the bead was filed. The pre-handoff refusals the lane itself makes (mailbox full, actor changed) already route through CompletionWaiterHandle::abandon and are NOT cached as final, so they are already safe-to-retry; the gap is the actor-side drops.
close_reason: Landed on main as 363cb2eb. ErrorCode::InputNotWritten (207) + WriteCompletion::NotWritten, plumbed through ApplyVerdict/PromptError/CLI (send-keys, prompt, answer). Genuinely-ambiguous paths deliberately left on delivery_unknown. Spec L1.md/proto.md draft-bumped, docs/consumers/agents.md 5.3 updated.

title: Make acknowledged input admission per Terminal instead of per server
description: Verification found one Arc<AtomicBool> acknowledged-input lane per server and a blocking completion wait on the shared input execution thread. Concurrent prompts to unrelated panes collide into RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED and an acknowledged write can head-of-line block human input elsewhere. Redesign admission and execution so unrelated Terminals progress independently while preserving same-Terminal idempotency, ordering, and operation-result caching.
acceptance_criteria: Acknowledged writes to different Terminals do not collide or head-of-line block; same-Terminal ordering and operation-id replay semantics remain covered.
close_reason: Admission keyed by TerminalId (AcknowledgedAdmission: Mutex<HashSet<TerminalId>>); completion wait moved off the lane onto a dedicated waiter thread that multiplexes every pending operation by ticket. Revert-checked: per-server admission fails acknowledged_admission_is_scoped_to_the_target_terminal; a blocking lane fails an_unresolved_acknowledged_write_does_not_stall_another_pane and later_input_to_the_same_pane_stays_behind_an_unresolved_batch. Same-Terminal exclusion, dedupe/replay semantics, and admission-time retention clock unchanged (existing tests pass unmodified except for the sink API). Commit 9685cf39; just ci-full green.

title: Route or explicitly refuse satellite agent metadata subscriptions
description: SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS is satellite-routed, but SUBSCRIBE_METADATA and GET_METADATA on a satellite-tagged Terminal remain local to the hub. phux agent wait and watch agent_state can therefore time out as if no transition occurred when the feature is actually unavailable. Route metadata subscriptions through the relay, or refuse satellite agent-state waits before subscribing with a typed capability error.
acceptance_criteria: A satellite agent wait either observes remote metadata correctly or fails immediately with a typed unsupported/refusal error; it never returns an ordinary 124 for an unrouted subscription.
close_reason:
REFUSE, argued, on branch army/w7z2-57-satellite-metadata. Routing is the eventual answer but not a 1.0 change: it needs a METADATA_CHANGED return leg re-tagging Terminal(Local) -> Terminal(Satellite), a decision about what Global/Group scopes mean across a federation boundary, and -- to be worth having -- federated APPLY_INPUT (phux-2en, post-1.0). Observe-without-act is half a feature, and agent start/answer/session ALREADY refuse satellite targets for exactly that reason, so agent wait was the last of the family still pretending. A refusal upgrades to routing without breaking a consumer: today's ERROR becomes tomorrow's METADATA_CHANGED.

THE PART THAT MATTERED MOST: the answer differed per layer, and the agent checked rather than assuming one fix covered both. Server-side, a satellite Terminal scope now installs nothing and pushes ERROR { request_id: None, code: UNSUPPORTED_SATELLITE_ROUTE }, reaching every consumer including the MCP adapter and third-party clients. But agent wait awaits a CORRELATED METADATA_VALUE, so an uncorrelated ERROR never surfaces in its request path -- the verb where the user actually feels the bug needed its own check. phux agent wait now refuses a satellite target with the existing satellite_target code, exit 2, at selector resolution. That replaces the no_agent_record misreport, which was worse than the timeout the bead named because it asserted a fact about the pane rather than a limit of the build.

NO NEW WIRE CODE, deliberately: UNSUPPORTED_SATELLITE_ROUTE = 106 already means 'carried a Satellite id, no route for it', and minting a new ErrorCode would be a hard decode error on older peers that draft.10 established no capability form can gate. PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 0.7.0; recorded as 0.7.0-draft.11 with a new normative L3 1.3 'L3 does not federate'.

GET_METADATA/LIST_METADATA left unchanged on purpose -- they report the receiving server's store where the key genuinely IS unset, so value: None is true rather than merely uninformative, and converting them to correlated errors would strand pending entries in consumers that retire them only on METADATA_VALUE (the TUI driver does exactly that).

Required companion: the TUI driver now skips satellite panes in sync_agent_meta_subscriptions, without which every remote pane in a hub TUI would earn a warn Notice on every pane-set change.

Mutation-verified: both fixes neutered independently, all three new tests failed with assertions rather than hangs, then restored.

title: Keep HELLO layers and peer identity across mid-connection DETACH
description: ServerState::detach removes connection-scoped negotiated layers and peer identity even though the DETACH handler keeps the connection alive. ClientTable::layers then fails open to LayerSet::all, letting an L1-only peer pass the L3 gate after ATTACH then DETACH. Separate connection teardown from attachment teardown, preserve negotiated state until transport close, and make the metadata fanout regression test send a real L3 HELLO.
acceptance_criteria: A live connection retains HELLO layers and peer identity across DETACH; an L1-only client remains unable to use L3; production-shaped HELLO coverage exists.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED, and one half is FAIL-OPEN -- a privilege escalation, not just state loss. Branch army/w7z2-55-hello-across-detach.

A mid-connection DETACH does not end the connection: the arm at runtime/client.rs:1544 emits DETACHED and keeps reading, deliberately, so the same connection can serve a later ATTACH. But ServerState::detach discarded two things that belong to the CONNECTION, not the attachment:

1. Negotiated HELLO.layers -- detach did clients.layers.remove(). client_layers defaults to LayerSet::all() for an UNKNOWN client, so removing the entry FAILS OPEN: an L1-only peer that attached and then detached began passing the proto.md 11.5 out-of-tier gate. Confirmed on the wire, not by reading: the mutation run answered a non-L3 consumer's GET_METADATA with MetadataValue { request_id: 7, value: None } where it should have refused.

2. PeerIdentity -- detach_and_release_consumer_state did remove_peer_identity. Its live consumer is handle_shutdown, which gates SHUTDOWN on transport == UnixSocket. This one FAILS CLOSED: the mutation run returned PermissionDenied to a LOCAL peer that had merely detached. Not a bypass, but the identity the authorization seam keys on vanished from a live connection.

Neither is recoverable in-connection: a second HELLO is a protocol error, and PeerIdentity is stamped by the accepting transport before the client task spawns.

WHAT CORRECTLY RESETS and was left alone: L3 metadata subscriptions and their mailboxes, agent-event subscriptions, input leases, output pumps, pane subscriptions, session-create result keys. docs/spec/L3.md 1.2 is explicit that metadata subscriptions drop on DETACH. The in-code comment calling them 'connection-scoped' contradicted itself -- behaviour right, wording wrong; wording corrected.

FIX: ServerState::detach is now attachment teardown only; new forget_connection = detach + drop layers + drop peer identity, reached via a new release_connection_state called from the accept loop's post-handle_client cleanup at client.rs:1082 -- the one site every connection on every transport funnels through, since all 20+ in-loop teardown paths return into it. The attach.rs/commands.rs call sites are force-detaches of OTHER still-connected clients and carried the same bug; they are fixed by the same change without being touched.

NO WIRE CHANGE, no spec edit, no draft number consumed. The observable effect is only that the 11.5 gate now holds where it previously opened.

BEAD FRAMING was 2/3 accurate. The third clause -- 'make the metadata fanout regression test send a real L3 HELLO' -- is STALE: the testkit's wait_for_socket has completed a real handshake advertising LayerSet::all() since #364, so every fanout test already negotiates properly. Only metadata_reply.rs's module comment still claimed otherwise; comment corrected, no test rework needed.
close_reason: Landed on main. FAIL-OPEN authorization bug: ServerState::detach removed the negotiated HELLO layers, and client_layers defaults to LayerSet::all() for an unknown client -- so an L1-only peer that attached and detached began PASSING the proto.md 11.5 out-of-tier gate. Proven on the wire by mutation, not by reading: the reverted run answered a non-L3 consumer's GET_METADATA with a real MetadataValue. Second half, PeerIdentity, fails closed -- a local peer that had merely detached got PermissionDenied from SHUTDOWN's UnixSocket gate. Neither is recoverable in-connection: a second HELLO is a protocol error and PeerIdentity is stamped by the transport before the client task spawns. Root cause is that a mid-connection DETACH does not end the connection -- it emits DETACHED and keeps reading, deliberately -- yet teardown discarded connection-scoped state alongside attachment-scoped state. Fixed by splitting the two: detach is attachment teardown only, and a new forget_connection runs from the single accept-loop site every transport funnels through, which also fixed the force-detach call sites in attach.rs/commands.rs without touching them. What correctly resets was left alone (metadata and event subscriptions, input leases, output pumps). No wire change. One bead clause was STALE -- the testkit has negotiated a real L3 HELLO since #364, so the requested test rework was unnecessary; only a lying module comment needed correcting.

title: Publish DSR release fallback documentation
description: A clean standalone worktree contains one unpushed documentation commit describing the dsr local release fallback, but has no remote branch or PR. Rebase it onto current main, validate repository docs, and publish it as a focused PR.
acceptance_criteria: The branch is based on current origin/main, docs-check passes, and a focused PR is open.
close_reason: Rebased onto current main, docs-check passes, pushed, and opened PR 409.

title: Document the 5s acknowledged-completion timeout and the cross-pane input coupling in docs/spec
description:
Found while landing phux-w7z2.5 (agent prompt on APPLY_INPUT).

Two server behaviours that a client MUST design around appear in no spec
document and in no ADR, so every future APPLY_INPUT caller has to rediscover
them by reading phux-server:

1. ACKNOWLEDGED_COMPLETION_TIMEOUT = 5s
   (crates/phux-server/src/runtime/input_lane.rs:79, waited at :821).
   A client submit deadline BELOW this abandons an operation whose id is about
   to be bound to a result it will never see. phux-client's SUBMIT_DEADLINE is
   8s purely because this constant was read out of the source.

2. The admission flag is held ACROSS that wait (drop(reservation) at
   input_lane.rs:899), and the flag is one AtomicBool for the whole server
   (:851, one lane per server at runtime/mod.rs:823). So the worst-case
   RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED retry interval is ~5s, and a backoff schedule giving up
   under ~6s fails spuriously against one wedged pane.

Also undocumented anywhere (L1.md, input.md, ADR-0053): an APPLY_INPUT to pane
X can stall attached INPUT_* and ROUTE_INPUT for pane Y for up to 5s, and drop
attached keystrokes past 1024 queued events (input_lane.rs:175-183, try_send +
warn!). That coupling is a real operational property of the server and belongs
in the spec, whether or not the lane is later made per-Terminal.

Belongs in docs/spec/L1.md 6.2.1 plus a docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md entry. No wire
change; this is documenting what already ships.
close_reason: Both halves resolved by phux-w7z2.58 (commit 9685cf39). The 5s ACKNOWLEDGED_COMPLETION_TIMEOUT and the resulting same-Terminal RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED retry interval are now stated in docs/spec/L1.md 6.2.1, with a docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md 0.7.0-draft.4 entry. The cross-pane coupling this bead wanted documented was fixed rather than written down: the spec now says the opposite — operations against distinct Terminals proceed concurrently and one Terminal's unresolved write MUST NOT delay input to another — pinned by an_unresolved_acknowledged_write_does_not_stall_another_pane.

title: Fold phux-client/src/ask.rs's hand-rolled APPLY_INPUT onto agent_prompt::apply_input_once
description:
Wave-2 duplication, found while landing phux-w7z2.5.

crates/phux-client/src/ask.rs:256-266 builds its own Command::ApplyInput for
`phux agent answer`, independently of crates/phux-client/src/agent_prompt.rs,
which landed the ADR-0076 error contract. Two APPLY_INPUT callers now exist
with two classification tables, and only one of them:

- pessimizes INTERNAL_ERROR and unknown ErrorCode values to
  INPUT_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN (agent_prompt::classify);
- bounds the round trip past the server's undocumented 5s completion wait
  (agent_prompt::SUBMIT_DEADLINE = 8s);
- backs off RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED past the ~5s admission hold under the SAME
  operation id (agent_prompt::backoff_schedule, jittered floor 6.12s);
- preserves Reply::interleaved rather than dropping it.

Drift here is not cosmetic: the readings ARE the contract, and 'answer' and
'prompt' both write into an agent turn. Fold ask.rs onto
agent_prompt::apply_input_once + classify + submit_with_backoff, or state in
ask.rs why it must differ.
notes: Filed from phux-w7z2.5. See description for the four concrete divergences.
close_reason:
STALE BEAD, verified rather than assumed. The fold had already happened in 8d06829c ('feat(agent): add acknowledged orchestration surface', #410, Aug 9) -- the same commit that CREATED agent_prompt.rs also rewrote ask.rs::deliver_answer to call apply_input_once and share ApplyVerdict/classify. A git log -p --all search found NO committed revision of ask.rs ever containing Command::ApplyInput; the bead was filed the same day against an intermediate uncommitted draft of that PR.

Each divergence the bead named, checked individually: the INTERNAL_ERROR/unknown-code pessimization and the completion-wait bound are both inherited for free from the shared path; the RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED backoff difference is DELIBERATE and preserved (agent answer's pre-write liveness check is a GET_STATE title read matched against the caller's --id, so a multi-second backoff would go stale across exactly that window and risk landing a validated answer on a question the agent has moved past -- the one failure the verb exists to prevent); Reply::interleaved preservation is deliberate and already asserted; operation-id minting is identical modulo one helper being inlined; and the ownership-verification difference is a real API-shape distinction, not drift -- deliver_answer takes an already-connected &mut Connection and its caller owns target resolution.

Shipped only a 17-line doc addition to ask.rs recording the backoff rationale in the file itself rather than only at the CLI call site. No behaviour change.

phux-w7z2.60's not-written/unknown asymmetry confirmed intact and inherited explicitly, with both remedy-text tests passing.

SPUN OUT: phux-jzup -- crates/phux/src/commands/agent/start.rs carries a THIRD hand-rolled Command::ApplyInput whose catch-all arm treats the new InputNotWritten as ambiguous. Conservative direction, so not harmful, but it is exactly the drift this epic is about, in a file this bead never named.

title: Split the detector's identify poll: pgid every tick, argv only on change
description:
phux agent start's dominant latency is not the 3s startup grace, it is identity ACQUISITION.

Constants, read out of crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/mod.rs: IDENTIFY_ACQUIRE_WINDOW is 1500ms and is anchored at DETECTOR CONSTRUCTION (pane creation), so a pane that already existed is long past it and re-identifies on the IDENTIFY_RECHECK 5s cadence. STARTUP_GRACE is 3s anchored at IDENTIFICATION and suppresses publication entirely. TICK_IDENTIFIED is 300ms.

Timeline after agent start's command line lands in an existing pane:
  t+0        APPLY_INPUT acknowledged; the shell execs the agent
  t+0..5s    the detector's next identify tick fires   <- up to 5000ms
  t+X        identified; cadence -> 300ms
  t+X+3s     startup grace expires
  t+X+3s..   first tick that scans a dirty grid publishes  <- up to 300ms
Worst case ~8.3s, expected ~5.8s, against herdr's 3s floor. The answer is correct; the wait is just long, and every ADR-0046 consumer pays it, not only this verb.

FIX: tcgetpgrp (one ioctl) is far cheaper than process_argv (a /proc read on Linux, two sysctls on macOS). Poll foreground_pgid at the ordinary tick cadence and call process_argv only when the pgid CHANGED or the 5s recheck is due. Acquisition drops from ~5s to ~300-500ms for essentially zero added cost. apply_identity is where it lands: remember the last pgid alongside the identification and treat a pgid change as an immediate re-identify trigger.

Note this composes with phux-w7z2.43 (pgid start time), which needs the same remembered-pgid slot.
close_reason: Merged path on branch army/w7z2-50-detector-poll. tick() now does a cheap pgid-only probe between periodic rechecks and pays the full argv read only on disagreement; the periodic recheck cadence is unchanged. The pid-reuse hardening from phux-w7z2.43 is preserved BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a richer cache key: the cheap probe never makes an identity decision, it only decides whether the expensive path is worth paying for, and the actual (pgid, start-time) comparison stays inside apply_agent/apply_vacancy which the probe cannot bypass. So a same-pgid recycle is invisible to the probe and falls through to the full recheck exactly as before. Two tests pin both directions, including a regression guard that runs 5 ordinary ticks against a same-pgid/different-start-time recycle and asserts the identified occupant stays pinned to the original. Confined to agent_detect/mod.rs and identify.rs.

title: phux.pane-occupant/v1: publish the available-shell answer the CLI cannot derive
description:
phux agent start needs to know whether a pane is sitting at an idle shell prompt before it types a launch command into it. herdr's gate is three clauses: foreground pgid == the pane's child pid, the job holds only that shell, and the name is a known shell.

phux has the raw materials for clauses 1 and 3 SERVER-SIDE ONLY and already pays for them: crates/phux-server/src/proc_query.rs foreground_pgid (one tcgetpgrp) and process_argv are exactly what the ADR-0046 detector calls on its identify path, on a 5s cadence, for every PTY-backed pane. identify.rs already dash-strips a login shell's -zsh and already knows the shell names as RUNTIME_WRAPPERS. Adding 'is this a shell' to argv the detector already fetched is pure computation.

Nothing carries the answer to a client. TerminalInfo (crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/info.rs) has id, window_id, cols, rows, title, cwd and no foreground-process field, and there is no other read path.

PROPOSAL: a Terminal-scoped phux.pane-occupant/v1 L3 record written by the same detector tick, edge-filtered exactly as phux.agent/v1 is. Value {"foreground":"zsh","is_pane_shell":true} and nothing more — no pid, no argv, no cwd (proc_query deliberately never logs argv above trace). Rides the shipped SET_METADATA / METADATA_CHANGED path: no frame, no tag, no PROTOCOL_VERSION change. Precedent is exact — ADR-0046 made the server a producer of one conventional key and ADR-0068 point 6 already has it publishing a second. Cost is a normative docs/spec/L3.md section plus a CHANGELOG entry and a spec version bump.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD, and why this matters: start.rs uses a degraded client-side check — the pane must show an OSC-133 semantic mark on the CURSOR'S row (a prompt mark further up the screen is equally true while a build runs in the foreground). It is three-valued: at-prompt passes, not-at-prompt refuses on positive evidence, unanswerable refuses because shell integration is off and phux cannot see. That last case is the common one on a shell without OSC-133 integration, so today the verb refuses a lot of legitimate panes and the escape hatch is --force. This key turns that refusal into an answer.

Clause 2 (every process in the job is the shell) is declined for now: nothing in the tree enumerates a process group and it needs new platform code in the one module that already carries unsafe FFI. With job control on, clause 1 already catches a foreground vim; clause 2 only adds coverage where job control is off.
close_reason: Published server-owned phux.pane-occupant/v1 metadata from the detector existing process query, with privacy-bounded foreground basename and pane-shell boolean, edge filtering with retry-safe actor enqueue, and client SET/DELETE rejection. agent start now waits through first detection, accepts unmarked confirmed shells, refuses non-shell foreground processes, and retains contradictory OSC-133 busy evidence. Added L3 3.7.2, 0.8.0-draft.1 changelog, consumer/operations/architecture docs, parser/ownership/unit and real-PTY coverage. just ci-full passed: 3,772 workspace tests, 59 real-server journeys, latency gates, docs, fleet smoke.

title: Module cycle inventory: 18 real 2-cycles across the workspace
description:
A first pass reported 35 module-level dependency cycles. After classifying by kinship, 18 are real:

## Cross-subsystem cycles — 6 (highest concern: these cross a design boundary)

| pair | edges |
|---|---|
| `phux-server::state/client` <-> `phux-server::terminal_actor/requests` | 2 / 5 |
| `phux-relay::lib` <-> `phux-relay::tokens` | 1 / 6 |
| `phux-record::cast` <-> `phux-record::timeline` | 1 / 5 |
| `phux-protocol::input` <-> `phux-protocol::wire/frame` | 2 / 4 |
| `phux-config::plugin` <-> `phux-config::schema` | 1 / 1 |
| `phux-server::hooks` <-> `phux-server::state` | 1 / 1 |

`state/client` <-> `terminal_actor/requests` is the one to look at first: it couples the client-routing table to the actor request vocabulary in both directions, which is the same seam ADR-0014 drew.

## Sibling cycles — 12

| pair | edges |
|---|---|
| `phux-protocol::wire/decode` <-> `wire/frame` | 5 / 33 |
| `phux-client::attach/driver` <-> `attach/server_frame` | 9 / 21 |
| `phux-client::attach/driver` <-> `attach/paint` | 13 / 6 |
| `phux-protocol::wire/frame` <-> `wire/info` | 9 / 8 |
| `phux-protocol::wire/decode` <-> `wire/info` | 1 / 13 |
| `phux-server::runtime/client` <-> `runtime/commands` | 6 / 7 |
| `phux-client::attach/driver` <-> `attach/input_dispatch` | 1 / 11 |
| `phux-server::grid/reference` <-> `grid/synthesizer` | 2 / 9 |
| `phux-server::hub/link` <-> `hub/relay` | 5 / 5 |
| `phux-client-core::predict/reconcile` <-> `predict/state` | 3 / 5 |
| `phux-server::runtime/commands` <-> `runtime/input_lane` | 2 / 5 |
| `phux-server::runtime/attach` <-> `runtime/client` | 1 / 3 |

The four `attach/driver` and three `wire/*` entries are tracked separately (phux-4fbs.4 covers attach). The `wire/*` triangle — decode, frame, info all mutually referencing — is arguably inherent to a codec where the frame vocabulary and the decoder are co-recursive, and may be a documented-accept rather than a fix.

## Explicitly NOT knots (recorded so the next scan does not re-raise them)

- **14 parent-child pairs** such as `terminal_actor` <-> `terminal_actor/spawn`, `runtime` <-> `runtime/client`, `config::widget` <-> `widget/widgets` (4/81). A parent declaring types its child implements, with the child referring back, is idiomatic Rust. Not a defect.
- **3 cross-crate pairs** — `phux-client::attach/connection` <-> `phux-dial::quic`, `phux-protocol::wire/frame` <-> `phux-server::state/client`, `phux-server-testkit::builder` <-> `phux-server::runtime`. Cargo forbids circular crate deps and the real DAG is acyclic; these are same-name symbol-resolution artifacts (see phux-4fbs.3 for the `ClientId` case that causes the protocol/server one).

## Reproducing

Requires a graphify pass (`graphify-out/graph.json`), then a script that rolls AST edges up to `crate::module/submodule`, drops test and example paths, finds 2-cycles, and classifies each pair as parent-child / sibling / cross-subsystem / cross-crate. Filtering the first and last categories is what takes the count from 35 to 18.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 6 cross-subsystem cycles is either broken or has a recorded reason to keep it. The wire/* codec triangle gets an explicit accept-or-fix decision rather than being left ambiguous.
close_reason: Integrated on untangle/architecture-knots; full just ci passes.

title: attach/driver is a 5k-line hub in three mutual-dependency cycles with its own siblings
description:
`crates/phux-client/src/attach/` is the densest tangle in the workspace. Size alone is not the defect — `phux-protocol/src/wire/frame.rs` is 4,864 production lines and is fine, because a codec is mechanically long and has near-zero fan-out. The defect here is size **plus** mutual recursion across module boundaries.

## Measurements (production lines, inline `#[cfg(test)]` excluded)

| module | prod | inline test |
|---|---|---|
| attach/driver.rs | 5,168 | 2,346 |
| attach/input_dispatch.rs | 3,129 | 4,071 |
| attach/server_frame.rs | 1,791 | 3,104 |
| attach/input.rs | 1,520 | 1,036 |
| attach/connection.rs | 1,758 total | |

## Module-level fan-in / fan-out (production edges only, from the AST graph)

- `phux-client::attach/driver` — fan-in 9, fan-out 30. The highest fan-out module in the workspace.
- `phux-client::attach/connection` — fan-in 31, fan-out 6.

## The cycles

`driver` participates in three mutual-dependency pairs at once:

- `attach/driver` <-> `attach/server_frame` (9 edges out, 21 back)
- `attach/driver` <-> `attach/paint` (13 out, 6 back)
- `attach/driver` <-> `attach/input_dispatch` (1 out, 11 back)

Rust permits mutually recursive modules, so none of this is a compile error. It does mean there is no order in which to read the subsystem, and no way to test `server_frame` or `paint` without standing up `driver`.

The shape suggests `driver` is doing two jobs: owning attach lifecycle state, and being the dispatch hub every sibling calls back into. Those are separable — the usual fix is to lift the shared state into a context struct that siblings take as a parameter, leaving `driver` as a one-way orchestrator.

## Comparable second cluster

`phux-server::runtime` shows the same pattern one level down and should be assessed with it:

- `runtime/commands` — fan-in 31, fan-out 14, 3,575 production lines, zero inline tests
- `runtime` <-> `runtime/client` (10/4), `runtime/client` <-> `runtime/commands` (6/7), `runtime/commands` <-> `runtime/input_lane` (2/5)
acceptance_criteria: attach/driver no longer participates in a module cycle: shared attach state is lifted into a context passed to siblings, and server_frame, paint, and input_dispatch depend on driver one-way or not at all. Verified by re-running the module-level cycle scan and finding no pair involving attach/driver.
close_reason: Integrated on untangle/architecture-knots; full just ci passes.

title: Same-name different-meaning types across the core/wire/server seam
description:
17 type names are defined in more than one crate. Most are harmless homonyms in unrelated domains. A few are the same *domain concept* modeled twice with different semantics, and those are the ones that mislead a reader and defeat tooling.

## Genuinely hazardous — same concept, different semantics, same name

- **`ClientId`** — `phux_protocol::ids::ClientId(u32)` (wire identity, macro-generated by `id_type!` in ids.rs:54) versus `phux_server::state::client::ClientId(u64)` (server routing identity, client.rs:22). Different width, different lifetime, different authority. The server side documents the distinction at client.rs:17-20; the protocol side does not. This pair is why graph tooling reported a phantom `phux-protocol -> phux-server` dependency: six `references` edges in wire/frame.rs and wire/info.rs resolve `ClientId` to the server's node.
- **`TerminalId`** — `phux_core::ids::TerminalId` (a slotmap `new_key_type!` arena handle) versus `phux_protocol::ids::TerminalId` (a `Local`/`Satellite` wire enum). Bridged by `IdSpace`. Two genuinely different things sharing a name across the layer boundary they are bridged over.
- **`AttachError`** — phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs:782 versus phux-server/src/state/client.rs:85. Client-side and server-side failure vocabularies for the same handshake.
- **`HistoryRejectionReason`** — phux-client-core/src/session.rs:43 versus phux-protocol/src/wire/frame.rs:894.
- **`WindowInfo`** — phux-config/src/widget/mod.rs:123 versus phux-protocol/src/wire/info.rs:183.

## Deliberate and documented, leave alone

- `SplitDir`, `LayoutNode`, `Direction`, `LayoutError` — the layout mirrors. Covered by phux-4fbs.1; the rationale is sound, only the guard is missing.

## Benign homonyms, no action

- `Fault` (config check versus testkit), `Scope` (L3 metadata scope versus search scope), `Rect` (layout cells versus raster pixels), `Theme` (TUI versus recording raster), `CellStyle` (config widget versus core screen), `Session` (core domain versus web client).
- `WsReader` / `WsWriter` — phux-client/src/attach/connection.rs:204,211 versus phux-dial/src/ws.rs:245,252. Verified NOT duplication: the client types wrap the dial types (`inner: ws::WsReader`) to add framing and bootstrap limits. A decorator sharing its subject's name. Mildly confusing, not wrong.

## Why it is worth a pass

Beyond reader confusion, same-name-different-crate defeats symbol-resolution tooling — it is what made a clean acyclic Cargo DAG look like it had twelve cycles. Renaming the hazardous five to say what they are (`WireClientId` versus `RoutingClientId`, or per-crate `Wire*` prefixes at the import site, which several modules already do ad hoc: `use phux_protocol::ids::TerminalId as WireTerminalId`) makes the seam legible.
acceptance_criteria: The five hazardous pairs are disambiguated, either by rename at the definition or by a consistently applied import-site alias convention documented in docs/CONVENTIONS.md. The ad hoc 'as WireTerminalId' pattern already in state/id_space.rs becomes the stated rule rather than a local habit.
close_reason: Integrated on untangle/architecture-knots; full just ci passes.

title: The occupant-kind correction does not reach panes running the Claude shim
description:
Known, deliberate limitation of the phux-w7z2.27 fix, flagged by two agents
independently and decided by neither. Filed so it is a recorded decision
rather than a silent gap.

THE INTERACTION. phux-w7z2.26's shim now writes `--name claude --kind claude`
on every hook. crates/phux-server/src/agent_state.rs note_explicit_set
therefore marks those panes `explicit_identity` AND `explicit_kind`. compose
then PRESERVES that kind, because docs/spec/L3.md 3.7 requires a server to
"preserve the `name`, `kind`, and `session` fields of an identity-only
declaration".

CONSEQUENCE: on a claude -> codex handover in a shim-driven pane, the record
lands on {name: claude, kind: claude, state: unknown} and then takes codex's
DERIVED state while still reading kind: claude. That is precisely the failure
phux-w7z2.27 was filed to fix, surviving on the largest population of panes.

IT IS NOT A BUG IN THE FIX. It is the ruling and the spec applied literally:
the kind belongs to an explicit writer, and the server does not overwrite what
an explicit writer set. `compose_preserves_an_explicitly_set_kind` pins this
as intended behavior. `phux agent clear`, or the next shim hook on the new
occupant, resolves it.

WHAT TO DECIDE, and it is a genuine fork:

(a) Accept it and document it — an explicit `kind` is the writer's
    responsibility to keep accurate, which is already true of an explicit
    `name`.
(b) Have the shim stop writing `--kind`, leaving kind to the detector. The
    detector identifies claude from argv anyway, so the shim's `--kind` adds
    nothing the detector cannot derive, and dropping it would put shim panes
    back under the correction. Cheapest option; check what depends on the kind
    being present BEFORE the detector's first tick.
(c) Amend L3.md 3.7's MUST-preserve list to let a server correct a `kind` it
    has positive evidence is wrong. A spec change with an ADR amendment and a
    CHANGELOG entry; the highest-ceremony option and probably not worth it.

Note phux-w7z2.37 may change the shim's hook shape substantially. Resolve that
one first — if the shim ends up writing identity once at session start, the
population and frequency of this interaction both change.

RELATED: ADR-0075's %name work is a downstream consumer of a trustworthy
`kind`.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: Stale docs: install-claude clap help and operations.md still claim the shim publishes lifecycle state
description:
Doc drift created by the phux-w7z2.26 fix, in files outside that change's
ownership. All three statements are now FALSE: the shim declares identity only
and writes no `state` at all.

1. crates/phux/src/commands/agent/mod.rs:180 — the clap doc for InstallClaude
   reads "Make plain `claude` launch inside phux and publish lifecycle state".
   This REGENERATES into docs/reference/cli.md:213 and :287, so both are stale
   too.

   IMPORTANT: do not hand-edit docs/reference/cli.md (ADR-0069 — it is
   generated). Edit the clap doc, then run `just docs-gen` IN THE SAME COMMIT,
   or refdocs::tests::generated_reference_docs_match_the_tree fails. That
   coupling is why this was left alone rather than fixed in passing.

2. docs/operations.md:142-144 — "The shim injects additional Claude hook
   settings for lifecycle publication: prompts set `working`,
   permissions/notifications set `blocked` and emit `phux ask`, stops set
   `done`, and session exit clears the record." Only the `phux ask` and the
   session-exit clear survive; the three state writes are gone.

3. docs/consumers/agents.md:956 (approximate, in the AgentWaitJson section)
   distinguished "`done` written by a lifecycle hook (`agent_record`
   provenance)" from screen-guessed `done`. ALREADY FIXED on this branch —
   listed here only so nobody re-reports it.

Suggested replacement wording for 1: "Make plain `claude` launch inside phux
and declare its agent identity." docs/consumers/agents.md's install-claude
entry already carries the full corrected explanation and can be the source of
truth to copy from.

NOTE: `just docs-check` does NOT catch any of this — it gates frontmatter,
TL;DR blocks and link shape, not semantic drift. Green CI said nothing here.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: Hook-sourced agent state: a REPORT_AGENT_STATE command that restores a done producer
description:
Deferred from phux-w7z2.26 by explicit ruling, with the reason recorded so it
is not re-litigated: this is the right END STATE and it was not the right
change for a five-bug fix branch.

THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES. A lifecycle hook is genuinely better evidence than a
screen rule — it knows the instant a turn starts and the instant it ends. But
today a hook can only express that by writing the record, and writing a
`state` into the record stands the server's derivation down on that pane for
the record's lifetime (L3.md 3.7, ADR-0046 point 8). So the shim had to choose
between hook-quality evidence and a live detector, and phux-w7z2.26 chose the
detector. The cost is written down there and in docs/consumers/agents.md:
`done` now has ZERO producers anywhere in the shipped binary, and `working` /
`blocked` carry up to one detect tick of extra latency.

THE SHAPE. A new command that lets a hook feed the DETECTOR rather than
overwrite the record — the hook becomes a high-priority evidence source that
the arbiter composes with screen and title evidence, instead of a writer that
silences them. That restores `done` (the only value no observation can
honestly produce) and restores hook timing, without reintroducing the latch.

WHY NOT ON THE FIX BRANCH. Command tag 0x16 is free (PUT_FILE = 0x15 is the
highest allocated command; the 0x16 that already exists is
TYPE_HISTORY_REQUEST, a FRAME type in a different namespace). But allocating a
command tag is an additive WIRE change, and ADR-0059's PUT_FILE bumped
PROTOCOL_VERSION 0.5.0 -> 0.6.0 for exactly that. So this needs a minor
protocol bump, a negotiation question, a new normative spec section, and its
own ADR. That is a feature landing inside a bugfix branch.

SCHEDULING CONSTRAINT: ADR-0071 is Proposed and freezes the CLI JSON surface
for 1.0. This adds wire surface, not CLI surface, but any accompanying verb
must land before that freeze or be carved into it.

ACCEPTANCE: an ADR; docs/spec/L1.md section 5.1 gains the command; a
docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md entry with the PROTOCOL_VERSION bump; the Claude shim
uses it; `done` has a producer again and docs/consumers/agents.md's `agent
wait` caveat about `done` is updated to say so.
close_reason: Added capability-gated REPORT_AGENT_STATE at command tag 0x17 and protocol 0.8. Hook working/blocked/done evidence enters the existing detector without latching metadata; pre-identity edges get a bounded startup grace and later screen/process evidence can supersede them. Claude shim schema 4 emits lifecycle reports, agent wait --until done is enabled, ADR/spec/CLI docs updated. just ci-full passed after rebase onto current main.

title: Move phux agent send-keys onto APPLY_INPUT once agent prompt lands
description:
Deliberate scope deviation recorded when phux-w7z2.7 was closed in wave 2. Filed so it is not lost.

phux-w7z2.7 specified that agent send-keys rides APPLY_INPUT for the same receipt semantics as agent prompt. agent prompt does not exist yet, so the shipped verb rides ROUTE_INPUT, fire-and-forget, in crates/phux/src/commands/agent/send_keys.rs. Both behaviours the bead actually named - all-or-nothing key validation before any byte is written, and the agent-ownership refusal - are real and tested. What is missing is the receipt.

THE OBSERVABLE CONSEQUENCE TODAY, and it is written into the shipped help text: the route-failure remedy deliberately does NOT say retry, because all-or-nothing covers validation and not delivery, and once a ROUTE_INPUT is acked those bytes are in the tty input queue. A caller that sees a transport failure cannot tell whether the keys landed. APPLY_INPUT with an ADR-0053 operation id is what makes that answerable, and it is the same idempotency property agent prompt exists to provide.

DEPENDS on phux-w7z2.5. When doing it, inherit the typed-error readings from ADR-0076 rather than re-deriving them - in particular the wave-2 correction that INPUT_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN is terminal and exits 1, NOT 3. Also inherit the ACK-is-a-kernel-queue-receipt framing: an OK proves the bytes reached the PTY master, which is strictly more than ROUTE_INPUT states and strictly less than consumption.

Also re-check the identity re-verification at that point. Today it shares one connection with the ROUTE_INPUT batch, ids 1 then 2, with a staleness bound of one server frame-handling turn on that connection. An APPLY_INPUT batch must preserve that ordering property or the bound stops holding.
acceptance_criteria: agent send-keys delivers over APPLY_INPUT with an operation id, an idempotency test reusing an operation id, and the staleness bound in the module docs re-verified against the new frame ordering.
notes: IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE in feat/agent-epic-fanout and full nix develop -c just ci is green (3525 passed, 72 skipped). Left open because Beads correctly blocks closure on unresolved human ADR ratification phux-w7z2.1 (or, for downstream items, on a bead blocked by it); do not reimplement.

title: Fold the four new agent error codes into json_err::codes so the closed vocabulary claim is true again
description:
Owed follow-up from wave 2, and it is a documentation-truth problem, not tidying.

WHAT HAPPENED. phux agent wait and phux agent send-keys shipped four new JSON error codes - no_agent_record at exit 2, agent_departed at exit 1, agent_mismatch at exit 2 and invalid_key_spec at exit 2. They live in PRIVATE mod codes blocks inside crates/phux/src/commands/agent/wait.rs and crates/phux/src/commands/agent/send_keys.rs, each with a comment saying they belong in json_err. They were put there deliberately because crates/phux/src/commands/json_err.rs was held by a concurrent change in the same wave, which was the right call at the time.

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC. docs/consumers/agents.md 5.3 documented a CLOSED CODE VOCABULARY living in one file. That claim became false the moment these landed. The wave-2 docs pass documented the four codes, because a consumer needs them, and NARROWED the parenthetical rather than asserting a single-file vocabulary that no longer holds. So the docs are honest and the code is fragmented, and the next verb author has two plausible homes to choose from and no reason to prefer either.

TASK: move the four consts into crates/phux/src/commands/json_err.rs codes, delete the private blocks, and revert the narrowed parenthetical in docs/consumers/agents.md 5.3 to the single-file claim. Verify each code exit mapping against crates/phux/src/exit_codes.rs while doing it - the wave-2 docs pass already checked them, so a mismatch found here means something drifted.

Cheap, and it should be done before any further agent verb adds a fifth private block.
acceptance_criteria: grep for mod codes under crates/phux/src/commands/agent returns nothing, all four codes are in json_err::codes, and docs/consumers/agents.md 5.3 states a single-file closed vocabulary again.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).
