title: SnapshotSynthesizer: distinguish wide-cell tails from blank cells via cell.wide()
description:
Surfaced in 460faeb. crates/phux-server/src/grid.rs::synthesize emits a space for any cell where cell.graphemes().is_empty() — covers both genuinely-blank cells AND wide-cell tails (the right half of '東', emoji, etc.). Affects snapshot fidelity for wide-character content.

Fix: use libghostty's CellIteration::raw_cell() then Cell::wide() to discriminate. When wide() indicates a tail position, skip emission (the base grapheme already advanced the cursor past it). Otherwise emit space.

Test: round-trip a snapshot containing CJK + emoji through Synthesizer → fresh Terminal → assert grid equivalence. Use the existing synthesizer_round_trips_via_libghostty test as the pattern.

Blocks: nothing critical, but affects byc.8's PANE_SNAPSHOT correctness for any pane content with wide graphemes.
close_reason: Landed in commit e8b92e8 via PR #19 (with the underlying grid.rs fix already on main in 5c0cb82). PR added CJK+emoji round-trip test (synthesizer_round_trips_cjk_and_emoji) hardening regression coverage via CellIteration::raw_cell()?.wide() = CellWide::SpacerTail.

title: RenderState::update second-call diagnosis (deferred from 460faeb)
description:
Wave-2 agent's regression test (call render() twice in a row, assert Dirty::Clean on second) hit Error::InvalidValue from libghostty. Agent dropped the test rather than diagnose. Production paths (server SnapshotSynthesizer + client PaneRenderer) work fine — they each call snapshot.set_dirty(Dirty::Clean) between updates. The contract IS clear from libghostty source: Snapshot holds &mut RenderState; you can update again after Snapshot drops.

InvalidValue comes from .dirty().and_then(|v| v.try_into().map_err(|_| Error::InvalidValue)) — FFI returned a Dirty value outside {Clean, Partial, Full}. Likely the test was missing the set_dirty(Clean) reset between updates, OR libghostty returns an out-of-band Dirty value in a specific scenario the agent didn't characterize.

Tiny investigation: reconstruct the failing test scenario, find the actual cause, either fix the test or file a libghostty upstream issue if the FFI is returning an unmodeled value.
notes: Re-prioritized 2026-05-26 from P3 → P2: this becomes load-bearing for state-sync per ADR-0018 addendum. State-sync's tick driver calls snapshot.dirty() per consumer per tick on the same RenderState across many updates. The FFI InvalidValue case the deferred test hit (Dirty value outside {Clean, Partial, Full}) must be either characterized (so the synthesizer can guard against it) or fixed upstream before phux-q0e.A ships. See phux-q0e (epic) for the dependent work.
close_reason: Diagnosed via PR #5: Outcome B (upstream FFI bug in libghostty-vt rev 31d1f70 at Snapshot::set — passes *const *const T to C instead of *const T). Calling Snapshot::set_dirty(_) poisons the next update's dirty() read with InvalidValue, value-agnostic. Diagnostic test in crates/phux-server/tests/phux_l0t_dirty_diagnosis.rs pins the contract. Existing .unwrap_or(Dirty::Full) workarounds in client renderer and server synthesize_incremental implement strict over-emission, preserving ADR-0018 loss-tolerance. Dirty::Clean/Partial fast paths are dead code in any pipeline that calls mark_synced until upstream is fixed. Upstream issue to file as follow-up.

title: phux-server::downsample: handle image protocols + keyboard protocol gating + OSC 8 stripping
description:
Follow-up to ADR-0013 byte-stream rewriter landing. The v0 rewrite_bytes() in phux-server::downsample handles truecolor SGR -> indexed256/16 only. SPEC §6.2 requires additional gating per client caps:

- Image protocols: drop or transform sixel (DCS) / kitty graphics (APC G) / iTerm2 (OSC 1337) when the client did not advertise the matching ImageProtocol bit. The OSC/DCS/APC passthrough is permissive today; needs a capability-gated drop path.
- Kitty keyboard protocol: APC keyboard-reply sequences must be stripped from the outbound stream for clients that did not negotiate the matching kbd_protocols bit. The canonical Terminal still processes them locally.
- OSC 8 hyperlinks: strip when ClientCapabilities.hyperlinks == false.
- ITU-style colon separators: the rewriter currently only recognises ';'. tmux handles both 'CSI 38;2;R;G;B m' and 'CSI 38:2::R:G:B m'; add the colon variant for parity.

Scope: code only (crates/phux-server/src/downsample.rs + tests). No SPEC changes needed — §6.2 already mandates the behavior; this is implementation catch-up.
notes: Follow-up filed as phux-4rj (ClientCapabilities wiring).
close_reason: Landed on main as 0b2b5f5 (cherry-picked from fanout/phux-9gz-downsample). downsample.rs now handles: sixel (DCS) / kitty graphics (APC G) / iTerm2 (OSC 1337) image protocol stripping; kitty keyboard APC stripping distinct from APC graphics; OSC 8 hyperlink stripping (text between OSCs preserved); ITU colon-separator SGR (CSI 38:2::R:G:B m) treated equivalently to semicolon variant, including empty colourspace field. 20 new tests (38 total in module). See follow-up phux-XXX for wiring real ClientCapabilities through.

title: SPEC cleanup: §12 flow control + §2 terminology + Appendix B + §11.1 ADR ref + §6.2 RenderingMode
description:
Post-ADR-0013 SPEC inconsistencies surfaced by the §8 rewrite agent (commit 2071f8f). Out-of-scope of that commit; needs a single small cleanup pass:

1. §12 Flow control still references PANE_DIFF and frame_id-based FRAME_ACK. Update to PANE_OUTPUT and per-pane seq.
2. §2 Terminology 'Frame' definition still uses frame_id. Reword to: 'frame: a server-emitted PANE_OUTPUT carrying a contiguous batch of VT bytes for one pane, identified by a monotonically increasing per-pane seq.'
3. Appendix B Reserved ranges still mentions DiffOp tag allocation guidance. Drop or replace with NamedKey/ErrorCode-only guidance.
4. §11.1 'What is deliberately absent' cross-references ADR-0002 (superseded). Repoint to ADR-0013 or to the appropriate post-supersession ADR.
5. §6.2 RenderingMode { Diff | VtReplay } kept for forward-compat but deprecated in prose; a future major-version SPEC removes the field entirely. File a separate v0.2 ticket if/when major bump happens.

Single-commit cleanup. Scope: SPEC.md only. No code touched.
close_reason: Already complete per SPEC.md Appendix C draft.4 changelog (2026-05-26). Verified in main: §2 Frame term re-anchored on per-Terminal seq (line 95); §6.2 RenderingMode deprecated in prose (line 318-322); §11.1 ADR ref points at ADR-0013 (line 1421-1423); §12 flow control uses TERMINAL_OUTPUT + per-Terminal seq (line 1427+); Appendix B explicitly drops DiffOp guidance (line 1898-1900). Ticket was filed but cleanup landed in the same wave that prompted it. No-op close.

title: phux-server: handle ATTACH frame and respond with ATTACHED + PANE_SNAPSHOT
description:
The server's per-client task in crates/phux-server/src/runtime.rs::handle_client today only handles FrameKind::Ping. The match arm for FrameKind::Attach / FrameKind::Detach / FrameKind::Input* falls through to a debug log and the connection sits idle. byc.6 (the integration tests) is blocked on this handler existing.

Under ADR-0013 the response sequence to ATTACH is bytes-on-wire:

1. Resolve target -> SessionId via ServerState.
2. Allocate per-client mpsc + spawn writer task draining into the UnixStream.
3. Build SessionSnapshot from the registry; send FrameKind::Attached { snapshot, initial_client_id }.
4. For each pane in the focused window: call phux_server::grid::SnapshotSynthesizer::synthesize(&terminal) to produce { cols, rows, vt_replay_bytes }, then send FrameKind::PaneSnapshot { pane_id, cols, rows, vt_replay_bytes, scrollback_bytes: None } per SPEC §8.4 / §13.
5. Subsequent live output flows as FrameKind::PaneOutput { pane_id, seq, bytes } -- the per-pane PTY pump + downsample::rewrite_bytes path that byc.5 covers.

On FrameKind::Detach: send Detached and drop the writer.

On AttachError::UnknownSession: send an ERROR frame with code SESSION_NOT_FOUND (102 per SPEC §14). Requires the ERROR variant — see follow-up phux-byc.9.

Acceptance: byc.6 tests #1, #2, #5 must pass once this and the ERROR-variant ticket land.

## Required Skills
rust,tokio,ipc,libghostty
design:
On receiving FrameKind::Attach { target, viewport, request_scrollback, scrollback_limit_lines }:
1. Resolve target → SessionId via ServerState (AttachTarget::ByName lookup is implemented; ById / Last / CreateIfMissing per SPEC §13).
2. Allocate a per-client mpsc channel and call ServerState::attach(client_id, name, tx).
3. Spawn a writer task draining the mpsc into the UnixStream's write half.
4. Build a SessionSnapshot from the registry and send FrameKind::Attached { snapshot, initial_client_id }.
5. For each pane in the session's active window, send FrameKind::PaneSnapshot per SPEC §13 attach sequence.

On FrameKind::Detach: send FrameKind::Detached, then drop the writer (which closes the socket on the server side).

On AttachError::UnknownSession: send an ERROR frame with code SESSION_NOT_FOUND (102 per SPEC §14). Requires the ERROR variant — see follow-up ticket.

Acceptance: byc.6 tests #1, #2, #5 must pass once this and the ERROR-variant ticket land.

title: Conform DiffOp to SPEC §8.1/§8.5: cursor + modes as PANE_DIFF fields, not ops
description:
SPEC §8.1 defines `PANE_DIFF` as carrying `cursor: CursorState`, `modes: PaneModes`, and `base_frame_id`/`revision` as **struct fields**, not as entries in the `ops` list. SPEC §8.5 is explicit on the rationale: "pulling them out into separate messages would increase wire chatter for no benefit." The current implementation models cursor as `DiffOp::CursorMove { row, col }` (op-byte 0x03) and `DiffOp::CursorStyle { visible, shape, blink }` (op-byte 0x04), and the `PaneDiff` frame body has no cursor / modes / base_frame_id / revision fields.

Why now: scope is small (one server example, one client mirror, a handful of tests). As more compute/apply/render code lands, the op-stream shape will calcify and the migration will be harder. Wire format is breaking — no external consumer yet — so do it before anyone latches.

Surgical edit list:
- crates/phux-protocol/src/diff/op.rs: delete `DiffOp::CursorMove` and `DiffOp::CursorStyle` variants
- crates/phux-protocol/src/diff/cursor.rs (new): re-home `CursorState`, `CursorShape`, add `PaneModes` bitset
- crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/diff.rs: delete op-byte 0x03/0x04 encode/decode + proptest strategy entries
- crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/frame.rs: `PaneDiff` gains `base_frame_id: u64`, `cursor: CursorState`, `modes: PaneModes`, `revision: u8`
- crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/decode.rs: decode the new fields
- crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/field.rs: add field-ID constants for new PaneDiff fields
- crates/phux-protocol/src/diff/compute.rs: stop emitting cursor ops; return cursor + modes alongside ops
- crates/phux-client/src/mirror/apply.rs: drop CursorMove/CursorStyle match arms; consume cursor+modes from PaneDiff
- crates/phux-client/src/mirror/state.rs: track modes (or pipe through)
- crates/phux-server/examples/diff_spike.rs and one_pane.rs: update to new compute_diff signature
- Tests: regenerate snapshots, append new cursor-field + modes round-trip tests, replace existing CursorMove/CursorStyle tests

title: Migrate wire encoder to TLV (SPEC Appendix A)
description:
Migrate the phux-protocol wire encoder from positional field encoding to TLV per SPEC.md Appendix A: {field_id: varint, wire_type: u8, value}.

## Why
The current encoder in crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/encode.rs writes fields positionally. This makes ANY extension to an existing frame body a wire-breaking change: e.g., adding a field to PaneSnapshotPayload, SessionInfo, or ATTACH requires a major-version bump because decoders cannot skip unknown trailing fields without TLV envelopes.

SPEC.md Appendix A mandates TLV precisely to make additive evolution backwards-compatible:
- Field IDs in crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/field.rs are ALREADY defined but unused by the encoder/decoder — they were laid down anticipating this migration.
- §6 obliges decoders to skip unknown fields by length, which TLV's self-delimiting structure makes mechanical.

## Cascade
This commit's spec-conformance pass for ATTACH/ATTACHED/PANE_SNAPSHOT/SessionInfo/WindowInfo/PaneInfo (followup to phux-4az) papers over the issue: it matches SPEC §13 shapes exactly but keeps the positional encoder. Any future field addition to those shapes is a breaking wire change today.

## Scope
- Replace primitive writes in Encoder/Decoder with field-tagged writes consuming field.rs constants.
- Define varint and tagged-union (wire_type=7) encoding per Appendix A.
- Maintain MAX_FRAME_LEN, big-endian, and existing decode-error semantics.
- Update all FrameKind variants to emit TLV bodies.
- Regenerate all wire snapshots.
- Add round-trip tests for unknown-field skipping (forward-compat invariant).

## Out of scope
- Schema versioning beyond what SPEC §6 already prescribes.
- Removing positional helpers used by sub-records (DiffOp encoding is unchanged unless we choose to TLV-ify it; that's a separate decision).
notes: REBASE ASSESSMENT 2026-05-29: wave5-tlv (commit ebb8770) is 21 commits BEHIND main, 1 ahead. The TLV commit is 2305 insertions / 67 files (encode.rs+decode.rs rewrite, ~40 .snap fixtures, wire_roundtrip.rs +738, spec). Since the branch point (merge-base 2460eeb), main added +310 lines to frame.rs (the 4li frame set: GetMetadata/ListMetadata/SpawnTerminal/TerminalResize/etc.) and +31 to decode.rs. So a git rebase is NOT viable as a fast-forward: it conflicts in frame.rs/decode.rs AND the ~15 newer frame variants would have no TLV encoding. Treat as a FRESH re-migration on current main using ebb8770 as the design reference, not a cherry-pick/rebase. Estimate: large (multi-hour), high snapshot churn. Defer behind the small additive wire items (4r1, ign).

title: phux-client attach loop: connect, render mirror, propagate input
description:
The base attach loop that 9gw.1 (predictive echo) was implicitly waiting on. Connects to a phux-server over UDS, sends HELLO + ATTACH, accumulates diff frames into a DiffMirror (9gw.2), forwards local keypress/mouse/focus/paste events upstream, and renders the mirror to the outer terminal (crossterm or direct VT writes). This is what makes 'phux attach <session>' a working command.

## Required Skills
rust,tokio,tui,vt-rendering
design:
Module: crates/phux-client/src/attach/
  connection.rs  — UDS connect, framed read/write halves
  loop.rs        — main attach loop (tokio select! over: server frames, stdin bytes from outer terminal, resize signals)
  render.rs      — VT emission from DiffMirror to stdout (crossterm or raw escapes; pick simplest first)
  input.rs       — read raw VT bytes from stdin, parse via libghostty's input layer, encode as INPUT_KEY/INPUT_MOUSE/etc, send upstream

Lifecycle:
  - parse args (server socket path, session name)
  - enter raw mode + alt screen on outer terminal
  - connect UDS, exchange HELLO, send ATTACH
  - on receive ATTACHED { snapshot }: ingest_snapshot into DiffMirror, full render
  - loop:
      tokio::select! {
        frame = framed_reader.next() => apply ops to mirror; redraw changed region
        stdin_bytes = stdin.read() => parse to InputEvent[]; send each upstream
        sigwinch = signal::unix::signal(SIGWINCH).recv() => send RESIZE to server
        ctrl+b d (or whatever the detach key is) => send DETACH; exit cleanly
      }
  - on exit: restore outer terminal (leave alt screen, disable raw mode)

Scope guard: does NOT implement predictive echo (that's 9gw.1, layers on top of this).

Depends on:
  - phux-9gw.2 (DiffMirror) ✓
  - phux-byc.3 (server runtime + UDS listener)
  - phux-byc.4 (ATTACH/DETACH lifecycle)
  - phux-6yl.* (wire codec, input event encoding)

Verify:
  cargo nextest run -p phux-client
  Manual: terminal A runs `phux serve`, terminal B runs `phux attach default`,
    typed keys appear in the inner shell and inner shell output renders.
acceptance_criteria: phux attach <session> connects, renders the active pane, propagates input, and detaches cleanly. cargo nextest run -p phux-client green. Manual test in two terminals works.

title: Integration test: server + synthetic client message exchange
description:
End-to-end harness that spins up a phux-server process (or in-process runtime), drives it with a synthetic client over the wire codec, and asserts the full HELLO → ATTACH → INPUT → diff-stream → DETACH lifecycle. Captures the byc epic's overall acceptance criteria.

## Required Skills
rust,tokio,integration-testing
design:
New: crates/phux-server/tests/end_to_end.rs

Harness approach (in-process, no subprocess fork):
  let socket = tempdir().path().join('phux.sock');
  let server = tokio::spawn(phux_server::runtime::run_with_shutdown(socket.clone(), shutdown_rx));
  // give it a moment to bind
  let client = UnixStream::connect(&socket).await?;
  let (mut reader, mut writer) = phux_protocol::codec::framed(client);

Scenarios to assert (one #[tokio::test] each, or one parameterized):

1. handshake_roundtrip:
   - Client sends HELLO with proto version
   - Server responds HELLO_ACK with negotiated capabilities (SPEC §6)
2. attach_returns_snapshot:
   - Client sends ATTACH(session='default')
   - Receives ATTACHED with SessionId + a pane snapshot frame
3. input_routes_to_pane:
   - After ATTACH, send INPUT_KEY('a')
   - Assert the pane's input log contains the encoded byte (stub from byc.4)
4. detach_clean_shutdown:
   - Send DETACH; receive DETACHED; the connection drains; no panics.
5. server_survives_mid_frame_disconnect:
   - Client writes a partial frame (half a length prefix) then drops the
     stream. Server must NOT panic; the per-client task exits cleanly.

Then shutdown_tx.send(()).await; server.await??; assert socket file unlinked.

Note: this test depends on byc.3 (runtime+socket) and byc.4 (ATTACH/DETACH).
Should be the LAST byc task to land.
acceptance_criteria: All 5 scenarios pass. cargo nextest run -p phux-server --test end_to_end green. No flakes under --test-threads=1.
close_reason: Landed on main as 07c2b37 (cherry-picked from fanout/phux-byc5-e2e). 5 scenarios in crates/phux-server/tests/end_to_end.rs: handshake_hello_no_reply (substitute for handshake_roundtrip - server consumes HELLO silently), attach_returns_snapshot, input_routes_to_pane (cat PTY fixture), detach_clean_shutdown, server_survives_mid_frame_disconnect. Each under 0.2s. Full phux-server crate 779/779 green.

title: phux-server: ATTACH/DETACH lifecycle + multi-client keystroke merge
description:
Implement the ATTACH/DETACH message handlers and the multi-client merge semantics: multiple clients attached to the same session see the same pane, with their keystrokes interleaved in arrival order at the PTY.

## Required Skills
rust,tokio,ipc
design:
Spec refs:
  SPEC.md:238-282 §7.1/7.2 Client/Server message catalog (ATTACH, ATTACHED)
  SPEC.md:283-308 §7.3 DETACH/DETACHED
  SPEC.md:955-1015 §10.1-10.2 Sessions/Panes

Builds on byc.3's per-client task and byc.1's Registry.

Server-side state:
  pub struct AttachedClient {
      id: ClientId,
      session: SessionId,
      tx: mpsc::Sender<ServerFrame>,  // server → client outbound frames
  }
  pub struct ServerState {
      registry: phux_core::Registry,
      attached: HashMap<ClientId, AttachedClient>,
      pane_subscribers: HashMap<PaneId, Vec<ClientId>>,
  }

ATTACH handler:
  - On ATTACH(session_name), look up SessionId (or create if not found and
    allowed by attach flags), register the AttachedClient in pane_subscribers
    for the active pane.
  - Send ATTACHED response with SessionId + initial pane snapshot.

DETACH handler:
  - Remove ClientId from pane_subscribers; close mpsc tx; respond DETACHED.

INPUT_KEY / INPUT_MOUSE / INPUT_FOCUS / INPUT_PASTE handlers:
  - For each input message from an attached client, route it to the
    server-side per-pane channel that ultimately writes to the PTY (PTY
    wiring lives in phux-bc1.2; for now route to a stub Pane::ingest_key
    method that just records the event).
  - Order: a SINGLE mpsc per pane consumes inputs from all attached
    clients. Whatever ordering the tokio scheduler delivers IS the
    arrival order — this is the multi-client merge contract.

Test (crates/phux-server/tests/multi_client_merge.rs):
  - Spin up server with one session/window/pane
  - Connect two synthetic UnixStream clients, both ATTACH same session
  - Each client sends a sequence of distinct INPUT_KEY events
  - Assert: the per-pane input log contains every key from both clients
    exactly once, in some interleaving (not strictly deterministic, but
    every key appears).
acceptance_criteria: ATTACH/DETACH round-trips. Two attached clients on the same session both see the same active pane. Per-pane input log records every keystroke from both clients exactly once. Integration test green.
close_reason: wave 6 swarm (byc.4 state scaffold + mdBook + crates.io). Wire integration deferred to phux-byc.6 pending phux-4az.

title: phux-server: tokio current-thread runtime + Unix socket listener
description:
Wire phux-server's main loop on a tokio current-thread runtime. Bind a Unix domain socket at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/phux/phux.sock (or fallback), accept client connections, hand each off to a per-client task that speaks the wire codec from phux-6yl.4.

## Required Skills
rust,tokio,unix-sockets
design:
Spec refs:
  SPEC.md:96-116 §4 Transport (UDS, framing assumptions)
  SPEC.md:117-149 §5 Framing (length-prefixed TLV from phux-6yl.4/5)

New: crates/phux-server/src/runtime.rs
  pub struct ServerRuntime { registry: phux_core::Registry, socket_path: PathBuf, ... }
  pub fn run(socket_path: PathBuf) -> Result<(), ServerError>:
    - Build tokio Builder::new_current_thread().enable_all().build()
    - block_on(async move { serve_loop(...).await })

serve_loop:
  - Bind UnixListener::bind(socket_path)
  - Loop: accept().await → spawn client task
  - On SIGINT/SIGTERM (use tokio::signal): drain accept loop, drop listener,
    unlink socket file. Existing client tasks get a cancellation token.

Per-client task:
  - Frame reader: phux_protocol::codec::FrameReader<UnixStream read half>
  - Frame writer: phux_protocol::codec::FrameWriter<UnixStream write half>
  - For byc.3 specifically: just LOG every incoming frame and respond with
    PONG to PING. Full message routing comes in byc.4.

Socket path resolution: \$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/phux/phux.sock if set,
else /tmp/phux-\$UID/phux.sock. Create the parent dir with 0700 perms.

Refuse to run if the socket file already exists AND a process holds it
(connect-probe). If stale, unlink and proceed.

Tests:
  - integration test in crates/phux-server/tests/socket_lifecycle.rs:
    spawn server in a temp dir, connect a tokio UnixStream, send a PING,
    read PONG, shut server down via the cancellation token, assert socket
    file is removed.
acceptance_criteria: Server binds UDS, accepts a connection, round-trips PING→PONG. Clean shutdown unlinks socket. Integration test in tests/socket_lifecycle.rs green.
close_reason: wave 5 swarm (4 agent retries + manual completion of all 4)

title: Selection / copy-mode protocol + libghostty selection APIs
description:
tmux copy-mode is one of its defining features; we need a peer. libghostty PR #12794 (merged 2026-05-24) adds selection APIs to libghostty-vt's C surface: select_word, select_line, select_all, select_output, format_buf, selection_adjust, selection_order, selection_contains, selection_equal. Wire these through phux's protocol so clients can drive copy-mode against the canonical server-side selection state.

Defer until libghostty-rs wraps the new C APIs (track via libghostty-rs commits — they were already integrating at the time of phux's wave 1).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Wire format additions in SPEC.md: SELECTION_BEGIN, SELECTION_ADJUST, SELECTION_FORMAT_REQUEST, SELECTION_FORMAT_RESPONSE, SELECTION_CLEAR. Per-pane, per-client (each client has its own selection).
- [ ] phux-server bridges to libghostty_vt::selection::* (once libghostty-rs wraps them).
- [ ] phux-client renders selection as a visual overlay on the diff mirror.
- [ ] Copy-mode keybind (default `Ctrl-b [`) enters selection mode; arrows adjust; Enter copies to clipboard via libghostty_vt clipboard OSC.
- [ ] Rectangular selection (Mosh's `RECT` order from PR #12794) supported.
- [ ] Semantic-prompt-aware select-output (jump from prompt to prompt) works.
- [ ] `cargo nextest run --workspace` green; clippy -D warnings clean.

## Out of scope for this epic

- Search-in-buffer (different feature, file separately later).
- Vim-style motion commands inside copy-mode (post-v0.1 UX polish).
- Yank-buffer history (tmux's `paste-buffer` list).

## Watch / unblock signal

libghostty-rs adds a 'selection' module wrapping the PR #12794 C surface. Until then this epic stays deferred.
notes:
COPY-MODE DESIGN DECISION (ADR-0030 reconciliation, 2026-06-07)

DEPENDENCY BLOCKER RESOLVED. The epic's "watch/unblock signal" (libghostty-rs
wraps the PR #12794 selection C surface) is MET. The pinned fork
phall1/libghostty-rs@6d49dfd ALREADY exposes a safe Rust `selection` module:
Selection::new(start,end,rectangle), adjust(Adjustment), contains/equals/order/
to_ordered, and on Terminal: select_word/select_line/select_all/select_output/
select_word_between/set_selection, format_selection_buf/format_selection_alloc,
SelectLineOptions::with_semantic_prompt_boundary. No pin bump, no C-surface
wrapping needed. (Closes the libghostty side of phux-3sy/phux-97w too.)

CURRENT STATE ON MAIN (measured by code-read):
- Client overlay render/overlay/copy_mode.rs computes a visual CellRange
  selection (char/line/rect), and on arrow/Enter emits
  OverlayCommand::SendSelection(SelectionEvent).
- input_dispatch.rs:187 sends that as an INPUT_SELECTION wire frame to the
  server; the server stores per-client/per-Terminal selection state
  (state/registry.rs::set_selection).
- THERE IS NO COPY. "Enter to copy" is a no-op end-to-end: no
  SELECTION_FORMAT_REQUEST is sent, no extraction runs, nothing reaches a
  clipboard. The server's extract.rs (format_selection_alloc) exists but is
  wired only to scrollback search, not to copy-mode.

ARCH CONFLICT: the INPUT_SELECTION frame + SelectionEvent/SelectionMode wire
types + server-side selection storage are a PRE-ADR-0030 design. ADR-0030
(decision 1-2) makes selection a CLIENT-SIDE PROJECTION: both ends run
libghostty (ADR-0013), so the client selects on its OWN engine copy, extracts
locally, and copies to the LOCAL clipboard — NO wire state. The current
server-stored/shared selection is exactly the "structured view on the wire"
ADR-0030 rejects.

DECISION:
1. copy-mode is CLIENT-LOCAL. On commit (Enter), the client maps its overlay
   CellRange -> libghostty GridRefs on the focused pane's own slot.terminal
   (Point::Viewport grid coords; the overlay already moves in grid columns, so
   libghostty owns wide-cell semantics — no char-offset remap needed),
   builds a Selection (rectangle flag from mode), format_selection_buf -> text,
   and writes it to the clipboard via OSC 52 to the host terminal. Purely
   local; no wire.
2. word/line/all/semantic-output adjust run on the client engine via the
   now-available select_* APIs.
3. Removing the INPUT_SELECTION wire frame + SelectionEvent/SelectionMode wire
   types + server-side selection state is WIRE-BREAKING + architectural ->
   PROTOCOL_VERSION bump + docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md + STOP FOR REVIEW. Not done
   unilaterally.

SUPERSEDED BEADS (pre-ADR-0030, now anti-goals): phux-dh4 (server-side
selection state), phux-bli phase-1 (INPUT_SELECTION wire frame). Reconcile/close.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED: client-local copy (Enter copies), wire-surface removal
(review-gated), engine-driven word/line/semantic select.
PROGRESS 2026-06-07 (ADR-0030 copy-mode client-local migration): phux-v6jw DONE (PR #82, merged) — copy-mode is now a client-side projection: Enter resolves the selection against the focused pane's own libghostty engine (format_selection_alloc) and copies via OSC 52 to the host clipboard; new attach::copy module + hand-rolled base64; copy actually works now (the old INPUT_SELECTION path sent a coordinate-free frame the server dropped). phux-q1ni DONE (PR #83, merged, wire-breaking, PROTOCOL_VERSION 0.5.0) — removed INPUT_SELECTION frame + Selection input-event + input/selection.rs + all server selection state; zero selection structure remains on the wire. REMAINING: phux-7143 (engine-driven word/line/all/semantic-prompt select on the client) — additive UX enhancement; needs the dispatcher to call select_word/line/all/output on slot.terminal and feed the resulting Selection endpoints back into the overlay's anchor/cursor (engine->overlay coordinate feedback). Rectangular selection already supported via the overlay's Rect mode + Selection::new rectangle flag. Success criteria largely met except the engine-driven select (7143) and copy-mode mode-cycling UI.
close_reason: Copy-mode/selection epic COMPLETE via PR #203 + ADR-0045: client-side copy-mode over the consumer's own libghostty engine (superseding the epic's original server-side-wire design per ADR-0030). Char/Line/Block selection modes (Tab-cycle), sound with_selection extraction (unblocked by the phall1/libghostty-rs fork fix), OSC-52 clipboard, no wire change. Follow-ups: phux-p9m5, phux-pzwd.

title: Predictive local echo (Mosh-class UX), client-side
description: Implement Mosh-style predictive local echo in phux-client: client maintains a prediction overlay against its diff mirror, dim-renders predicted cells, reconciles on server FRAME_ACK (SPEC §6). Transport-agnostic — Unix socket today, QUIC later. Mandated by ADR-0007.
design:
Module: crates/phux-client/src/predict/
  state.rs    — PredictionState { pending: VecDeque<Prediction>, mirror: Grid }
  overlay.rs  — render predictions over the diff mirror (dim attribute)
  reconcile.rs — on FRAME_ACK, walk pending predictions and drop confirmed ones; on mismatch, snap mirror to authoritative state

Algorithm (Mosh-style, on our cell diffs):
  1. User key event K arrives client-side.
  2. Send K upstream; locally apply guess(K) to a copy of the mirror.
  3. Render guess cells with PREDICTION attribute (dim).
  4. On FRAME_ACK from server (matched by frame_id), compare server cells
     in the affected range with our prediction.
       match → drop prediction, render normally
       mismatch → drop prediction, render authoritative
  5. On timeout (no ACK within N ms) → drop prediction.

PredictionPolicy enum: Always, Adaptive (RTT-based), Never. Configurable via TOML (phux-nz4).

Reference: Mosh SSP paper, section on prediction.
acceptance_criteria: Typing over a 200ms-RTT simulated link feels instant. Predictions render dim, reconcile within one FRAME_ACK. Snapshot test for the prediction overlay state machine. cargo nextest run -p phux-client passes; clippy -D warnings clean.
notes:
Spec refs:
  SPEC.md:150-161 — §6 FRAME_ACK (the reconciliation signal)
  ADR/0007-mosh-class-transport-and-satellites.md — load-bearing rationale

Verify:
  cargo nextest run -p phux-client predict::
  cargo clippy -p phux-client -- -D warnings
  Manual: `tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 200ms` then type rapidly

Off by default behind PredictiveConfig::enabled; new run_with_predict entry point. ~970 LOC including tests; 26 new tests. Follow-ups: phux-9gw.1.1 (widen safe set), phux-9gw.1.2 (TOML config knob).

title: Client + TUI rendering composition
description:

title: Multiplexer core: Session/Window/Pane domain + IPC
description:
phux-core domain types with SlotMap-based stable IDs (SessionId, WindowId, PaneId), a layout tree, attach/detach lifecycle. phux-server runtime exposes them over the wire format from phux-6yl via Unix domain socket. tokio current-thread runtime throughout.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Two `phux attach <session>` invocations against the same server see the same pane and have their keystrokes merged in arrival order.
- [ ] Detach (Ctrl-b d equivalent) preserves session; reattach within 30s shows current state via initial snapshot then diff stream.
- [ ] Layout ops (split-horizontal, split-vertical, kill-pane, focus-direction) work via IPC and update all attached clients.
- [ ] Server survives client disconnect mid-frame (no crash, no leaked FDs).
- [ ] `cargo nextest run -p phux-core -p phux-server` green; integration test spins up a server, attaches a synthetic client, asserts message exchange.
close_reason: EPIC complete: all 9 children closed (byc.1-9). Multiplexer core shipped — SessionId/WindowId/PaneId registries, layout tree, current-thread runtime + UDS listener, ATTACH/DETACH lifecycle + multi-client keystroke merge, ERROR frame, and all 5 wire-level integration tests (byc.6.*). Audited + byc.6 completed 2026-05-29.

title: agent_prompt_wire::a_resting_level_never_satisfies_prompt_wait leaks unjoined tasks under load
description: Sighted 2026-08-17 by the merge sentinel during the cleanup-trio ci-full gate: nextest reported '1 leaky' — the test PASSED but leaked past the grace window. ATTRIBUTED AWAY FROM THAT BRANCH on four pieces of evidence: the file is untouched by all three branches in the batch; it spawns unjoined tokio::spawn tasks at crates/phux-client/src/agent_prompt_wire.rs (around lines 132 and 136); it did not leak in three prior gates; and it passes with no leak when run in isolation. So this is load-dependent TEST HYGIENE, not a product regression and not a member of the phux-5wxp timing-flake family — the assertion never fails, the task just outlives the test. FIX: join or abort the spawned tasks (a JoinHandle held to the end of the test, or a CancellationToken) so the test owns its own teardown. Low priority: a leak is reported, not a failure, so it cannot redden a gate today — but leaky counts are how a real teardown bug hides.
notes: CORROBORATION 2026-08-17: the very next ci-full gate (w4/seed-pane-spawned, 3915 tests) reported ZERO leaky — the agent_prompt_wire leak did not recur. That supports the load-dependence attribution: the unjoined tasks outlive the test only when the box is saturated, so this is test hygiene rather than a deterministic teardown bug. Still worth fixing, because a leaky count is exactly where a real teardown bug would hide, but it is not urgent and not a regression from any branch in that batch.

title: read_cell_graphemes does a full snapshot update and row scan per cell
description: Found 2026-08-17 (efficiency review); PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by this session's diff, but every call site was touched so it is worth recording. crates/phux-client/src/attach/render.rs read_cell_graphemes performs a full pool walk (RenderState::update) AND a linear row scan to the target row PER CELL. The predict reconcile loops (attach/input_dispatch/dispatch.rs ~:785 and attach/server_frame/handler.rs ~:428) call it once per cell, so one keystroke costs N snapshot updates and O(N*rows) row steps. FIX if it ever shows in a profile: a read_row_graphemes(row, cols) that starts ONE walk and selects each column from the same cell_iter. Filed rather than fixed because it is a real change to a hot path and wants a profile behind it, not a guess. NOTE the RenderPool cleanup (2026-08-17) did NOT make this worse — the generation compare is a register-width branch.

title: Extract the repeated protocol-violation close preamble in runtime/client.rs
description: Found 2026-08-17 (reuse review). crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs repeats a 3-line preamble before every protocol-violation close: abort_output_pumps(..) then detach_and_release_consumer_state(..) then close_for_protocol_error(..) then return. Pre-existing at ~:1394, :1440, :1620, :2022; the phux-2o3r framing fix added a fifth verbatim instance (plus ~:1334 for cancellation). The SPEC section 9 ordering (abort pumps, release consumer state, ERROR, DETACHED, close) is re-typed at each site and getting it wrong is invisible in review. FIX: one close_protocol_violation(..) that owns the order once. Pre-existing debt, but this session's diff grew it, which is why it is filed now rather than left. Note a related decision already made and NOT to be revisited: close_for_protocol_error deliberately does NOT take a FrameKind — it uses the same string for the ERROR and the DETACHED message, so a frame parameter would force a destructure-with-unreachable-arm and churn ten call sites (weighed and declined during the cleanup pass).

title: ws_attach.rs carries the same leased-not-reserved free_port() copy
description: Found 2026-08-17 while fixing phux-vbnr. crates/phux-server/tests/ws_attach.rs:38 has an identical free_port() helper that binds 127.0.0.1:0, reads the number, and drops the listener — the same lease-not-reservation defect that let one satellite answer under two names in hub_relay_federation. This copy binds the port live afterward, so a collision fails LOUDLY rather than producing a wrong-but-plausible aggregate — lower severity, same class. Fix it the same way phux-vbnr was fixed, and check for further copies (grep free_port across crates/*/tests). See the epic phux-5wxp for the taxonomy shape.

title: Narrow ServerState::metadata_broadcast's visibility or signature
description: Found 2026-08-17 (altitude review of phux-q7ks). metadata_broadcast (crates/phux-server/src/state/metadata.rs:302) is pub with the same visibility as metadata_set/metadata_delete, but its correctness contract lives entirely in a doc comment ('the caller is responsible for broadcasting only when the underlying mutation actually happened'). A future caller can therefore emit a METADATA_CHANGED for an ordinary key whose value GET_METADATA then contradicts — a protocol lie the type system permits. FIX: narrow the signature to the intercepted-key set (a ServerInterceptedKey enum, two variants today), or drop it to pub(crate) if nothing outside the crate needs it. Low probability, but it is correctness-by-documentation on shared infrastructure. The two-method split itself is CORRECT and reviewed — do not undo it.

title: Amend ADR-0088: adoption-marker sweep now has a second trigger
description: Found 2026-08-17 (altitude review of phux-8514). ADR/0088-adopting-a-live-server-into-supervision.md:88 states exactly ONE sweep trigger: 'a marker whose unit has vanished is swept on sight.' The phux-8514 fix added a SECOND — status_report's adoption_complete sweeps the marker when the init system is already running the unit (a completed hand-over). The ADR was not amended and the new adr-index-sync gate does not catch semantic drift like this, only index rows. Amend ADR-0088 to state both triggers.

title: Split terminal_actor::run_loop::run (505 lines) and tick_emit (293)
description: Filed 2026-08-17 from the phux-jx39 measurement pass, replacing the stale server-side half of phux-jr84 (closed). The terminal actor was already decomposed across 16 files: mod.rs is now 942 lines / 13 methods (NOT the 2623 lines / 56 methods older beads describe), with construct 466, consumers 504, events 503, io 580, native 938, requests 861, run_loop 858, spawn 1578, sync 277, tick 158, osc133 327. title: Audit docs/spec/L3.md section 3.1 well-known-key bullets against the 0.3.0+ implementation
description: Follow-up from phux-q7ks (2026-08-16). The phux.session.name/v1 bullet in L3.md 3.1 still described the pre-0.3.0 shape (GroupId scope, plain UTF-8 name) when the shipped convention is Global scope with a current\0new payload — it had drifted and nobody noticed until a rename fix touched it. Sweep the remaining 3.1 well-known-key bullets against the implementation (scopes, payload shapes, retention semantics) and correct any other drift, with CHANGELOG entries where the text change is semantic.

title: Client attach path emits no ERROR frame on a framing violation (server-side half landed in phux-2o3r)
description: Follow-up from phux-2o3r (2026-08-16, branch w1/frame-too-large, commit 15f62ef3). SPEC proto.md section 5 says a PEER receiving an oversized/invalid frame length MUST send ERROR{FRAME_TOO_LARGE} and close. The server-side readers and hub links now comply. The client attach path still raises AttachError::Protocol without emitting the ERROR frame: its readers do not hold the write half at the decode seam, so emission there requires re-plumbing the decode sites to reach a writer (or reclassifying the requirement as server-only in the spec, which would need its own CHANGELOG entry). Decide: re-plumb or spec-carve. Low urgency — a server sending malformed frames is the rarer direction.

title: ensure_server's live-server fast path should sweep a stale adoption marker
description: Follow-up from phux-8514 (2026-08-16). The login-bootstrap path leaves the ADR-0088 adoption marker stale: launchd bootstraps the armed plist at login but nothing on that path clears the marker. phux-8514 made 'phux service status' heal it lazily (armed+running is reported as a completed hand-over and the marker is swept), but if status is never run the marker lingers. Fix: ensure_server's live-server fast path can also sweep the marker when it observes a live supervised server, so the stale state never outlives the first phux command. See status_report/armed_adoption_unit in crates/phux/src/commands/service.rs (added on branch w1/service-status, commit 96fa74da).

title: Flaky under load: phux-dial ws::tests::keepalive_reports_a_stalled_peer_instead_of_hanging
description:
Observed 2026-08-16 during a 'just ci-full' run on the phux-k0cw.10 branch. The test failed inside the full-workspace nextest pool; the run cancelled with 13 tests still running and 1530 not yet started, so the pool was at full width when it fired.

Re-run in isolation 5/5 times: PASS, ~0.39s each. Two separate full 'just ci' runs on the same tree also passed it (3830/3830), and a second 'just ci-full' immediately after was fully green. So this is load-dependent, not a defect in the code under test, and it belongs to this epic's taxonomy rather than to the WebSocket work itself.

Likely shape, matching the siblings here: the test asserts a keepalive DEADLINE is reported rather than hung, so it is timing-sensitive by construction. Under a saturated runner the stalled-peer detection window competes with 15 other test threads for wakeups, and a deadline chosen against an idle machine is not a deadline on a busy one.

Provenance: the test is new — it arrived with 'fix(transport): give the WebSocket lane liveness and make reconnect transport-aware' (#469, d46db0ad), merged shortly before this run. That makes it the newest member of the family and the one with the least soak behind it.
acceptance_criteria: The test either uses a load-tolerant deadline (or a virtual clock) or is quarantined out of the parallel pool, and survives repeated full 'just ci-full' runs on a loaded machine.
notes: Not fixed on the phux-k0cw.10 branch on purpose: that branch touches the client sidebar sweep and has nothing to do with the WebSocket keepalive lane, and folding an unrelated timing fix into it would make both harder to review and to revert.
close_reason: dial keepalive window is timed from the policy's own origin instead of from before the dial

title: Flaky: spatial_e2e::spatial_cli_persists_topology_and_preserves_attached_focus
description:
Sighted 2026-08-15 by the army/w3-test-health agent during a clean 'just e2e' lane on a branch that touches nothing in spatial: FLAKY 2/3, i.e. it failed once and passed on the lane's own retry. A second 'just e2e' on the same branch was 59/59 clean.

Machine was under fleet load (about nine concurrent agent builds; load average 100-170 across the session), which is the family's signature.

Panic was inside spatial_e2e.rs:277 reached from spatial_cli_persists_topology_and_preserves_attached_focus (spatial_e2e.rs:359) -- a helper, so several call sites funnel through it. Diagnose the shape before fixing; see phux-5wxp for the taxonomy and do not re-derive it.

Note the lane hides this: 'just e2e' runs with --retries=2, so this surfaces as a FLAKY line rather than a failure and does not fail the gate. That is fine for the gate and bad for visibility -- the sighting was only caught because the agent was reading the lane output rather than its exit code.

title: RenderPool rebuilds on geometry change but not on Terminal replacement (client replica generations)
description:
Found during phux-wbak. phux_protocol::render_pool::RenderPool keys its rebuild on the terminal's (cols, rows). That closes phux-5pyx, but it does NOT cover the client's other lifecycle: phux-client-core publishes a NEW replica Terminal per generation (session.rs staging/publish), while the pooled RenderPool in phux-client's PaneSlot.renderer (and phux-client-ffi's RenderCache, keyed by TerminalId) survives the swap. A generation swap at the SAME geometry therefore reuses a RenderState whose cache came from a different Terminal.

Believed safe today only because a republish is followed by paint_full_frame, which passes force_full=true and makes render_at_inner repaint every row from the fresh snapshot regardless of dirty state. That is an unstated coupling between two modules: nothing fails if a future paint path republishes without force_full.

Options: give RenderPool a caller-supplied generation/identity token alongside last_dims, or assert the coupling with a test that a republish without force_full still serves fresh rows.
notes: GROOMED 2026-08-16 (autonomous run): do BOTH options — give RenderPool a caller-supplied generation/identity token alongside last_dims (rebuild when it changes), AND add the regression test that a republish without force_full still serves fresh rows. The token removes the unstated coupling; the test pins it.
close_reason: pooled RenderState is rebuilt when the replica generation changes, not only on resize

title: Adopt RenderPool in phux-record, phux-client-ffi, and phux-server-testkit (3 remaining trio copies)
description:
ADR-0086 put the pooled libghostty RenderState+RowIterator+CellIterator trio (and the phux-5pyx rebuild-on-geometry-change) in phux_protocol::render_pool::RenderPool, and adopted it in phux-server's SnapshotSynthesizer and phux-client's TerminalRenderer.

Three private copies remain, all found during phux-wbak and all MISSING from that bead's audit:
- crates/phux-record/src/replay.rs (Replayer) — also owns the Terminal; has a public resize() that does NOT rebuild the pool.
- crates/phux-client-ffi/src/client.rs (RenderCache) — pooled per TerminalId across replica generations.
- crates/phux-server-testkit/src/screen.rs (Screen) — owns the Terminal; never resizes, so latent only.

Blocked on a feature-graph decision, not on effort: all three depend on phux-protocol WITHOUT the server feature, and enabling it pulls png + the full libghostty type surface into crates whose Cargo.toml comments deliberately exclude them. Options: (a) a narrower phux-protocol feature that gates render_pool on dep:libghostty-vt only, (b) upstream RenderPool into the phall1/libghostty-rs fork (ADR-0086's declined first choice), (c) leave them.
notes:
GROOMED 2026-08-16 (autonomous run): decision is option (a) — add a narrower phux-protocol feature (e.g. 'render-pool') that gates render_pool on dep:libghostty-vt only, without png or the full server feature surface. Then adopt RenderPool in the three remaining copies. Option (b) upstreaming to the fork stays declined per ADR-0086; option (c) rejected because phux-994s shows the copies drift on lifecycle handling.
SECOND REASON 2026-08-17 (from phux-994s): phux-client-ffi's RenderCache is pooled per TerminalId ACROSS replica generations, so it carries the same latent generation hazard phux-994s just fixed for phux-client — not merely the resize hazard this bead originally described. It was deliberately left untouched on w2/renderpool-generation because adopting RenderPool there requires exactly the feature-graph decision this bead tracks (option (a), the narrow render-pool feature gating on dep:libghostty-vt only, remains the groomed answer). This raises the bead's value: it is now a correctness follow-up, not only a dedupe.
BEAD REWRITE NEEDED 2026-08-17 (altitude review, verified against the tree): phux-client-ffi is NOT 'one of three copies missing the new fix'. RenderCache (crates/phux-client-ffi/src/client.rs:51-67) holds a raw RenderState/RowIterator/CellIterator trio and HAS NO last_dims FIELD AT ALL — it never adopted RenderPool, so it carries BOTH hazards: phux-5pyx (rebuild on resize) AND phux-994s (rebuild on republish). The cache is evicted only on Tombstone and TerminalClosed (lib.rs:855, :867), NOT on a bootstrap republish. TWO FACTS THAT MAKE THIS CHEAPER AND MORE URGENT THAN FILED: (1) the fix's own input is already in scope — client.rs:631 reads 'let key = self.terminal_key(terminal_id)?' (a ReplicaKey) NINETEEN LINES above the cache.state.update(terminal) call, so migrating is RenderPool::begin(terminal, key.generation_token()) plus the feature-graph decision. (2) 'phux-u8zm' appears NOWHERE in the tree — zero hits in .rs and .md, while phux-994s has thirteen — so the FFI file carries no marker and ADR-0086 asserts the trio 'now lives in one type', which is NOT TRUE of the shipped tree. A deferral with a bead nobody can find from the code is how this rots.

title: Emit ERROR{FRAME_TOO_LARGE} on a SPEC 5 framing violation (no transport does today)
description:
Audit evidence (phux-nwpw, 2026-08-15): docs/spec/proto.md section 5 says a peer receiving a frame with length outside 1..=16777216 MUST send ERROR { code: FRAME_TOO_LARGE } and close the transport. ErrorCode::FrameTooLarge exists in phux-protocol (wire value 4) but is emitted by NOTHING in the workspace - grep finds it only in the enum, its as_wire mapping, and roundtrip tests.

Every reader instead closes silently: the UDS/QUIC/WebTransport/WebSocket readers surface io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, which runtime/client.rs turns into a debug-level 'client read error; closing' with no ERROR frame; the client attach path raises AttachError::Protocol; hub/link.rs returns a String. So the close half of the requirement is met and the ERROR half is not, uniformly, on every transport.

phux-nwpw unified the detection into phux_protocol::wire::framing (FramingError), so the emit side now has a single typed signal to hang off - the follow-up is plumbing FramingError to a close_for_protocol_error(ErrorCode::FrameTooLarge) on each reader rather than re-deriving the condition.

Note this IS an observable behaviour change (new bytes on the wire in a case that currently emits none) and needs its own spec CHANGELOG draft entry, though not a PROTOCOL_VERSION bump: it adds an error frame in a path that previously sent nothing before closing, and ADR-0061 treats additive error emission as compatible.
close_reason: server now emits ERROR{FRAME_TOO_LARGE} then DETACHED{PROTOCOL_ERROR} before closing on a framing violation, across all transports

title: Flaky: failure_ux_e2e::last_pane_death_surfaces_its_exit_status
description:
Sighted by the wave-two integrator: failed 3/3 tries once, then passed on re-run and stayed green across the remaining lanes. Nothing in the branch under test at the time (phux-m64c, test-only, confined to crates/phux-server/tests/agent_detect.rs) could reach it.

Same load-dependent family as the rest -- see parent epic phux-5wxp for the five-shape taxonomy and the rules. Do not re-derive them, and do not lengthen a timeout.

SHAPE HYPOTHESIS, to confirm rather than assume: the name says it asserts the LAST pane's death surfaces its exit status. That is a race between a pane exiting, the session being reaped, the server self-exiting, and the client still being connected to observe the report -- which is close to taxonomy shape 2 (the pane dying before the collection window closes, surfacing as a confusing early-eof rather than anything about the feature). If the client's connection drops before the exit status is delivered, the test would fail for a reason that says nothing about exit-status reporting.

Note this one is ADJACENT TO A REAL CONTRACT rather than pure scaffolding: last-pane death drives session reap and server self-exit (ADR-0063 and the last-pane self-exit path), and surfacing the exit status is what tells a user why their terminal vanished. If the flake turns out to be a genuine ordering bug -- the server self-exiting before the status reaches the client -- that is a user-visible defect worth far more than P3. Establish which before treating it as test hygiene.

Run the tailscale probe first (PHUX_TAILSCALE=/nonexistent/tailscale) per the epic; one member of this family has already turned out to be that, and one has turned out NOT to be, so it is cheap information either way.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-15 on army/w3-test-health. THE CONTRACT QUESTION THIS BEAD RAISES IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS: NOT A DEFECT. P3 is correct. Detail below, because the bead is right that it was worth establishing rather than assuming.

THE SERVER ORDERING IS SOUND. Traced end to end in `runtime/client.rs`:
  * `spawn_terminal_exit_watcher` gathers the subscriber mailboxes, interns the wire id and reaps the pane in ONE critical section (phux-emdv), then AWAITS `broadcast_terminal_closed`, which pushes `TERMINAL_CLOSED { exit_status }` into each client's bounded `Outbound` mpsc. Only AFTER that await does it evaluate `server_empty && served && !root_token.is_cancelled()` and fire `root_token.cancel()`. The exit status is in the mailbox before self-exit is even signalled.
  * The cancellation is then drained, not slammed. `accept_loop`'s cancel arm joins every client task within `CLIENT_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` (2s). Each `handle_client` cancel arm appends `DETACHED { ServerShutdown }` behind the already-queued frame and calls `close_client_writer`, which signals the writer to close, drops the sender, and lets the writer "drain every frame already ordered before this command" before `FrameWriter::close`.
  * So TERMINAL_CLOSED is ordered ahead of DETACHED in one FIFO, and the close is ordered behind both. There is no window in which the server self-exits past an undelivered exit status. Nothing to fix in the product.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT WAS THE TEST'S BARRIER, and it was a textbook shape 3 -- "the event fires before the observer is registered", with a barrier that only looked like one. `AttachedClient::wait_until_painting` waited for ONE painted byte and then slept 500ms. The painted byte proves nothing: `phux attach` emits terminal setup before it dials the socket. So the entire barrier was the 500ms, and when it lost, `send-keys "exit 7"` killed the last pane while this client was still mid-ATTACH -- it was never in the fanout set, never learned the exit status, and failed on `wait_exit`/`wait_for_output` for a reason that says nothing about exit-status reporting.

MEASURED, rather than argued. Instrumented the interval from the client's first painted byte to the server reporting `attached_clients > 0`, across 14 runs:
  load ~50-100:  114, 117, 121, 123, 130, 157, 161, 310 ms
  load ~144:     238, 267, 299, 352, 359, 511 ms
511ms EXCEEDS THE 500ms SETTLE. The old bet is not marginal on a loaded box; it loses outright, and the margin shrinks without bound in the load.

THE FIX: replace the sleep with a barrier on the server's side of the wire. `wait_until_attached` polls `phux ls --json` until the session reports `attached_clients >= 1`. That counter only moves once the server has PROCESSED this connection's ATTACH, and `ls` is a command that carries a reply -- its exit is proof of delivery, not merely of sending, which is the distinction the epic is built around. Shape 4 does not apply: nothing here measures an idle lifetime and the harness server's `--exit-after-idle` is ten minutes.
Renamed to `wait_until_attached` so the name states the property. The two scenarios that inject keystrokes into the CLIENT's own PTY (rather than through the server) additionally call `settle_for_local_keystrokes` -- the same 500ms, kept explicit and named, because a client-local stdin-reader install crosses no wire and therefore has no observable barrier. Scenarios driven through `phux send-keys` do not call it and must not.

REPETITION: 20 consecutive serial runs under 24 synthetic CPU burners (load 66 -> 158): 20/20. Plus 6 runs under load 144 during the measurement above, and two full `just e2e` lanes: green.

TAILSCALE PROBE: not the cause. `ServerGuard::start` blocks on the socket file, so `overlay::detect()` is paid before the client exists.
close_reason: Fixed on army/w3-test-health. NOT a product defect: the server queues TERMINAL_CLOSED into every subscriber's mailbox BEFORE firing root_token.cancel(), and both accept_loop and handle_client drain already-ordered frames before closing, so the exit status can never be lost to self-exit. P3 was right. The defect was the test's barrier -- one painted byte plus a 500ms sleep, where the painted byte precedes the dial. Measured first-byte-to-attached at 511ms under load 144, i.e. the old bet loses outright. Replaced with a server-side barrier on phux ls --json attached_clients. 20/20 serial repetitions under load 66-158.

title: Flaky: workspace_archive_e2e::native_agent_session_is_replayed_after_pane_restart_and_rejects_stale_ownership
description:
Sighted by the wave-two integrator. IMPORTANT: it initially looked like a HARD REGRESSION and was not one -- the story is worth more than the bead.

The integrator's baseline run failed this 3/3 tries, twice, INCLUDING IN ISOLATION. It bisected: green at d32d71fe and deb73ca1, red at a77daec4 ('feat: ship agent discovery suite'). That is a textbook regression signature. It then passed 59/59 in every one of six subsequent full e2e lanes.

The bisect was fooled by AMBIENT LOAD: five worker agents were cold-building in parallel during it. The failure signature -- 'wait timed out after 34 polls', exit 124, against a 5s budget -- is CPU starvation, the same root cause phux-m64c diagnosed for agent_detect (shape 5 on the parent epic: one deadline paying for both the subject and an ambient precondition).

TWO LESSONS, both worth more than the fix:
1. A BISECT RUN UNDER FLEET LOAD IS UNTRUSTWORTHY. It will happily hand you a culprit commit that is innocent. Quiesce the machine before bisecting a timing-sensitive e2e test, or bisect with the m64c counterfactual technique instead of raw pass/fail.
2. 3/3 failures in isolation is NOT proof of determinism when other processes are saturating the box. 'In isolation' means no other tests in THIS run, not no other load on the machine.

FIX SHAPE: the same paint barrier m64c gave agent_detect. Make the pane signal it has painted using a shell BUILTIN (': > path' -- forks nothing, leaves the process group leader and agent identification untouched), start the deadline from there, and leave the deadline value unchanged so it measures only the subject. Prove it with m64c's counterfactual: prepend 'sleep 9' to the seed to make the starvation deterministic, confirm the test fails pre-fix and passes post-fix, then 20+ repetitions under full parallel load.

See parent epic phux-5wxp for the five-shape taxonomy; do not re-derive it.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-15 on army/w3-test-health. The diagnosis in this bead is right; the PRESCRIBED FIX IS NOT APPLICABLE, and the substitute is a better fit for the same taxonomy entry.

WHY THE PRESCRIBED FIX DOES NOT APPLY: the bead says to add "the same paint barrier m64c gave agent_detect" -- make the pane signal it has painted with a shell builtin, start the deadline from there. But this test's stimulus IS `phux wait --until <text>`, which is already a poll for a paint. There is no separate subject deadline hiding behind the paint to protect. Adding a builtin-written marker file would just be a second, parallel way of waiting for the same event.

WHAT REPLACES IT (same principle, adapted): SPLIT the one deadline into the two things it was paying for.
  1. `wait --until "FAKE_AGENT_ARGS=" --timeout 60` -- the AMBIENT precondition: did the machine run the plugin's shell script at all. Generous, with a message that names the environment.
  2. `wait --until "FAKE_AGENT_ARGS=--resume <id>" --timeout 5` -- the SUBJECT: is the replayed argv exactly right. The value is UNCHANGED, exactly as the taxonomy asks, and it is now honest: the fake agent writes all its lines in one burst, so once the first has landed the rest are already there. A timeout at stage 2 means the restored argv is genuinely wrong, which is the only thing this test exists to catch.
Applied at all three `--timeout 5` sites in the file, plus `wait_for_terminal_absent` (which forks a whole `phux` per poll, so its 5s was mostly buying process startup too).

COUNTERFACTUAL, and it reproduced the bead's failure signature CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER. Prepend `sleep 9` to `scripts/fake-agent.sh`:
  * pre-fix 5s budget: FAIL at 10.32s with `phux: wait timed out after 34 polls` -- the exact string the wave-two integrator recorded, including the poll count.
  * post-fix split: PASS at 20.65s.
That is as close to proof as this gets: the reported failure was this, not a regression in `feat: ship agent discovery suite`.

THE BEAD'S TWO LESSONS ARE CONFIRMED AND WORTH KEEPING. A bisect under fleet load hands you an innocent culprit; "3/3 in isolation" is not determinism when the box is saturated. Adding a third: the counterfactual is not just a proof technique, it is a DIAGNOSTIC one -- reproducing the literal failure string is what distinguishes "I fixed a flake of this shape" from "I fixed THE flake that was reported".

REPETITION: 20 consecutive serial runs under 24 synthetic CPU burners (load 66 -> 158): 20/20 pass. Plus two full `just e2e` lanes (59 tests each): green.

TAILSCALE PROBE: not the cause. Both servers in this test are explicitly spawned and the test blocks on the socket file appearing before doing anything, so any `overlay::detect()` cost is paid before the measured window opens.
close_reason: Fixed on army/w3-test-health by splitting the one 5s deadline into an ambient budget (did the plugin's shell run at all, 60s, message names the environment) and the unchanged 5s subject budget (is the replayed argv exact). The bead's prescribed paint barrier did not apply -- 'phux wait --until' IS the paint barrier. Counterfactual with sleep 9 reproduced the integrator's exact failure string including 'after 34 polls'. 20/20 serial repetitions under load 66-158; two clean just e2e lanes.

title: Move overlay detection off the pane-startup window
description:
Recommended by the phux-c6g6 agent after fixing the eager-evaluation half; deliberately not implemented there, since it is a different change with a different risk profile.

crates/phux-server/src/runtime/mod.rs pre-seeds the pane, THEN resolves the WS and QUIC listen addresses, THEN starts accepting. Any cost in that middle step therefore lands between 'the session exists' and 'the server is reachable' -- a window where a pane is live and nothing is listening. That is precisely the startup-order shape that produced the agent_events flake family: the pane's clock had started while the accept loop had not.

phux-c6g6 removed the acute instance (overlay detection no longer runs when the gates are closed, and runs at most once when they are open -- 203.5ms to 42ns closed-gate). But the ORDER is unchanged, so the window still exists for anything else that ever lands there, and for the open-gate case where detection legitimately runs.

OPTIONS THE AGENT NAMED:
1. Do the overlay lookup BEFORE the pre-seed. A slow or wedged tailscale then delays pane creation rather than creating a live-pane/no-listener gap. Simplest.
2. Run it in parallel with the pre-seed via tokio::join!, moving the blocking shell-out to spawn_blocking. Keeps the latency off the critical path entirely, at the cost of a little more startup concurrency to reason about.
3. Cache the overlay address across restarts -- it rarely changes -- so warm starts skip the shell-out altogether. Largest change, biggest win on the open-gate path, and needs a staleness answer.

Labelled post-1.0 because the acute defect is fixed and this is a robustness improvement, not a correctness one. Promote it if another flake in the phux-5wxp family turns out to be this window again.

ACCEPTANCE: either the ordering is changed with a test pinning that the accept loop is ready before or with the pane rather than after it, or a written statement of why the current order is correct.

title: Flaky: terminal_actor::tests::pane_kill_lets_foreground_process_flush_before_death
description:
Sighted by the phux-c6g6 agent during a full 'just ci' run; passed in isolation immediately afterwards. Branch touched only crates/phux-server/src/runtime/mod.rs's overlay gating, nothing near the terminal actor, so it is not that change's doing.

See the parent epic phux-5wxp for the full four-shape taxonomy and the rules -- do not re-derive them here.

SHAPE HYPOTHESIS, to be confirmed rather than assumed: the name says the test asserts a foreground process gets to FLUSH before the pane dies. That is a race between a kill and an I/O drain, which smells like taxonomy shape 2 (the pane dying before the collection window closes) or a genuine ordering bug in the flush-before-kill path. If it is the latter it is a REAL DEFECT rather than a test problem -- a pane kill that truncates a foreground process's final output would lose the last thing a user saw, and that would be worth far more than a P3. Establish which before treating it as test hygiene.

Run the tailscale probe first (PHUX_TAILSCALE=/nonexistent/tailscale) per the epic -- one member of this family has already turned out to be that.

Note this test lives in a #[cfg(test)] module inside crates/phux-server/src/terminal_actor/, not in tests/, so it runs in the lib-test pool alongside everything else.
notes:
PARTIALLY FIXED 2026-08-15 on army/w3-test-health, and the honest answer to this bead's own question is: NEITHER of the two options it offers.

THE BEAD'S HYPOTHESIS IS WRONG ON BOTH BRANCHES. It asks whether this is shape 2 (pane dying before the collection window closes) or "a genuine ordering bug in the flush-before-kill path", and says to establish which. It is neither. The flush-before-kill path is correct: `shutdown_pty` snapshots the foreground group BEFORE signalling, SIGHUPs the foreground group first and the shell group second, keeps the PTY master open for the whole window so the child can still write, POLLS both groups for exit rather than sleeping, and only SIGKILLs survivors afterwards. There is no ordering bug to find.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS: shape 5 twice over, plus an irreducible remainder that no test-side change can reach.

`.config/nextest.toml` ALREADY CONTAINS THE ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS for this exact test, and it is worth reading before touching it -- it records that `test-group`/`pty-serial` was measured and found insufficient (2 failures in 3 full-suite runs), that `threads-required = 'num-cpus'` is the knob that worked, and that the real assertion is "the process got scheduled inside PANE_KILL_GRACE, a deliberate 500ms PRODUCT budget, not a test constant". A future agent re-deriving that from scratch is wasted work.

FIXED HERE (the part that was still test-side):
The pre-hangup setup had TWO ambient deadlines, both paying for `/bin/sh` fork+exec+schedule -- a 2s poll for a distinct process group, then a 5s wait for the `armed` file. The 2s one bought nothing: `armed` is written by the inner shell AFTER `trap`, and the inner shell IS the process the outer shell's `set -m` put in its own group at exec, so the armed file strictly dominates the group check and implies it in the only order it can happen. Removed it; the group is now read ONCE after the barrier and asserted. The `armed` wait keeps its role as the single barrier but gets a budget sized for what it actually covers (30s) and a message that names the environment instead of blaming the flush path.

COUNTERFACTUAL: prepend `sleep 9` to the fixture script to make the starvation deterministic.
  * pre-fix 5s ambient budget: FAIL at 5.18s.
  * post-fix 30s ambient budget: PASS at 9.19s.

WHAT CANNOT BE FIXED FROM INSIDE THE TEST, and is now written into the test's doc comment so nobody re-opens it: the final assertion requires the trap handler to run within PANE_KILL_GRACE = 500ms. That window belongs to the product. Lengthening it changes shipped behavior to suit a test; no barrier can fence a window the product itself defines. `threads-required = 'num-cpus'` clears the nextest pool but cannot clear nine concurrent agent builds on the same box. A failure here on a loaded machine is a statement about the machine, not the code -- and that is now what the failure message says.

REPETITION: 20 consecutive serial runs under 24 synthetic CPU burners (load 66 -> 158): 20/20 pass. 4 full-parallel workspace runs (3773 tests), one at load 171: green.

TAILSCALE PROBE: not applicable -- this is a lib test with no server startup in it at all. `overlay::detect()` is called from `runtime/mod.rs`, which this test never reaches.
close_reason: Test-side seams fixed on army/w3-test-health; the residual is inherent and now documented in the test rather than tracked as a bug. The bead's two hypotheses were both wrong: it is not shape 2, and the flush-before-kill path has no ordering bug (shutdown_pty snapshots the foreground group before signalling, keeps the master open, and polls for exit before any SIGKILL). Removed a redundant 2s process-group deadline the armed barrier already dominates, and sized the armed barrier for the ambient cost it covers. Counterfactual with sleep 9: pre-fix FAIL at 5.18s, post-fix PASS at 9.19s. What remains is that the assertion needs a shell scheduled inside PANE_KILL_GRACE, a 500ms PRODUCT budget -- unfixable from the test, already mitigated by threads-required = num-cpus in nextest.toml. 20/20 serial repetitions under load 66-158.

title: Flaky: phux_3uv_acked_incremental::acked_incremental_converges_and_seq_is_monotonic
description:
Two independent sightings today, both under full parallel load, both passing in isolation immediately afterwards:

1. The phux-a5xj agent, during its own full-suite run.
2. The phux-yb1m agent, during a 'just ci' run -- notably as a live instance of the very flake class that bead is about, since the failure aborted 'just ci' before it reached the doc/deny gates.

Load-dependent, not branch-specific: neither branch touches the acked-incremental path.

BEFORE TREATING THIS AS AN ORDINARY SCHEDULING FLAKE, check the environmental hypothesis. The agent_events cluster looked like a load flake for weeks and turned out to be phux_config::overlay::detect() shelling out to the tailscale CLI when it is on PATH, stalling server startup ~286ms before the accept loop runs and eating a seed's head start. CI has no tailscale, so it was green there and red on developer machines. Filed as phux-c6g6 and being fixed. Probe with PHUX_TAILSCALE=/nonexistent/tailscale -- that is exactly how the agent_events root cause was proven.

This repo's flake taxonomy has four shapes: (1) the pane dies too early; (2) the pane dies before the collection window closes -- a short seed sleep racing a 15s WIRE_RECV_TIMEOUT, surfacing as a confusing 'early eof'; (3) the event fires before the observer is registered, where a barrier anchored on the client having SENT a frame is INSUFFICIENT if that frame gets no reply -- use a following command whose CommandResult you wait for, per crates/phux-server/tests/agent_asked.rs; (4) the probe perturbs what it measures.

A monotonic-sequence convergence assertion smells like (2) or (4) rather than (3), but diagnose it rather than pattern-matching -- two tests in one file have had different shapes before.

DO NOT lengthen a timeout. ACCEPTANCE: the shape named, a barrier or environment-independence fix, and 20+ repetitions under full parallel load as proof. Sibling: phux-m64c (agent_detect flake, same family).
notes:
THIRD independent sighting, by the phux-w7z2.57 agent during a full --all-features workspace run; passed in isolation and on the clean re-run. Its branch touches runtime/client.rs metadata refusal, agent/wait.rs and the TUI driver -- nothing near the acked-incremental path. The agent's own read was 'PTY snapshot timing'.

Three sightings, three unrelated branches, three different agents. This is the most reproducible member of the phux-5wxp family and should be taken first.
FIXED 2026-08-15 on army/w3-test-health. Shape 1, and the diagnosis is cheap once you look at WHICH assertion fires.

THE DEFECT: the seed was `sh -c 'sleep 0.5; printf MARKER; sleep 30'`. That half-second is a bet that attach + bootstrap finish first, so the marker lands as a live delta rather than inside the snapshot. When the bet loses, the marker IS in the bootstrap chunk and the failure is `assert_eq!(count_occurrences(&payload, MARKER), 0)` at what is now line 118 -- an assertion about the snapshot, which says nothing whatsoever about the acked-incremental loop or about monotonic seq. That is why three different agents read it three different ways ("PTY snapshot timing" was the closest).

THE FIX: a barrier, not a longer sleep. The seed now blocks on a file the TEST creates, and creates only after it has drained BOOTSTRAP_READY: `until [ -e "$PHUX_TEST_GO" ]; do sleep 0.05; done; printf MARKER; sleep 30`. The snapshot is provably on the wire before the file exists, so no scheduling delay can reorder them. The poll forks a `sleep` per iteration instead of spinning, so waiting does not make a starved machine worse.

COUNTERFACTUAL (m64c's technique, and it is decisive here). Inserting `tokio::time::sleep(9s)` immediately before the test's `wait_for_socket` makes the lost bet DETERMINISTIC:
  * pre-fix seed + 9s delay: FAIL in 9.17s, panicking at the bootstrap-carries-marker assertion -- exactly the observed shape.
  * post-fix barrier + 9s delay: PASS in 9.90s.
Same mutation, opposite verdicts. The barrier is real.

REPETITION: 20 consecutive serial runs (`--test-threads=1`) under 24 synthetic CPU burners, load average 66 -> 158: 20/20 pass. Plus 4 full-parallel `cargo nextest run --workspace` runs (3773 tests each), one at load 171 and one at load 121-168: green every time.

TAILSCALE PROBE, per the epic: RULED OUT. `tailscale` IS on PATH on this box (/Users/phall/go/bin/tailscale), so the hypothesis was live, and `PHUX_TAILSCALE=/nonexistent/tailscale` changes nothing -- passes either way. Consistent with phux-c6g6 having already gated and memoized `overlay::detect()`; the cost is paid before the socket binds, and this test's clock starts after `wait_for_socket`.

SIDE EFFECT: the test got faster. It no longer pays an unconditional 0.5s -- ~1.5s before, 0.94s after.
close_reason: Fixed on army/w3-test-health: seed's 0.5s timing bet replaced with a go-file barrier the test creates after draining BOOTSTRAP_READY. Counterfactual (9s attach delay): pre-fix FAIL at the bootstrap-carries-marker assertion, post-fix PASS. 20/20 serial repetitions under load 66-158, plus 4 full-parallel workspace runs. Tailscale ruled out with tailscale present on PATH.

title: Flaky: agent_detect::a_declared_kind_never_gains_a_state_derived_from_a_different_occupant
description:
Observed by the integrator during the phux-j1zj gate run. Failed once under --fail-fast and passed under --no-fail-fast on the SAME tree; j1zj touches no detector code, so it is not that branch's doing.

Load-dependent, same family as the agent_events cluster, but NOT fixed by the agent-events-env work (phux-c6g6 / commit cc9b058e) -- that fix replaced the timing bets in crates/phux-server/tests/agent_events.rs specifically, and this test is in the detector suite.

CONTEXT THAT MATTERS FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: the agent_events family turned out to have an environmental root cause, not a scheduling one. phux_config::overlay::detect() shells out to the tailscale CLI when it is on PATH, stalling server startup ~286ms before the accept loop runs and eating the head start a seed's sleep was betting on. That is filed as phux-c6g6 (which also records that PHUX_NO_AUTO_LISTEN does not actually prevent the shell-out, because detect() is evaluated eagerly as an argument before the gates discard it).

So before treating this as an ordinary scheduling flake, check whether it is the same startup stall in a different costume: does it fail only where tailscale is on PATH? Do not tune a timeout. This repo's flake taxonomy has three shapes -- the pane dying too early, the pane dying before the collection window closes, and the event firing before the observer is registered -- and a barrier anchored on the client having SENT a frame is insufficient when that frame gets no reply. crates/phux-server/tests/agent_asked.rs carries the reference idiom (a following command whose CommandResult proves in-order server-side processing).

ACCEPTANCE: the shape named, a barrier or environment-independence fix rather than a longer sleep, and 20+ repetitions under full parallel load as proof.
close_reason:
Fixed on branch army/m64c-detector-flake, test-only, +107/-2 in crates/phux-server/tests/agent_detect.rs.

NOT the tailscale cause -- ruled out with numbers, 20/20 pass with PHUX_TAILSCALE=/nonexistent and 20/20 without. NOT a wire-protocol race either. It is a new shape, now recorded as shape 5 on the parent epic phux-5wxp: one deadline paying for two unrelated things. The 8s DETECT_DEADLINE covered both the detector converging (the subject, bounded) and the seed pane's child process getting scheduled at all (ambient, unbounded). A trace caught the pane's FIRST byte arriving at T+7.77s -- the freshly spawned /bin/sh did not run for 7.8 seconds under load. The detector had already scanned the blank grid at T+0.81s and published the fail-safe idle, and a permission dialog paints once so wants_screen was false forever after.

Diagnostic tell worth remembering: failures came in BURSTS tracking ambient machine load and never appeared under synthetic CPU-only load. Clustering rather than scattering points at something the machine schedules.

FIX: the fake agent creates a paint marker with ': > path', a shell BUILTIN chosen so it forks nothing and leaves the process group leader and agent identification untouched; each case waits for that marker before it starts timing the detector. DETECT_DEADLINE is UNCHANGED at 8s and now measures only the subject. A pane that never paints fails against its own separate budget with a message naming the environment. All six cases in the file carried the same bet, so all six got the barrier. Note agent_detect already had threads-required = num-cpus, so more reservation was not available as a fix.

PROOF, and the technique is the best produced today: prepending 'sleep 9' to the fake agent makes the starved child deterministic, converting an unreproducible flake into a mutation test -- 8 of 9 cases fail on pre-fix main, 9 of 9 pass with the barrier. Plus 360/360 repetitions at 6-way parallelism and three full -p phux-server runs green.

Left alone deliberately: a_kind_change_never_leaves_a_stale_kind_beside_a_live_state has the same shape but is far less exposed, since codex is exec'd from an already-scheduled process rather than posix_spawn'ed cold.

title: A milestone-label gate that does not lie about tracker freshness
description:
phux-i7vu labelled every open bead rc-1.0 or post-1.0 and wrote down the criterion. The other half of its acceptance -- a gate that keeps it true -- is not shipped, because the obvious implementation would be wrong.

The tracker is a local Dolt DB; .beads/issues.jsonl is a PASSIVE EXPORT.
